a11y-interaction-trace.title: A11y Interaction Trace
a11y-interaction-trace.description: Record keyboard focus failures and export local traces for bug reports.
a11y-interaction-trace.why: Record keyboard actions and focus changes, then export one trace file for an accessibility bug report.
a11y-interaction-trace.detail: Browser extension that records explicitly started test sessions, captures keyboard/focus events, opt-in screenshots, and a narrowed accessibility snapshot, then exports a self-contained trace viewer. Non-goals: continuous surveillance, automated remediation, general analytics, or uploading sessions.
a11y-interaction-trace.user: A web developer or accessibility tester who needs a small reproducible record of keyboard focus, visible UI, and accessibility-tree changes for a broken interaction.
a11y-interaction-trace.distinct: It is a reproducibility handoff artifact, not another automated accessibility scanner.
a11y-interaction-trace.workaround: Record a screen video, paste screenshots into an issue, manually describe focus order, and hope the receiving developer can reproduce it.

a11y-playtest-captioner.title: A11y Playtest Captioner
a11y-playtest-captioner.description: Caption game states and test action order before playtests.
a11y-playtest-captioner.why: Author localized game-state captions and rehearse their keyboard order before browser-game playtests.
a11y-playtest-captioner.detail: An npm library plus local preview page: developers register named canvas/game states, write localized descriptions and focus order, then test them with keyboard navigation and browser speech synthesis. Non-goals: OCR, automatic accessibility claims, or replacing disabled playtesters.
a11y-playtest-captioner.user: Browser-game creators who need to author and hear concise, multilingual descriptions for important visual game states before inviting disabled playtesters.
a11y-playtest-captioner.distinct: It helps authors expose intentional game state, rather than attempting an unreliable AI screen reader for arbitrary games.
a11y-playtest-captioner.workaround: Add alt-like text ad hoc, test only with browser devtools, rely on a generic OCR overlay, or postpone accessibility until late playtesting.

abc-score-play.title: ABC Score Play
abc-score-play.description: Write, hear, loop, share, and print a short ABC score.
abc-score-play.why: Play score-based ABC practice with immediate feedback.
abc-score-play.detail: Static web editor for ABC input with error highlighting, rendered staff, MIDI playback, bar looping, tempo practice, printable card, and URL fragment sharing. Non-goals: AI composing, rights-managed sheet music, collaboration accounts.
abc-score-play.user: Musicians and educators who want to write a short, shareable score in plain text and immediately play, loop, and print it.
abc-score-play.distinct: It is a text-to-practice bridge, not an AI music generator or notation-suite clone.
abc-score-play.workaround: Use MuseScore for notation, hand-format ABC, or share screenshots and separate audio files.

accessible-page-capture.title: Accessible Page Capture
accessible-page-capture.description: Record a blocked web task as a private issue packet.
accessible-page-capture.why: Save a page view with the reading details that ordinary screenshots lose.
accessible-page-capture.detail: A browser extension that records an explicit 30-second interaction trace, page URL, focused element labels, and optional user note, then exports a redacted Markdown/JSON issue packet. Non-goals: continuous session recording, submitting issues automatically, accessibility certification, or uploading confidential page content.
accessible-page-capture.user: Low-vision workers and the colleagues supporting them who need to report one inaccessible web interaction with enough evidence for a product team to fix it.
accessible-page-capture.distinct: It converts a lived access barrier into a reproducible engineering artifact rather than adding another automated accessibility scanner.
accessible-page-capture.workaround: Send an imprecise support email, record a screen video, try to identify ARIA failures in devtools, or wait for an accessibility audit.

accessible-photo-catalog.title: Large Type Catalog
accessible-photo-catalog.description: Sort one local photo folder with large controls, keyboard shortcuts, and private browser storage.
accessible-photo-catalog.why: Sort and label local photos with large controls and a complete keyboard workflow. Photos stay on this device.
accessible-photo-catalog.detail: Local browser catalog for one folder: huge thumbnails, adjustable contrast and text, keyboard-only keep/reject/tag/rename queue, and CSV sidecar export. Non-goals: face recognition, cloud gallery, image editing, or replacing a DAM.
accessible-photo-catalog.user: A low-vision knowledge worker or older family member who needs to inspect and sort a local photo collection with reliably large controls and keyboard/voice-friendly operations.
accessible-photo-catalog.distinct: The differentiator is accessible classification workflow, not AI photo organization or a general gallery.
accessible-photo-catalog.workaround: Apple Photos/Google Photos, Explorer/Finder, small thumbnails, or a full DAM with many inaccessible controls.

accessible-table-ocr-check.title: Accessible Table OCR Check
accessible-table-ocr-check.description: Check scanned-table OCR reading order and export accessible files in your browser.
accessible-table-ocr-check.why: Check an OCR table's reading order, fix headers, and export HTML or CSV.
accessible-table-ocr-check.detail: A local PWA that accepts page images/OCR JSON, overlays detected blocks and reading order, lets a user relabel table cells and headers, and exports HTML/CSV plus an issue report. Non-goals: training an OCR model, hosting copyrighted books, full document editing, or automatic perfect reconstruction.
accessible-table-ocr-check.user: Readers, librarians, and accessibility practitioners converting scanned tables who need to verify that extracted text retains reading order and cell structure before sharing it.
accessible-table-ocr-check.distinct: It is a human QA layer for OCR accessibility, not an LLM OCR wrapper or a generic PDF editor.
accessible-table-ocr-check.workaround: Try several OCR engines, manually retype tables, or accept an unstructured PDF/text layer and discover errors only while reading it.

action-parity-probe.title: Action Parity Probe
action-parity-probe.description: Check GitHub Actions workflows for runner differences before changing CI.
action-parity-probe.why: Compare workflow assumptions before moving a CI job.
action-parity-probe.detail: A CLI that statically inventories workflow actions, images, permissions, service containers, and shell assumptions, then runs a small probe suite and emits a portable/nonportable report. Non-goals: a CI runner, workflow translation, or hosted execution.
action-parity-probe.user: Teams evaluating local or alternate runners after GitHub Actions incidents who need evidence of workflow behavior differences before moving CI.
action-parity-probe.distinct: It measures migration readiness rather than becoming another GitHub Actions substitute.
action-parity-probe.workaround: Run act locally, read image documentation, fix failures one by one, and only discover platform differences after an outage or cutover.

actuals-job-sequencer.user: A solo or two-person trade business scheduling dependent job steps who needs the next promised dates to move when the prior step actually finishes late.
actuals-job-sequencer.distinct: It recomputes only the consequences of actual job progress; it is not a dispatch platform or generic project manager.
actuals-job-sequencer.workaround: Maintain a whiteboard or spreadsheet, change every downstream date manually, then text clients if someone notices the collision.

adaptive-metronome-lab.detail: Offline web metronome with bounded random drift, ramp, delayed-beat, and recovery drills; save/share a tiny session preset and export a practice log. Non-goals: AI listening assessment, music streaming, or notation editing.
adaptive-metronome-lab.user: Musicians practicing timing and expressive playback who need controlled tempo variation and repeatable drills rather than a fixed click or destructive notation hacks.
adaptive-metronome-lab.distinct: It is a reproducible timing-drill instrument, not a thin AI music tutor or a standard click-track clone.
adaptive-metronome-lab.workaround: Use a fixed metronome, manually change tempo, create notation hacks, or edit audio after export.

agent-cli-contract.title: Agent CLI Contract

agent-cli-contract.why: Define a command-line contract for an agent tool.
agent-cli-contract.detail: CLI that runs a declarative fixture suite against another CLI, snapshots TTY and JSON modes, validates error taxonomy, detects nondeterministic fields, and writes a Markdown/JSON contract report. Non-goals: an agent framework, natural-language command generation, terminal emulator or benchmark league table.
agent-cli-contract.user: CLI maintainers whose commands will be driven by coding agents and scripts, and who need to verify stable machine contracts without making the human CLI unpleasant.
agent-cli-contract.distinct: It tests deterministic interfaces for agents and humans, rather than wrapping a CLI in another LLM layer.
agent-cli-contract.workaround: Hand-test prompts, parse colored terminal output, or build custom smoke tests for each command.

agent-diff-gate.title: Diff Gate

agent-diff-gate.why: Review agent-authored changes with required owners and test evidence before merge.
agent-diff-gate.detail: GitHub app that turns one agent PR into a policy-tagged review packet: changed contracts, migrations, tests run, risky paths, and required owner sign-off. Non-goals: generating code, replacing Git hosting, or autonomous merges.
agent-diff-gate.user: 3–30 person software teams using coding agents who need a responsible engineer to understand, constrain, and approve an agent-produced change before merge.
agent-diff-gate.distinct: It is a review-control surface for accountable change, not another coding agent or generic PR summarizer.
agent-diff-gate.workaround: Open huge PR diffs, rely on agent prose summaries, or ask a second agent to review the first.

agent-permission-map.title: Permit Map
agent-permission-map.description: Resolve coding-agent permissions before an agent runs.
agent-permission-map.why: Map the permissions an agent can use.
agent-permission-map.detail: A local CLI that reads configured agent policy files, resolves precedence into an allow/deny table, highlights shadowed rules, and emits a reviewable Markdown report. Non-goals: running agents, storing secrets, or changing vendor settings.
agent-permission-map.user: Engineers using coding agents across several repositories who need to see the effective allow/deny policy before an agent runs.
agent-permission-map.distinct: It is a resolved-policy inspector, not another agent, secret vault, or permission system.
agent-permission-map.workaround: Hand-read several JSON settings files, duplicate global rules into projects, and discover mismatches through prompts or failed tool calls.

agent-secret-capsule.title: Agent Secret Capsule
agent-secret-capsule.description: Run one coding-agent command with a temporary credential, redact output, and save a no-value receipt.
agent-secret-capsule.why: Give a coding agent one temporary credential without placing its value in the prompt or receipt.
agent-secret-capsule.detail: A local CLI that injects a selected secret only into a named subprocess or localhost credential broker, strips exact and encoded values from captured stdout/stderr, expires the lease, and writes a no-value receipt. Non-goals: secret-manager replacement, browser automation, or autonomous approval of new scopes.
agent-secret-capsule.user: Developers allowing a coding or browser agent to use a narrowly scoped credential who need the command to succeed without exposing the raw credential in prompts, terminal output, or tool traces.
agent-secret-capsule.distinct: It governs one agent action and its observable output, rather than storing another copy of the team's secrets.
agent-secret-capsule.workaround: Put secrets in environment variables, give an agent broad shell access, manually redact output, use a separate sandbox, or prohibit the action altogether.

agent-write-barrier.title: Agent Write Barrier
agent-write-barrier.description: Block coding-agent writes outside your project and review lasting changes in watched paths.
agent-write-barrier.why: Block coding agents from writing outside allowed project paths.
agent-write-barrier.detail: A CLI wrapper that launches an agent in a constrained directory, snapshots allowed and adjacent paths, blocks writes outside policy, and emits a reviewable write receipt including ignored/untracked files. Non-goals: autonomous code review, remote execution, or malware detection claims.
agent-write-barrier.user: Developers running coding agents locally who need to let an agent edit a worktree while preventing persistent files outside the intended review surface.
agent-write-barrier.distinct: It makes the filesystem review boundary explicit; it is neither a coding agent nor a thin wrapper around one.
agent-write-barrier.workaround: Trust the agent, use a broad container mount, inspect git diff, or hand-configure OS sandboxing per tool.

alert-config-change-ledger.title: Alert Config Ledger

alert-config-change-ledger.why: Compare reviewed and live alert routes, then show recipient, severity, and route changes.
alert-config-change-ledger.detail: A CLI that snapshots configured alert objects through read-only APIs or exports, normalizes them, compares to a git baseline, and renders a timeline of route/recipient/severity changes. Non-goals: sending alerts, replacing Grafana, or configuration writes.
alert-config-change-ledger.user: Platform teams with alert routes and notification policies spread between dashboards and git who need to answer what changed, where it came from, and whether the live state matches review.
alert-config-change-ledger.distinct: It is an accountability lens for live alert configuration, not another observability dashboard or IaC engine.
alert-config-change-ledger.workaround: Export dashboard JSON, browse UI history, keep partial YAML in a repository, and reconcile changes during incidents.

alert-evidence-envelope.title: Alert Evidence Envelope

alert-evidence-envelope.why: Attach redacted query evidence to an alert before forwarding it.

alert-evidence-envelope.user: On-call engineers and webhook consumers who need a safe, sufficient incident excerpt with an alert instead of a bare dashboard link followed by extra authenticated lookups.
alert-evidence-envelope.distinct: It creates a portable, least-privilege incident artifact rather than another alerting system or message-noise filter.
alert-evidence-envelope.workaround: Click through to a dashboard, copy logs into Slack, or grant downstream automation broad dashboard/API credentials.

android-backup-coverage.title: Android Backup Coverage

android-backup-coverage.detail: An Android app that inventories configured source folders, computes local file manifests, reads a user-selected destination manifest/share, highlights missing/late files, and schedules a visible verification reminder. Non-goals: a cloud-storage provider, hidden background uploads, or app-data backup bypasses.
android-backup-coverage.user: Android owners who self-host or use multiple backup destinations and need proof that new photos and selected folders actually reached a second copy.
android-backup-coverage.distinct: It measures backup coverage across tools instead of competing to become the user’s next photo cloud.
android-backup-coverage.workaround: Trust background upload, open a backup app periodically, compare folders manually, or write ad hoc rsync scripts.

android-backup-receipt.title: Android Backup Receipt

android-backup-receipt.detail: Android app that inventories chosen SAF folders, computes a privacy-preserving manifest, compares it with an attached USB/WebDAV/S3 destination, and produces a dated restore receipt with missing/changed counts. Non-goals: backing up protected app data, bypassing Android permissions, or operating a cloud.
android-backup-receipt.user: Android owners moving phones or relying on self-hosted backup who need to know which local photos, files, and app-export folders are actually recoverable.
android-backup-receipt.distinct: It verifies backup coverage across destinations rather than trying to replace every Android backup provider.
android-backup-receipt.workaround: Assume a cloud photo app succeeded, copy selected folders by USB, or discover missing files while restoring a new phone.

android-compat-scout.title: Android Compat Scout
android-compat-scout.description: Compare Android setup changes after an update with a local command-line report.
android-compat-scout.why: Check Android app and device compatibility before you install or update.
android-compat-scout.detail: Installable desktop CLI that collects a consented adb snapshot, checks declared app/device prerequisites, compares saved before/after snapshots, and creates a private compatibility report. Non-goals: rooting, bypassing Android Auto restrictions, or modifying installed apps.
android-compat-scout.user: Owners of customized Android phones, vehicle dongles, and niche local apps who need to know why an upgrade or unrooted device no longer supports their setup.
android-compat-scout.distinct: It is a configuration-diff and diagnosis tool for legitimate local setups, not an Android modification service.
android-compat-scout.workaround: Users downgrade, root, read device-specific threads, toggle settings blindly, or buy another dongle without an evidence trail.

android-select-speak-canvas.title: TapRead Canvas

android-select-speak-canvas.why: Select text in a screenshot or image and hear it read aloud. OCR and speech stay on your device.
android-select-speak-canvas.detail: An Android accessibility-service companion: a user invokes a floating button, draws one rectangle, gets on-device OCR and immediate TTS, and can repeat the last region. Non-goals: continuous screen recording, gameplay automation, remote streaming, translation, or cloud OCR.
android-select-speak-canvas.user: An Android user who needs text in a game, streamed desktop, image, or custom canvas read aloud quickly without waiting for the app to implement accessibility labels.
android-select-speak-canvas.distinct: It is a deliberately narrow, one-gesture reading aid for inaccessible pixels, not another general OCR scanner or voice assistant.
android-select-speak-canvas.workaround: Use system Select to Speak where it works, take screenshots into an OCR app, ask someone else, or abandon the activity.

android-site-blocker-private.title: Android website blocker that never phones home

android-site-blocker-private.why: Block websites on Android without accounts or tracking.

android-site-blocker-private.user: Android users who want a permanent, hard-to-bypass block on specific sites without a focus-app subscription or an app that logs their browsing; job: block a domain list device-wide with no data collection.
android-site-blocker-private.distinct: Positioned on verifiable zero-telemetry and simplicity rather than feature breadth; incumbents monetise tracking or subscriptions.
android-site-blocker-private.workaround: NextDNS/AdGuard DNS (third-party service), uBlock filters in Firefox only, Digital Wellbeing (limits, not blocks), paid focus apps.

animatic-event-strip.title: Animatic Event Strip
animatic-event-strip.description: Plan frames, sound cues, and event markers offline before engine work.
animatic-event-strip.why: Plan animation events in a simple timeline.
animatic-event-strip.detail: Offline timeline with image cards, waveform snippets, named markers, frame-range labels, and JSON/CSV export for Godot/Unity adapters. Non-goals: tweening, character animation, AI image generation, or a full project manager.
animatic-event-strip.user: Solo 2D animators and small game teams who need to plan visual beats, sound cues, and interaction windows before committing to a full animation package or engine scene.
animatic-event-strip.distinct: The core unit is an implementation-neutral event strip, not an AI animator or replacement game engine.
animatic-event-strip.workaround: Use sticky notes and a video editor, put placeholder code calls directly in an engine animation, or maintain a spreadsheet that drifts from the animatic.

animation-shot-runner.title: Shot Runner
animation-shot-runner.description: Render named animation previews from one local command.
animation-shot-runner.why: Run named animation shots locally, cache frames, and preserve verifiable preview receipts from one safe CLI.
animation-shot-runner.detail: Local CLI reading a shot manifest, invoking allowlisted renderer commands, caching frame sequences, producing contact sheets and a JSON receipt with source hash/fps/colorspace. Non-goals: animation authoring, cloud rendering, video hosting, or generative video.
animation-shot-runner.user: Small animation teams and technical artists who need repeatable preview renders for named shots without driving a browser UI or maintaining a full studio pipeline.
animation-shot-runner.distinct: It is a provenance and repeatability layer around existing creative tools, not another timeline editor.
animation-shot-runner.workaround: Keep a browser or editor open, click export per shot, record ad-hoc shell notes, or build a bespoke render script.

answer-anchored-flashcards.title: Recall Anchor
answer-anchored-flashcards.description: Score flashcards from typed answers and set the next review date.
answer-anchored-flashcards.why: Make flashcards from answers you already wrote.
answer-anchored-flashcards.detail: Offline PWA for 3 card types: exact text, numeric tolerance, and checklist recall. It records the answer before revealing the key, shows why the suggested interval changed, and exports CSV/Anki fields. Non-goals: generating cards, hosting decks, or diagnosing learning ability.
answer-anchored-flashcards.user: Anki-style self-learners who know a card only when they can produce a concrete answer, but dislike guessing their own recall rating.
answer-anchored-flashcards.distinct: It improves the decision between recall and scheduling rather than being another flashcard library or an LLM card generator.
answer-anchored-flashcards.workaround: Learners select an Anki rating from memory, type a private note elsewhere, or avoid cards that cannot be scored exactly.

api-example-linter.title: API Example Linter
api-example-linter.description: Lint API documentation examples against OpenAPI before readers use them.
api-example-linter.why: Catch stale JSON and curl examples against OpenAPI before readers do.
api-example-linter.detail: CLI extracts JSON/curl examples from Markdown/OpenAPI, validates them against a chosen operation/schema, optionally runs safe mock checks, and posts line-level CI annotations. Non-goals: documentation hosting or API fuzzing.
api-example-linter.user: API maintainers who need documentation examples to remain executable and representative as schemas and generated clients change.
api-example-linter.distinct: It tests the examples humans copy, not merely the formal specification.
api-example-linter.workaround: Copy examples into tests, trust generated docs, or discover stale examples through support tickets.

api-fixture-matrix.title: Fixture Matrix
api-fixture-matrix.description: Test one API endpoint with local JSON fixture variants.
api-fixture-matrix.why: Run one API endpoint across a reviewable matrix of local JSON fixtures.
api-fixture-matrix.detail: A local CLI that reads an OpenAPI operation plus JSON fixtures, runs a Cartesian or named matrix, and emits a colorized HTML/JSON failure diff. Non-goals: hosted mock APIs, auth vaults, or test-framework replacement.
api-fixture-matrix.user: Backend/API engineers who need to prove one endpoint works across a small but meaningful matrix of payload variants.
api-fixture-matrix.distinct: The useful unit is a reproducible fixture matrix and semantic result diff, not another REST client.
api-fixture-matrix.workaround: Duplicate requests in Postman/Bruno, hand-maintain JSON files, or add one-off test code.

api-handoff-audit.title: API Handoff Audit
api-handoff-audit.description: Check API handoff gaps before a teammate inherits a repository.
api-handoff-audit.why: Find missing setup steps before handing an API workspace to someone else.
api-handoff-audit.detail: CLI that reads an API workspace repository, detects unresolved variables and undocumented prerequisites, executes an explicitly selected smoke set against a local/staging target, and emits a shareable handoff report. Non-goals: API design, request authoring UI, cloud workspace hosting, or credential vaulting.
api-handoff-audit.user: A two-to-ten person engineering team that needs a new contributor to run a shared API workflow without asking where its collection, variables, credentials, and setup steps live.
api-handoff-audit.distinct: It is a handoff completeness checker, not another API client or the existing fixture-result matrix concept.
api-handoff-audit.workaround: Put Bruno/Insomnia/Postman files in Git, pass environment details in chat, or write one-off curl commands.

api-profile-guard.title: API Profile Guard
api-profile-guard.description: Block wrong-environment API requests before your client runs.
api-profile-guard.why: Block API requests that do not match the chosen environment or policy.
api-profile-guard.detail: A local proxy/CLI wrapper that resolves named env files, displays a non-secret profile fingerprint, validates host/method/path/body policies, requires an explicit production acknowledgement, and logs a no-value receipt. Non-goals: an HTTP client GUI, secret vault, API gateway, or request history cloud.
api-profile-guard.user: Developers switching API requests among development, staging, and production who need an unmistakable, policy-checked preflight before a request uses the wrong base URL, environment file, or credential class.
api-profile-guard.distinct: It adds a portable safety checkpoint around existing clients and curl, not a new REST client or another API test suite.
api-profile-guard.workaround: Rename .env files, use separate collections, edit base URLs by hand, rely on color conventions, or fall back to curl with copied variables.

api-scenario-patch.title: API Scenario Patch
api-scenario-patch.description: Record API flows as redacted Markdown and YAML patches for Git review.
api-scenario-patch.why: Record multi-step API flows as redacted Markdown and YAML scenario patches for Git review.
api-scenario-patch.detail: A CLI/proxy that records an opted-in sequence of HTTP exchanges, replaces configured secrets with placeholders, extracts selected response values into named variables, and writes a deterministic Markdown plus YAML scenario patch. Non-goals: being a REST client, cloud collaboration suite, or API test framework.
api-scenario-patch.user: Small API teams that need to review a realistic, multi-step request scenario in Git without sharing a hosted API-client workspace.
api-scenario-patch.distinct: The product captures a reviewable change narrative for an API flow; it does not compete to replace the user's everyday HTTP client or duplicate a fixture matrix runner.
api-scenario-patch.workaround: Duplicate requests in Postman/Bruno, paste curl commands into pull requests, or maintain loosely related JSON files and README notes.

api-version-replay.title: Version Replay
api-version-replay.description: Test saved webhook versions against localhost before a provider API upgrade.
api-version-replay.why: Capture, redact, compare, and replay old webhook contracts against localhost.
api-version-replay.detail: A local CLI that stores redacted HTTP/webhook fixtures with version labels, replays them to localhost, and reports header/body/schema differences by version. Non-goals: payment processing, a public webhook relay, or a provider emulator.
api-version-replay.user: Engineers maintaining an integration pinned to an older third-party API version who need to test local code against that exact wire contract before upgrading.
api-version-replay.distinct: It is a versioned inbound-contract replay tool, not another REST client, mock server, or billing integration.
api-version-replay.workaround: Change an account-wide API default, expose a temporary internet endpoint, hand-edit fixtures, or defer an upgrade until a dependency catches up.

app-flow-reader.title: App Flow Reader
app-flow-reader.description: Follow each saved route through dense workplace apps, one clear step at a time.
app-flow-reader.why: Read a web app as a sequence of screens and actions.
app-flow-reader.detail: A Chromium extension that lets a user save 3-10 named steps for a site, announces the current step and its visible anchor, and provides large, high-contrast next/back controls. Non-goals: autonomous clicking, credential handling, or a replacement screen reader.
app-flow-reader.user: Knowledge workers with progressive low vision who must complete recurring tasks in dense web applications such as Salesforce, PowerBI, and internal tools.
app-flow-reader.distinct: It preserves a person's own reliable workflow through imperfect enterprise software instead of attempting to replace a screen reader with an AI agent.
app-flow-reader.workaround: Increase font size, invert contrast, memorize keyboard paths, use a conventional screen reader, or ask a colleague for help.

appointment-capacity-map.title: Capacity Map
appointment-capacity-map.description: Check service-job overlaps before changing your calendar.
appointment-capacity-map.why: Plan capacity for a small service team.
appointment-capacity-map.detail: Local planning PWA with staff, services, shared resources, overlap rules, and a visual what-can-book-now matrix. Non-goals: public booking page, payments, calendar sync, or route planning.
appointment-capacity-map.user: Two-to-ten-person service businesses that need to express which jobs can overlap by staff member, service type, and shared resource without buying enterprise scheduling.
appointment-capacity-map.distinct: It makes conditional overlap understandable; it is not a booking link clone.
appointment-capacity-map.workaround: Separate calendars, duplicate event types, manual availability blocks, or rejecting useful bookings to avoid accidental conflicts.

arazzo-proof-runner.title: Arazzo Proof Runner
arazzo-proof-runner.description: Run Arazzo workflows and create a redacted proof bundle for API reviews.
arazzo-proof-runner.why: Run Arazzo workflows locally and save a redacted proof bundle for API reviews.
arazzo-proof-runner.detail: CLI supports a documented Arazzo subset, executes against a selected environment, captures redacted request/response metadata and assertions, compares two runs, and writes a static HTML/JSON proof bundle. Non-goals: an API client GUI, LLM agent integration, cloud collaboration, or broad OpenAPI generation.
arazzo-proof-runner.user: An API owner experimenting with OpenAPI Arazzo who needs a small local runner that turns a multi-step workflow into a reproducible evidence report for tests and integration reviews.
arazzo-proof-runner.distinct: It focuses on auditable workflow evidence for an under-served open standard, not another general API client.
arazzo-proof-runner.workaround: Hand-write Postman/Bruno collections or scripts, run an experimental runner, and save request/response snippets manually.

assessment-authorship-receipts.title: Work Log Check
assessment-authorship-receipts.description: Local-first assignment journal that lets students attach timestamped planning notes, intermediate exports, source citations, and a two-minute self-explanation;
assessment-authorship-receipts.detail: Local-first assignment journal that lets students attach timestamped planning notes, intermediate exports, source citations, and a two-minute self-explanation; teachers receive a concise receipt. Non-goals: AI detection, keystroke logging, webcam monitoring, or replacing an LMS.
assessment-authorship-receipts.user: Teachers assigning take-home work in the chatbot era who need a humane way to see a student's process without webcam proctoring or AI-detection claims.
assessment-authorship-receipts.distinct: It documents a learner's chosen evidence of process instead of pretending to infer authorship from writing or surveillance data.
assessment-authorship-receipts.workaround: Use invasive proctoring, unreliable AI detectors, oral defenses for everyone, or ignore process and grade only a polished final artifact.

async-trace-stitcher.title: Async Trace Stitcher
async-trace-stitcher.description: Build a reviewable timeline for one failed transaction from redacted logs, queues, and webhook exports.
async-trace-stitcher.why: Build a reviewable timeline for one failed transaction from redacted log, queue, and webhook exports.
async-trace-stitcher.detail: A local web app that accepts redacted JSON/NDJSON exports from logs and webhooks, correlates configured IDs and timestamps, displays a proposed timeline with confidence, and exports a shareable incident bundle. Non-goals: ingesting live telemetry, replacing an APM, or making causal claims from no evidence.
async-trace-stitcher.user: An engineer debugging one failed customer transaction across their app, queues, webhooks, and vendors who needs a defensible timeline without deploying a full tracing platform.
async-trace-stitcher.distinct: It packages a one-off investigation from imperfect evidence rather than selling another always-on tracing backend.
async-trace-stitcher.workaround: Open several vendor consoles, search each by request ID, paste timestamps into a document, and manually infer causality.

audio-chain-cards.title: Chain Cards
audio-chain-cards.description: A local web tool that packages ordered effect recommendations/commands with audition checkpoints, timestamp labels, and a portable JSON card; it can launch…
audio-chain-cards.why: Build, audition, and share repeatable audio repair chains without uploading a recording.
audio-chain-cards.detail: A local web tool that packages ordered effect recommendations/commands with audition checkpoints, timestamp labels, and a portable JSON card; it can launch compatible Audacity/ffmpeg actions but does not implement proprietary restoration. Non-goals: a de-reverb model, cloud rendering, or a full DAW.
audio-chain-cards.user: Beginning audio creators who need to apply and share a known-good repair or finishing sequence—such as de-echo followed by cleanup and labeled review—without learning a whole DAW template system.
audio-chain-cards.distinct: It captures a reviewable audio-treatment procedure rather than competing with restoration software.
audio-chain-cards.workaround: Search effect menus, save opaque app presets, keep screenshots of settings, and leave timestamps in notes.

audio-gap-loop.title: Audio Gap Loop
audio-gap-loop.description: Practise audio clips with timed speaking gaps and repeats.
audio-gap-loop.why: Bring your own audio. Listen, pause to speak, and repeat at your pace—privately and offline.
audio-gap-loop.detail: A browser-only audio practice player: import personally owned clips, mark a transcript line, set listen/pause/repeat cadence, and keep a local completion log. Non-goals: speech scoring, a licensed media catalog, or child data collection.
audio-gap-loop.user: A language learner or parent helping a child who needs repeatable listen-say-check practice from short audio without addictive gamification.
audio-gap-loop.distinct: It is a configurable cadence tool for owned audio, not another course, chatbot, or unreliable pronunciation grader.
audio-gap-loop.workaround: Replay clips in a media player, make audio Anki cards, or use Duolingo despite its incentive design.

audio-graph-sketchpad.title: Patchboard
audio-graph-sketchpad.description: Build, hear, and export a six-module Web Audio graph before adding it to your code.
audio-graph-sketchpad.why: Build, hear, inspect, and share small Web Audio signal graphs in your browser.
audio-graph-sketchpad.detail: Static web patchboard with six native nodes, animated signal path, BPM scheduler, click-to-hear A/B changes, and shareable URL fragment. Non-goals: DAW tracks, cloud projects, sample marketplace, AI composition.
audio-graph-sketchpad.user: Creative coders learning Web Audio who need to hear and inspect a small signal graph before embedding it in a performance or toy.
audio-graph-sketchpad.distinct: It teaches audible causal relationships in a graph, rather than wrapping an LLM around sound design.
audio-graph-sketchpad.workaround: Read API docs, make throwaway CodePens, or debug by ear in an application that also contains UI and game logic.

audio-reactive-scene.title: Audio Reactive Scene
audio-reactive-scene.description: Make page audio drive a private, responsive canvas scene.
audio-reactive-scene.why: Add sound-driven scenes to a web project.
audio-reactive-scene.detail: A copyable web component with three local canvas scenes, Web Audio analyser input, motion-reduction mode, manual intensity controls, and static poster fallback. Non-goals: microphone analytics, cloud rendering, AI art, or audio hosting.
audio-reactive-scene.user: Indie site owners, streamers, and event makers who want a tasteful, controllable audio-reactive visual scene without recording visitors or embedding a heavy visualiser product.
audio-reactive-scene.distinct: It is an accessible, privacy-first scene component, not an autoplaying effect library or a full music visualiser app.
audio-reactive-scene.workaround: Embed a generic waveform, use a CPU-heavy visualiser package, autoplay decorative effects, or commission a custom canvas sketch.

audio-reflection-markers.title: Audio Reflection Markers
audio-reflection-markers.description: Mark podcast and lecture moments, then save one short cue to revisit.
audio-reflection-markers.why: Catch one useful moment from any recording, turn it into a recall cue, and revisit it later.
audio-reflection-markers.detail: Mobile-first PWA for user-supplied audio/video links or local files: one-button timestamp marker, typed/voice takeaway, optional action date, and Markdown/CSV export. Non-goals: downloading platforms' media, automatic episode transcription, summaries, or public clip sharing.
audio-reflection-markers.user: Podcast and lecture listeners who need to turn a personally useful moment into one short recall/action prompt without trying to summarize an entire episode.
audio-reflection-markers.distinct: It captures an intentional learning commitment, not a transcript, AI summary, or media library.
audio-reflection-markers.workaround: Bookmark timestamps, make voice notes, use Snipd/Readwise, or manually create a document of Q&A later.

audio-wrapper-batch.title: Wrapline
audio-wrapper-batch.description: Add intros, outros, and music to voice tracks, then export WAV or MP3 batches without uploads.
audio-wrapper-batch.why: Add the same intro, outro, music bed, loudness, and filenames to many voice tracks in your browser.
audio-wrapper-batch.detail: A local desktop/PWA utility that accepts WAV/MP3 voice files plus a recipe for intro, outro, bed, loudness, and naming; it renders a reviewable batch and writes a receipt. Non-goals: multitrack editing, cloud storage, transcription, or AI voice generation.
audio-wrapper-batch.user: Independent podcasters, radio makers, and course creators who need to turn many finished voice tracks into consistently branded deliverables without rebuilding the same intro, outro, bed, and export setup every time.
audio-wrapper-batch.distinct: It is a recipe-driven finishing line, not another audio editor or a generative podcast service.
audio-wrapper-batch.workaround: Manually duplicate a project, apply Audacity macros, or outsource the batch job to a DAW or ffmpeg script.

automation-action-receipts.title: Action Receipts
automation-action-receipts.description: Record automated changes as signed local receipts, then verify them without a server.
automation-action-receipts.why: Create portable, signed receipts for automated repository and service changes. Verify the full chain offline.
automation-action-receipts.detail: A local sidecar/CLI protocol that accepts declared tool events, chains hashes, signs an exportable JSON/HTML receipt, and verifies it offline. Non-goals: agent orchestration, surveillance, credential storage, or proving real-world identity.
automation-action-receipts.user: Teams letting agents, scripts, or CI automations change repositories and services who need a readable, tamper-evident answer to what ran, with which inputs, and under whose authorization.
automation-action-receipts.distinct: It makes automation accountability portable and verifiable, rather than adding another autonomous agent or generic logging service.
automation-action-receipts.workaround: Rely on mutable CI logs, screenshots, chat transcripts, or an internal database audit trail that does not cover the actual command/input/output chain.

availability-dst-audit.title: Availability DST Audit
availability-dst-audit.description: Check booking hours across daylight-saving changes before you publish availability.
availability-dst-audit.why: Audit booking availability across daylight-saving changes.
availability-dst-audit.detail: A static web tool that accepts weekly hours, IANA zones, and a date range, then renders overlap/DST boundary cases and exports an ICS/CSV expected-slot fixture. Non-goals: calendar sync, booking pages, reminders, or AI scheduling.
availability-dst-audit.user: A consultant, recruiter, or distributed team coordinator who needs proof that published booking availability respects intended local working hours across daylight-saving changes.
availability-dst-audit.distinct: It tests scheduling claims rather than replacing a calendar or booking product.
availability-dst-audit.workaround: Manually inspect a booking page around DST weekends, add buffer blocks, or wait for invitees to report wrong times.

backfill-timecards.title: Backfill Timecards
backfill-timecards.description: Reconstruct freelance workweeks from calendar events, then export invoice-ready CSV.
backfill-timecards.why: Reconstruct a freelance workweek privately, then export an invoice-ready CSV.
backfill-timecards.detail: Offline weekly board that imports calendar events, clones prior patterns, fills project→client mappings, records explainable work blocks, and exports invoice-ready CSV. Non-goals: employee monitoring, screenshots, automatic AI time inference, payroll, or invoicing.
backfill-timecards.user: A freelancer who records a week of work after the fact and needs to reconstruct, copy, and associate repeated time entries with the right client/project before invoicing.
backfill-timecards.distinct: It supports honest retrospective reconstruction, not surveillance-style automatic time tracking or a full project suite.
backfill-timecards.workaround: Run a timer imperfectly, rely on calendar history and memory, then copy/paste entries in a spreadsheet or timesheet system at week end.

background-worktree-verifier.title: Worktree Verifier
background-worktree-verifier.description: Check changed Git worktrees in the background and keep each branch's current result visible.
background-worktree-verifier.why: Run configured checks in separate Git worktrees and see each current result and last passing commit.
background-worktree-verifier.detail: A local daemon/CLI that discovers configured git worktrees, watches relevant changes, runs declared fast checks in isolated worktrees, and serves a localhost status page with last-pass commit hashes. Non-goals: cloud CI, agent orchestration, test generation, or full-suite scheduling.
background-worktree-verifier.user: Developers using multiple agent or human worktrees who need inexpensive continuous smoke validation of each changed worktree without opening a test UI or mixing branches.
background-worktree-verifier.distinct: It coordinates test freshness across real worktrees rather than creating another test runner or AI coding agent.
background-worktree-verifier.workaround: Switch branches, wait for CI, run tests manually in a root worktree, or keep several terminals with unclear test freshness.

backup-coverage-ledger.title: Backup Coverage Ledger
backup-coverage-ledger.description: Track backup coverage and restore proof in one browser ledger.
backup-coverage-ledger.why: Record backup coverage and proof that files restore.
backup-coverage-ledger.detail: Offline/shared YAML-or-CSV ledger with asset records, backup targets, last proof date, recovery instructions, expiry alerts, and a printable restore drill checklist. Non-goals: performing backups or storing credentials.
backup-coverage-ledger.user: A small-team operator who needs to know which critical data sets are covered, by which backup, and whether the backup can actually be extracted.
backup-coverage-ledger.distinct: It makes backup coverage auditable across tools instead of becoming another backup engine.
backup-coverage-ledger.workaround: Spreadsheets, wiki lists, cron scripts, full-disk snapshots, and periodic manual restore attempts.

backup-restore-drill.title: Restore Drill
backup-restore-drill.description: Verify one important backup file restores before you need it.
backup-restore-drill.detail: A local CLI that runs configured safe sample restores into a temporary directory, verifies hashes and selected application-open checks, records an immutable receipt, and alerts only on a failed or overdue drill. Non-goals: backup transport, credential vaulting, or full disaster-recovery orchestration.
backup-restore-drill.user: Individuals and small teams with scripted backups who need a low-friction, repeatable proof that their backup can restore the files they care about.
backup-restore-drill.distinct: It proves recovery through a small recurring drill instead of being another backup engine or dashboard.
backup-restore-drill.workaround: Read backup job logs, run an occasional vendor-specific check, or attempt a full restore only during an emergency.

bank-csv-intake-check.title: Bank CSV Intake Check
bank-csv-intake-check.description: Check bank CSV, OFX, and QFX files for import issues before they reach a ledger.
bank-csv-intake-check.why: Check a bank CSV or OFX for silent row loss and ambiguous assumptions before importing it into your books.
bank-csv-intake-check.detail: Local drag-and-drop CSV/OFX preflight that identifies delimiter/encoding/date/decimal assumptions, duplicate and missing transaction candidates, balance coverage, and emits a scrubbed import report. Non-goals: bank connectivity, bookkeeping, categorization, or tax advice.
bank-csv-intake-check.user: A self-employed person or bookkeeper importing a bank CSV who needs to know, before changing books, whether the file parsed completely and which rows are ambiguous.
bank-csv-intake-check.distinct: It is a reversible pre-import evidence step, not another personal-finance ledger.
bank-csv-intake-check.workaround: Retry an import, edit CSV headers and encodings in a spreadsheet, then manually compare balances and row counts.

bank-import-receipts.title: Bank Import Receipts
bank-import-receipts.description: Check CSV, OFX, and QIF bank files before import, then export a signed receipt.
bank-import-receipts.why: Check a bank CSV before import and save a record of what changed.
bank-import-receipts.detail: Local CSV/OFX/QIF preflight tool that detects encoding/date/column errors, previews normalized transactions, estimates duplicates, reconciles opening/closing balance when supplied, and exports a signed import receipt. Non-goals: bank credential aggregation, transaction categorization AI, budgeting, or cloud storage.
bank-import-receipts.user: A local-first budgeter importing bank files who needs a trustworthy explanation of what was read, ignored, duplicated, and changed before it affects the budget.
bank-import-receipts.distinct: It is an explainable preflight and audit artifact that complements budget apps instead of cloning one.
bank-import-receipts.workaround: Retry the import, inspect browser logs, manually compare balances, or postpone using a self-hosted budget tool.

barcode-intake-card.title: Barcode Intake Card
barcode-intake-card.description: Create private, printable item cards from barcodes.
barcode-intake-card.why: Scan an item, add its details, and print an intake card.
barcode-intake-card.detail: Offline PWA scanner with manual/CSV lookup, photo and supplier fields, duplicate-candidate review, and printable one-up label/card export. Non-goals: warehouse management, automatic web scraping, purchase orders, or a universal product database.
barcode-intake-card.user: A micro-seller or workshop receiving miscellaneous stock who needs to turn a barcode scan into a reviewable item card without sending supplier or inventory data to a third party.
barcode-intake-card.distinct: It solves the uncertain first intake step before a business needs a stock system, rather than cloning an ERP or label suite.
barcode-intake-card.workaround: Type details manually, use a generic barcode lookup, upload a CSV to a label site, or write one-off API scripts.

batch-cart.title: Batch Cart
batch-cart.description: Combine recipes into one shopping list when servings change.
batch-cart.why: Calculate a household shop across several items.
batch-cart.detail: Browser-local recipe cards or pasted ingredients; per-recipe servings; deterministic unit-aware aggregation; pantry checkbox exclusions; and a print/share shopping list. Non-goals: recipe scraping, grocery delivery, nutrition advice, or social recipes.
batch-cart.user: People cooking several recipes for a household or event who need a single accurate shopping list after changing servings for each recipe.
batch-cart.distinct: The central artifact is a deterministic, editable multi-recipe purchase calculation—not a recipe site or a thin LLM shopping-list wrapper.
batch-cart.workaround: Copy ingredients by hand to a notes app, use a spreadsheet, or wire recipes through an LLM and task app.

bench-bin-bom.title: Bench Bin BOM
bench-bin-bom.description: Check project parts lists against bench drawers before you start building.
bench-bin-bom.why: Compare a project BOM with what is already in your drawers.
bench-bin-bom.detail: A local desktop app with bin locations, part photo/value/quantity, CSV BOM paste, shortage and substitute notes, and a print-friendly project pull list. Non-goals: supplier marketplace, barcode hardware requirement, team ERP, automatic purchasing, or agent control of tools.
bench-bin-bom.user: A home maker or small homelab builder who needs to compare a project bill of materials with parts already in drawers before ordering or starting a build.
bench-bin-bom.distinct: The primary object is a build-ready BOM versus drawer stock, not a general warehouse system or tool-rental network.
bench-bin-bom.workaround: Memory, drawer labels, a spreadsheet, photos, a generic inventory package, or buying another part 'just in case.'

bgg-import-normalizer.title: Shelf Bridge
bgg-import-normalizer.description: Convert a BGG collection CSV into reviewable files before importing it into another tracker.
bgg-import-normalizer.why: Convert a BoardGameGeek collection CSV into reviewable CSV and JSON in your browser.
bgg-import-normalizer.detail: Static web converter that imports a BGG collection export, lets users map statuses/ratings/comments to a target-neutral schema, validates duplicates, and exports CSV/JSON profiles for Yamtrack and NeoDB-style imports. Non-goals: scraping BGG, hosting a collection, price tracking, or copying game art.
bgg-import-normalizer.user: Board-game collectors moving a BoardGameGeek collection into a personal tracker who need their ownership, wishlist, and past-ownership states to survive an import predictably.
bgg-import-normalizer.distinct: It is a reviewable collection-state bridge, not a replacement BGG database or another play-log app.
bgg-import-normalizer.workaround: Export BGG CSV, import only the rows a target accepts, then recreate statuses and notes by hand or keep multiple trackers in parallel.

big-csv-browser-viewer.title: Open, filter and pivot multi-million-row CSVs entirely in the browser
big-csv-browser-viewer.description: Filter, pivot, query, and export large CSV files entirely in your browser.
big-csv-browser-viewer.why: Filter, summarize, query and export large CSV files in your browser.
big-csv-browser-viewer.detail: Static page: drop CSV/TSV/XLSX; DuckDB-WASM loads it (streamed, up to a few GB with OPFS); virtual grid; column stats; filter builder, sort, group-by aggregates, simple pivot; SQL box for power users; export filtered CSV/Parquet. No formulas grid, no charts beyond counts, no cloud save, no collaboration.
big-csv-browser-viewer.user: Analysts, ops and finance staff handed CSV exports too big for Excel (>1,048,576 rows or multi-GB) who need to look, filter, group and cut a smaller file; job: answer a question from the file without Python or uploading it.
big-csv-browser-viewer.distinct: Combines DuckDB-scale performance with an Excel-like filter/pivot UI without upload; incumbents are either cloud or CLI.
big-csv-browser-viewer.workaround: Power Query, LibreOffice (1M-row cap), pandas/DuckDB CLI, paid desktop viewers, or upload to online CSV tools.

bike-check-card.title: Bike Check Card
bike-check-card.description: Record bike-fault evidence before asking a mechanic or cycling community for help.
bike-check-card.why: Capture exact bike fault symptoms, measurements and photos before asking for help.
bike-check-card.detail: Offline form for bike, component, mileage, pressure, symptom timeline, sensor-vs-GPS reading, and annotated photos; exports a single private link/PDF. Non-goals: diagnosing safety, recommending replacement, telemetry ingestion, or social feeds.
bike-check-card.user: A self-maintaining cyclist who needs to capture a fault's exact symptoms, component state, photos, and ride context before deciding whether to pause riding or ask a mechanic/community for help.
bike-check-card.distinct: This is an evidence-capture and handoff tool, not another ride tracker or maintenance reminder.
bike-check-card.workaround: Take ad-hoc phone photos, write a long forum post, and try to remember pressure, mileage, and sensor readings.

bike-service-receipts.title: Bike Service Receipts
bike-service-receipts.description: Record bike service, costs, odometer readings, and reminders offline on your device.
bike-service-receipts.why: Keep bicycle service receipts and get maintenance reminders privately.
bike-service-receipts.detail: Offline-first PWA with bike profiles, one-tap service receipts (actions, photo, cost, odometer), rule-based reminders, and CSV/PDF export. Non-goals: marketplace bookings, social sharing, or claiming to diagnose mechanical faults.
bike-service-receipts.user: Everyday cyclists maintaining one or more bikes who need a simple, evidence-backed record of what was done, what it cost, and what is next.
bike-service-receipts.distinct: The primary artifact is a portable service receipt and next-action evidence, not another ride feed or bike-shop CRM.
bike-service-receipts.workaround: Keep receipts in a drawer, add vague phone reminders, or remember the last clean/lube/part change.

bike-service-timeline.title: Bike Service Timeline
bike-service-timeline.description: Track service history and see what is due across all your bikes.
bike-service-timeline.why: Keep a private, portable component-service history and next-service view for every bicycle you own.
bike-service-timeline.detail: Offline PWA with bikes, components, service entries, receipts/photos, mileage/date triggers, and one chronological all-bike view exportable as CSV/print. Non-goals: parts marketplace, mechanic booking, or diagnostic advice.
bike-service-timeline.user: Owners of multiple bicycles who need a complete, portable component-service history and a clear next-service view across every bike.
bike-service-timeline.distinct: It is a portable ownership timeline across bikes, not a ride tracker or a generic to-do list.
bike-service-timeline.workaround: Keep paper notes, rely on recent activity in one bike app, search chat history, or remember when a part was last touched.

bill-runway.title: Bill Runway
bill-runway.description: Compare upcoming bills with expected income before a cash gap.
bill-runway.why: Compare upcoming bills with expected income and find the first cash gap.
bill-runway.detail: Offline PWA for a list of bills/invoices, expected income dates, one-time or recurring due rules, and a timeline that flags an uncovered amount; export a one-page payment run. Non-goals: bank aggregation, payments, credit scoring, debt advice, or tax calculation.
bill-runway.user: A person or caregiver who needs to see upcoming invoices, due dates, and cash needed before income arrives, without connecting bank accounts or adopting a full budgeting system.
bill-runway.distinct: It is a due-date cash runway, not a general ledger, expense tracker, or banking dashboard.
bill-runway.workaround: Spreadsheets, calendar reminders, paper bills, and a full expense app that starts after a transaction is already paid.

billable-receipt-split.title: Billable Split
billable-receipt-split.description: Split supplier receipts across jobs and export billable records offline.
billable-receipt-split.why: Split a supplier receipt across jobs and export cost packets.
billable-receipt-split.detail: Offline PWA that stores a receipt image, creates manual line items, allocates each line across jobs with billable flags, and exports per-job CSV/PDF evidence. Non-goals: OCR promises, bank feeds, bookkeeping automation, or tax returns.
billable-receipt-split.user: A contractor buying materials for several jobs at once who must split one supplier receipt into billable, non-billable, and reimbursable job costs without losing the source record.
billable-receipt-split.distinct: The product solves the allocation decision after capture; it is neither a receipt scanner nor a full expense-accounting clone.
billable-receipt-split.workaround: Photograph the receipt, duplicate it in a spreadsheet or accounting package, and later reconstruct the split from memory.

bills-due-board.title: Bills Due Board
bills-due-board.description: Track bills by due date, plan next week's cash, and confirm each payment on your device.
bills-due-board.why: List bills, see due weeks, and mark payments.
bills-due-board.detail: Offline bills board with manual/CSV entry, due-date and cash-week views, attachment links, paid confirmation, and export back to CSV. Non-goals: bank syncing, accounting ledger posting, payment initiation, or tax advice.
bills-due-board.user: A solo operator who records bills in a personal/business finance tool but needs a clear due-date queue and an intentional 'paid' action when cash becomes available.
bills-due-board.distinct: It is a payable-attention layer that complements a ledger instead of claiming to be accounting software.
bills-due-board.workaround: Create artificial clearing accounts, maintain a spreadsheet, or scan calendar/email reminders while separately entering payment transactions.

bills-runway.title: Bills Runway
bills-runway.description: See your lowest balance after upcoming bills, paydays, and planned spending.
bills-runway.why: See your balance after the bills you already know about.
bills-runway.detail: Offline PWA with starting balance, recurring/one-off bills, paydays, optional manual spending, and a 30/60-day daily balance projection with a low-buffer alert. Non-goals: bank sync, investment tracking, credit scoring, payment initiation, or tax advice.
bills-runway.user: People who know their regular obligations but need a trustworthy near-term cash runway without bank connections or a full envelope-budget overhaul.
bills-runway.distinct: It is a narrow cash-calendar answer, not another expense categorizer, transaction aggregator, or autonomous money tool.
bills-runway.workaround: Use a spreadsheet, calendar plus bank balance, a Plaid dashboard, or a full zero-based budget that users often abandon.

bird-audio-slicer.title: Nightjar Slicer
bird-audio-slicer.description: Split overnight bird recordings into local WAV clips for BirdNET Analyzer.
bird-audio-slicer.why: Split long bird recordings into resumable, analyzer-ready clips with a private local CLI.
bird-audio-slicer.detail: Local CLI that reads WAV/FLAC headers, makes fixed or silence-aware chunks, emits a timestamped manifest and spectrogram thumbnails, and can resume a failed batch. Non-goals: species identification model, cloud upload, or automatic public reporting.
bird-audio-slicer.user: Birders recording long overnight AudioMoth or field-recorder files who need to split, sample, and queue clips for BirdNET analysis without crashing a GUI or waiting through repeated extraction.
bird-audio-slicer.distinct: It solves the recording-scale handoff before identification, not another bird-recognition wrapper.
bird-audio-slicer.workaround: Manually split WAV files, wait for a full analysis, reduce recordings arbitrarily, or abandon a recording after the GUI fails.

bird-id-evidence-card.title: Bird ID Evidence Card
bird-id-evidence-card.description: Record bird evidence before you log an uncertain sighting.
bird-id-evidence-card.why: Record what you saw and heard before you log an uncertain bird sighting.
bird-id-evidence-card.detail: Offline-first mobile web form for recording date/location precision, visual traits, call notes, candidate species, confidence, and links to user-selected licensed reference recordings; export as a Markdown/CSV evidence card. Non-goals: species identification AI, copyrighted call library hosting, or a replacement citizen-science database.
bird-id-evidence-card.user: Birders using an identification app who need to compare a tentative result against their own observed evidence before deciding whether to log it.
bird-id-evidence-card.distinct: It improves calibration and provenance around an ID rather than offering another black-box identifier.
bird-id-evidence-card.workaround: Open multiple field-guide tabs, compare vague memories of calls, screenshot app suggestions, or record an uncertain sighting with no reasoning trail.

bird-sighting-proof-card.title: Bird Sighting Proof Card
bird-sighting-proof-card.description: Make a private bird-sighting record with local evidence and PDF or JSON exports.
bird-sighting-proof-card.why: Make a private bird-sighting record with evidence, notes, safe location choices, and PDF or JSON export.
bird-sighting-proof-card.detail: Offline proof-card builder with photo/audio attachments, extracted timestamp, rounded location options, field-mark checklist, candidate/confidence notes, and shareable PDF/JSON. Non-goals: automated species identification, public sighting map, eBird submission, or research GPS management.
bird-sighting-proof-card.user: A birder with an uncertain observation who needs to package photo, sound, time, location precision, field marks, and identification uncertainty for later review without oversharing sensitive locations.
bird-sighting-proof-card.distinct: It improves the quality and safety of uncertain observations without pretending to replace bird-identification or citizen-science networks.
bird-sighting-proof-card.workaround: Post a prose description with attachments, keep separate spreadsheets, or rely on an identification app's single suggestion.

boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.title: Meeple Import Doctor
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.description: Fix failed board-game catalog imports with a readable one-URL report.
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.why: Check why a public board-game or record page did not import into your self-hosted catalog.
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.detail: A browser-based URL inspector with pluggable public-page parsers that displays fetched status, detected fields, selector failures, normalized preview, and a copyable manual-import JSON record. Non-goals: bypassing authentication/anti-bot controls, bulk scraping, or redistributing marketplace data.
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.user: Board-game and vinyl collectors importing item URLs into a self-hosted catalog who need a clear answer when an external metadata scraper returns nothing.
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.distinct: It diagnoses an import attempt before a catalog writes anything; it is neither a BoardGameGeek clone nor a Discogs client.
boardgame-catalog-import-debugger.workaround: Try another URL, inspect container logs, retype metadata by hand, or abandon the import workflow.

boardgame-session-notes.title: Boardgame Session Notes
boardgame-session-notes.description: Record setup, rulings, scores, and outcomes for one boardgame session, then reopen the note offline.
boardgame-session-notes.why: Keep private, durable notes for every boardgame session—even offline.
boardgame-session-notes.detail: Offline session template with participants, pre-play state/photo, reusable house-rule snippets, event timeline, and final score; export a single Markdown/PDF receipt. Non-goals: rules lookup, automated scoring, BGG import, or replacing a campaign manager.
boardgame-session-notes.user: A game group that wants a compact record of a particular play—starting state, disputes, house rules, score laps, and outcomes—without losing it when an item leaves the collection.
boardgame-session-notes.distinct: It protects ephemeral session context, not another online collection or rules encyclopedia.
boardgame-session-notes.workaround: Trust memory, keep paper notes, or rely on a remote collection import to be available at the table.

booking-side-notes.title: Booking Side Notes
booking-side-notes.description: Keep side notes beside appointments without changing bookable time.
booking-side-notes.why: Keep operational notes beside appointments without blocking bookable time.
booking-side-notes.detail: Local companion PWA that imports a day’s ICS events and attaches nonblocking, time-anchored notes, checkboxes, and reminder status; print or export a daily brief. Non-goals: public booking pages, SMS delivery, calendar hosting, or CRM.
booking-side-notes.user: A small appointment business that needs to keep operational notes—call back, access detail, follow-up, supplier delay—visible beside a booking without falsely blocking another appointment slot.
booking-side-notes.distinct: It explicitly separates operational context from availability, a smaller problem than appointment scheduling itself.
booking-side-notes.workaround: Put notes in a separate notebook, a private calendar, or fake appointments that accidentally make time unavailable.

bookmark-escape-hatch.title: Bookmark Escape Hatch
bookmark-escape-hatch.description: Local browser/CLI utility that imports HTML/JSON/CSV exports, normalizes URLs/tags/dates, detects duplicates and malformed records, produces a vendor-neutral…
bookmark-escape-hatch.why: Export, find migration damage, and create portable files on your device.
bookmark-escape-hatch.detail: Local browser/CLI utility that imports HTML/JSON/CSV exports, normalizes URLs/tags/dates, detects duplicates and malformed records, produces a vendor-neutral archive plus a destination-specific dry-run report. Non-goals: another hosted read-later service or content scraping.
bookmark-escape-hatch.user: People with years of browser and service bookmarks who need a reliable, inspectable export before changing tools or services.
bookmark-escape-hatch.distinct: It is an escape and verification utility across bookmark products, not a destination bookmark manager.
bookmark-escape-hatch.workaround: Keep browser exports, try imports blindly, use vendor-specific APIs, or abandon metadata and archived context during migration.

bookmark-freshness-review.title: Bookmark Freshness Review
bookmark-freshness-review.description: Review saved links, separate check results, and export a clean archive from a local browser extension.
bookmark-freshness-review.why: Find stale bookmarks and keep notes about why each link matters.
bookmark-freshness-review.detail: Local browser extension that imports HTML bookmarks, checks status and canonical duplicates on demand, groups stale candidates, stores a short user-written purpose/context note, and exports standard HTML. Non-goals: hosted sync, AI summaries, or scraping paywalled pages.
bookmark-freshness-review.user: Researchers and professionals with years of saved links who need to decide what is dead, duplicated, paywalled, changed, or still worth keeping without uploading their bookmark archive.
bookmark-freshness-review.distinct: It is an intentional decay-management pass for a local archive, not a social read-later clone.
bookmark-freshness-review.workaround: Leave a growing archive untouched, use folders/tags manually, or migrate between bookmark services after one shuts down.

bookmark-import-audit.title: Bookmark Import Audit
bookmark-import-audit.description: Check bookmark HTML for duplicate links and folder conflicts before import.
bookmark-import-audit.why: Export for folder collisions, duplicate URLs, and missing titles before you import.
bookmark-import-audit.detail: A fully local web app that reads Netscape bookmark HTML, builds a path-aware inventory, flags lossy-import hazards and duplicate/redirect clusters, and exports a corrected HTML plus a review CSV. Non-goals: hosting bookmarks, crawling the web, or AI-written summaries.
bookmark-import-audit.user: People moving a years-old browser bookmark library who need to preserve its nested meaning and find destructive import problems before committing to a new manager.
bookmark-import-audit.distinct: It is an import safety inspection and repair tool, not another bookmark database or a thin categorization wrapper.
bookmark-import-audit.workaround: Import blindly, hand-clean folders afterward, or keep an unusable browser-export HTML file as a backup.

bookmark-merge-map.title: Bookmark Merge Map
bookmark-merge-map.description: Merge two bookmark exports, resolve duplicates and conflicts, then download merged HTML and a review CSV.
bookmark-merge-map.detail: Offline browser app that imports two bookmark HTML exports, normalizes canonical URLs, pairs likely duplicates, surfaces conflicts and one-sided links, and exports a merged HTML plus a review CSV. Non-goals: bookmark hosting, AI summaries, and account sync.
bookmark-merge-map.user: Someone whose desktop and mobile bookmark trees have diverged and who needs to merge, deduplicate, and find omissions without losing a link.
bookmark-merge-map.distinct: This is a reconciliation and proof tool before sync, rather than another bookmarking destination.
bookmark-merge-map.workaround: Export HTML, use browser sync and hope it converges, manually compare folders, or switch to Raindrop/xBrowserSync.

bookmark-proofbook.title: Bookmark Proofbook
bookmark-proofbook.description: Save context for every bookmark, then search and export your local proofbook.
bookmark-proofbook.why: Save bookmarks with the words and reason you need to find later.
bookmark-proofbook.detail: Browser extension that captures a bookmark with user-written reason, title, selected text and content hash; imports browser HTML, offers local full-text search, and exports a self-contained HTML/JSON proofbook with link-health changes. Non-goals: social bookmarking, cloud sync, automatic LLM summaries, or web-page piracy.
bookmark-proofbook.user: People with thousands of browser bookmarks who need to retain why a link mattered and export a durable local collection as bookmarking services disappear.
bookmark-proofbook.distinct: It treats a bookmark as a portable research assertion with provenance, not another feed, read-later app, or LLM tagging wrapper.
bookmark-proofbook.workaround: Keep browser folders, move to Raindrop/Pinboard, use Pocket until it closes, or rely on browser history/search and never clean the collection.

branching-problem-circle.title: Branching Problem Circle
branching-problem-circle.description: Compare approaches to one math problem with anonymous votes and facilitator-controlled hints on one shared device.
branching-problem-circle.why: Explore branching math problems together on one local board.
branching-problem-circle.detail: Offline-capable facilitator web app: author one problem, add up to six approach branches, collect anonymous ‘try this’ votes, reveal hints/branches, and export a one-page session recap. Non-goals: public child profiles, rankings, standardized-test banks, and AI solution generation.
branching-problem-circle.user: A volunteer math-circle leader running a small group of curious children who needs to reveal divergent solution paths without turning the session into test prep.
branching-problem-circle.distinct: It preserves and sequences competing approaches for a live small group, not another quiz, worksheet library, or generic online whiteboard.
branching-problem-circle.workaround: Use a whiteboard, shared slides, paper handouts, and ad hoc discussion; promising wrong approaches vanish after the meeting.

browser-game-replay-capsule.title: Replay Capsule
browser-game-replay-capsule.description: Record and replay browser-game bugs from one local file.
browser-game-replay-capsule.why: Record browser-game inputs and checkpoints, then save a replay file.
browser-game-replay-capsule.detail: NPM library to record pointer/key/gamepad events plus developer-supplied seed and checkpoints, then download/import a capped replay file. Non-goals: video recording, user-session tracking, server playback, anti-cheat.
browser-game-replay-capsule.user: A solo developer of a 2D browser game who needs a bug report that recreates the player’s inputs and timing without operating a full analytics stack.
browser-game-replay-capsule.distinct: It is an event-level reproducibility primitive, not surveillance replay or a game framework.
browser-game-replay-capsule.workaround: Ask for a screen recording, add console logs, or attempt to reproduce a vague report manually.

browser-history-export-sentinel.title: History Export Sentinel
browser-history-export-sentinel.description: Export and verify Firefox or Chromium history before changing computers or accounts.
browser-history-export-sentinel.why: Export Firefox and Chromium browser history locally, with counts, date bounds, and hashes you can verify.
browser-history-export-sentinel.detail: A local CLI that detects installed Chromium/Firefox profiles, copies databases safely, exports normalized JSON/CSV, and reports record/date ranges, locked-profile errors, and hashes. Non-goals: web-page archiving, cloud sync, or bypassing browser encryption.
browser-history-export-sentinel.user: People archiving or moving their browser history who need a cross-platform export they can verify is complete before an account or machine changes.
browser-history-export-sentinel.distinct: It is an export-verification utility, not another read-later service or browser-history visualizer.
browser-history-export-sentinel.workaround: Copy browser database files, run brittle shell scripts, or assume an export succeeded because a file was created.

calendar-handoff-card.title: Calendar Handoff Card
calendar-handoff-card.description: Create a shareable event card when a calendar invite is hard to open.
calendar-handoff-card.why: Turn an event or ICS file into a clear, timezone-safe card for chat, email, or print.
calendar-handoff-card.detail: A local web tool that accepts pasted event fields or an ICS file and creates accessible plain text, a compact image/PDF card, timezone equivalents, joining details, and a minimal add-to-calendar link. Non-goals: calendar sync, event hosting, invitations, or contact storage.
calendar-handoff-card.user: Families and small teams coordinating across calendar ecosystems who need a dependable, copyable event handoff when an invite is missed, blocked, or inconvenient to open.
calendar-handoff-card.distinct: It is a calendar interoperability handoff format, not another scheduling or shared-calendar product.
calendar-handoff-card.workaround: Forward an ICS file, screenshot the event, manually type the time/meeting link into chat, or ask everyone to join the same calendar service.

calm-scroll.title: Calm Scroll
calm-scroll.description: Stop sample page motion before installing the desktop Chromium extension.
calm-scroll.why: Stop parallax, autoplay, and distracting page motion in your browser.
calm-scroll.detail: A browser extension that detects autoplay, transforms, smooth-scroll, sticky animation, and parallax; offers a one-click stable reading mode plus per-site exceptions. Non-goals: rewriting site content, anti-ad blocking, or medical treatment claims.
calm-scroll.user: People with vestibular disorders or screen-induced motion sickness who need a stable way to read ordinary web pages without parallax, auto-advance, or animated scrolling.
calm-scroll.distinct: It provides targeted user control over real page motion instead of a generic dark theme or a site-wide accessibility audit.
calm-scroll.workaround: Turn on OS reduced motion, disable a few site settings, use reader mode where available, or leave the page.

calorie-week-view.title: Calorie Week View
calorie-week-view.description: Review calories, macros, and weight across seven days without daily scores.
calorie-week-view.why: See a week of meals and calorie or macro totals without an account.
calorie-week-view.detail: Offline PWA accepting manual entries or CSV, showing seven-day calorie/macro bands, optional weight trend, missing-day annotation, and print/export. Non-goals: barcode database, photo estimation, social feeds, coaching, or dieting prescriptions.
calorie-week-view.user: Someone logging food who needs a calm weekly view of calories and weight rather than a streak-driven daily dashboard.
calorie-week-view.distinct: The product is a weekly reflection surface for existing logs, not a gamified food-tracking clone.
calorie-week-view.workaround: Mentally average daily totals, export to a spreadsheet, or accept opaque in-app progress scores.

camera-effect-postcard.title: Postcard FX
camera-effect-postcard.description: Phone-first local web app with face landmarks, three original geometric effects, portrait-safe crop guides, timer, and PNG download. Non-goals: social feed…
camera-effect-postcard.why: Make a playful geometric postcard with your camera. Your photo stays on this device.
camera-effect-postcard.detail: Phone-first local web app with face landmarks, three original geometric effects, portrait-safe crop guides, timer, and PNG download. Non-goals: social feed, face recognition, video storage, branded celebrity effects.
camera-effect-postcard.user: Friends and event hosts wanting a playful, phone-first face effect that produces a shareable still without installing a virtual camera or surrendering video to a service.
camera-effect-postcard.distinct: It is a privacy-preserving, orientation-correct camera toy—not another social filter network.
camera-effect-postcard.workaround: Use social-network filters, awkward desktop webcam sites, or install OBS/virtual-camera components.

camera-fx-cues.title: Camera FX Cues
camera-fx-cues.description: Trigger six camera effects with number keys on your camera or the isolated sample signal.
camera-fx-cues.why: Try camera effects with cues for each shot.
