camera-fx-cues.detail: Static web scene with local camera preview and six original effects (laser, outline, pixel burst, freeze, zoom, shake), keyboard cue triggers, and a no-camera preview mode. Non-goals: face identity, recording/uploading, beauty filters, social feed.
camera-fx-cues.user: Small game-jam and classroom teams who want playful webcam effects that react to simple, explicit cues without sending video to a server.
camera-fx-cues.distinct: It is a controllable effects instrument for play, not a surveillance camera product or social-filter clone.
camera-fx-cues.workaround: Use TikTok/Instagram filters, OBS plug-ins, or custom shader code that is hard to control from a small project.

canvas-export-proof.title: Export Proof
canvas-export-proof.description: CLI/browser extension that captures a canvas's accessibility/text tree and bounding boxes before export, compares it to rendered PNG/PDF OCR/layout, and emits…
canvas-export-proof.why: Compare a live canvas with its PNG or PDF export.
canvas-export-proof.detail: CLI/browser extension that captures a canvas's accessibility/text tree and bounding boxes before export, compares it to rendered PNG/PDF OCR/layout, and emits an annotated proof image. Non-goals: hosting canvases, editing artwork, or general visual regression SaaS.
canvas-export-proof.user: People publishing diagrams, collaborative pixel canvases, and teaching visuals who need confidence that a PNG/PDF export says the same thing as the live canvas.
canvas-export-proof.distinct: It verifies the distributed creative artifact rather than competing with collaborative drawing software.
canvas-export-proof.workaround: Open every export by hand, crop screenshots, or discover a bad label after sharing the file.

canvas-regression-reel.title: Canvas Regression Reel
canvas-regression-reel.description: An npm recorder/reporter for browser canvas games: capture a seeded input trace, render checkpoint PNGs, compare tolerantly, and emit a self-contained HTML…
canvas-regression-reel.why: Replay game inputs and find the first visual canvas regression.
canvas-regression-reel.detail: An npm recorder/reporter for browser canvas games: capture a seeded input trace, render checkpoint PNGs, compare tolerantly, and emit a self-contained HTML reel. Non-goals: cloud test farm, autonomous bug fixing, asset hosting, or a game engine.
canvas-regression-reel.user: Solo browser-game developers who need visual evidence of rendering regressions, not just headless logic tests and a pile of manual screenshots.
canvas-regression-reel.distinct: It is a game-frame replay and diagnosis artifact, not generic visual-regression SaaS or an AI playtester.
canvas-regression-reel.workaround: Rerun the game manually, save screenshots by hand, use headless bots for logic only, or accept visual checks late in the release cycle.

caption-choice-memory.title: Caption Choice Memory
caption-choice-memory.description: Keep each site's caption language and on/off choice one action away.
caption-choice-memory.why: Keep your caption language and on-or-off choice for each video site.
caption-choice-memory.detail: A browser extension with a per-site caption policy: prefer language list, enable/disable default, single keyboard shortcut, and clear unsupported-player notice. Non-goals: subtitle downloading, translation, or modifying DRM playback.
caption-choice-memory.user: Caption-dependent video viewers who need their language and auto-caption preferences to be reachable in one action and retained per site/device.
caption-choice-memory.distinct: It is an accessibility preference router, not a caption generator or another video platform.
caption-choice-memory.workaround: Scroll language menus, toggle captions video by video, or tolerate an unwanted default.

caption-clarity.title: Caption Clarity
caption-clarity.description: A local WebVTT/SRT player and standards-compliant video overlay with profiles for emphasis, line length, pause-on-keyword, and user-defined confusing terms.…
caption-clarity.why: Play local video with captions shaped around the words you find hard to hear.
caption-clarity.detail: A local WebVTT/SRT player and standards-compliant video overlay with profiles for emphasis, line length, pause-on-keyword, and user-defined confusing terms. Non-goals: scraping DRM services, speech recognition, or claiming audiological personalization.
caption-clarity.user: People with high-frequency hearing loss who need captions styled around likely-to-be-misheard dialogue rather than one undifferentiated text stream.
caption-clarity.distinct: It improves how existing captions are consumed, not another automated-caption generator.
caption-clarity.workaround: Raise global caption size, rewind repeatedly, turn on subtitles that cannot be tailored, or use headphones.

caption-confidence.title: Caption Confidence
caption-confidence.description: Local web app/extension that imports VTT/SRT or reads an exposed HTML5 track, highlights user-defined sound-confusion pairs and low-confidence timing gaps, and…
caption-confidence.why: Find uncertain words in captions and replay the current line.
caption-confidence.detail: Local web app/extension that imports VTT/SRT or reads an exposed HTML5 track, highlights user-defined sound-confusion pairs and low-confidence timing gaps, and offers one-key replay. Non-goals: scraping DRM streams, generating captions, or medical claims.
caption-confidence.user: People with high-frequency hearing loss who use captions and need uncertain words made easy to catch without replaying every line.
caption-confidence.distinct: It improves comprehension of an existing caption track rather than competing as another transcription service.
caption-confidence.workaround: Replay scenes, turn on generic captions, or manually inspect a transcript.

caption-cues.title: Caption Cues
caption-cues.description: Highlight names, speaker labels, sound cues, and saved words in caption text the page makes available.
caption-cues.why: Highlight names, speaker labels, sound cues, and saved words in captions already shown by a page.
caption-cues.detail: A browser extension that transforms captions already exposed by the page: selectable emphasis rules for names, speaker changes, bracketed sound cues and manually saved words; keyboard replay of the last line. Non-goals: generating captions, scraping protected streams, diagnosing hearing loss, or claiming clinical personalization.
caption-cues.user: A viewer with high-frequency hearing loss who can follow captions but needs the most easily misheard names, words, and sound cues to stand out.
caption-cues.distinct: It improves comprehension within existing captions instead of offering another caption generator or a blanket font/theme switcher.
caption-cues.workaround: Replay a scene, increase all caption text, turn on every sound-description cue, or manually switch among poorly named subtitle options.

caption-fix-queue.title: Caption Fix Queue
caption-fix-queue.description: Review SRT and WebVTT caption findings locally before publishing.
caption-fix-queue.why: Find caption lines that need review before small video teams and community educators publish.
caption-fix-queue.detail: A local drag-and-drop SRT/VTT checker that flags improbable repeats, blank runs, unsupported characters, long reading-speed cues, inconsistent speaker names, and glossary mismatches; reviewers accept, dismiss, or repair each flag. Non-goals: generating captions, video hosting, or automatic factual correction.
caption-fix-queue.user: Small video teams and community educators who need to find the few caption defects that make an otherwise usable video inaccessible before publishing.
caption-fix-queue.distinct: The product is a review prioritizer for captions already made, not a thin transcription-model wrapper.
caption-fix-queue.workaround: Manually read the entire SRT, trust automatic transcription, or send all caption work to an expensive external vendor.

caption-placement-check.title: Caption Placement Check
caption-placement-check.description: Check captions against video frames before they hide speakers, slides, interpreters, or text.
caption-placement-check.why: Check whether captions cover important picture areas.
caption-placement-check.detail: A local drag-and-drop WebVTT/SRT plus video checker that samples frames, detects subtitle overlap with faces and dense text, and recommends safe zones or timed moves in a review list. Non-goals: transcription, video hosting, generative editing, or replacing a human accessibility review.
caption-placement-check.user: A solo educator, creator, or small organization publishing captioned video who needs to know when captions cover a speaker, slide, sign-language interpreter, or essential on-screen text.
caption-placement-check.distinct: It checks whether captions remain usable against the video rather than competing as another automatic caption generator.
caption-placement-check.workaround: Accept an editor’s default bottom-center position, scrub the whole video manually, or make a second edited version.

caption-salience.title: Caption Salience
caption-salience.description: Make uncertain caption words easier to notice in local SRT and WebVTT files.
caption-salience.why: Review captions for uncertain words, speakers, and terms on your computer.
caption-salience.detail: A local caption-player companion for user-provided WebVTT/SRT or microphone captions that marks low-confidence tokens, speaker changes, and user-defined terms with accessible emphasis presets. Non-goals: extracting captions from DRM services, diagnosing hearing loss, or cloud transcription by default.
caption-salience.user: People with partial or high-frequency hearing loss who use captions while retaining some audio and need uncertain or acoustically important words to stand out.
caption-salience.distinct: This is a caption presentation control surface, not another speech-to-text service.
caption-salience.workaround: Turn captions on, repeatedly rewind, increase system volume, or accept that speech and text do not line up with the parts that were hard to hear.

caption-style-checker.title: Caption Style Checker
caption-style-checker.description: Check caption speed, lines, speakers, markup, and placement before publishing.
caption-style-checker.why: Check caption files for lost meaning, speed, speaker cues, and placement before upload.
caption-style-checker.detail: A local drag-and-drop WebVTT/SRT/TTML linter that previews several accessible styles and reports lost semantics, overlong reading speed, missing speaker labels, and unsupported tags per selected platform profile. Non-goals: video hosting, automatic translation, or scraping/uploading platform media.
caption-style-checker.user: Independent video educators and accessibility reviewers who need to catch caption files that lose speaker cues, emphasis, placement notes, or readability before publication.
caption-style-checker.distinct: It verifies accessibility semantics at the publishing boundary instead of competing as a general subtitle editor.
caption-style-checker.workaround: Hand-inspect caption files, upload a private test video, or settle for the platform's basic caption conversion.

capture-clock-repair.title: Capture Clock Repair
capture-clock-repair.description: A local CLI that groups by camera/source, flags timezone and filename/date conflicts, proposes reversible XMP sidecar patches, and outputs a review CSV.…
capture-clock-repair.why: Make a conservative, reversible repair plan for missing and shifted photo capture times.
capture-clock-repair.detail: A local CLI that groups by camera/source, flags timezone and filename/date conflicts, proposes reversible XMP sidecar patches, and outputs a review CSV. Non-goals: face recognition, cloud photo storage, or claiming forensic certainty.
capture-clock-repair.user: Photographers consolidating photos from cameras, phones, messengers, and travel across time zones who need to repair missing or shifted capture times without overwriting trustworthy originals.
capture-clock-repair.distinct: It makes a reversible decision plan for mixed-source timestamps rather than being another EXIF tag editor.
capture-clock-repair.workaround: Run delicate ExifTool commands, use filesystem time as a proxy, correct files one by one, or accept a wrong timeline.

care-dose-board.title: Dose Witness
care-dose-board.description: Track each medication dose for an older relative on one private household board.
care-dose-board.why: Record given, skipped, or uncertain medication doses for an older relative on one household board.
care-dose-board.detail: A local-first PWA for one household: medication cards, scheduled doses, an explicit given/skipped/uncertain status, caregiver initials, offline printable handoff, and encrypted export/import between devices. Non-goals: interaction checking, prescription changes, pharmacy ordering, or clinical advice.
care-dose-board.user: Families coordinating an elderly relative’s medications who need every caregiver to see whether a particular dose was actually given.
care-dose-board.distinct: It records shared responsibility for an actual dose, not just a medication list or an alarm.
care-dose-board.workaround: Shared documents, calendar alarms, text messages, and verbal handoffs.

care-visit-brief.title: Care Visit Brief
care-visit-brief.description: Turn daily symptom notes into a printable visit brief for a clinician.
care-visit-brief.why: Prepare notes for a care visit.
care-visit-brief.detail: Offline PWA with one-tap symptom severity, optional trigger/medication tags, a missed-day-safe timeline, and a printable one-page visit brief. Non-goals: diagnosis, care advice, insurance billing, wearables, or clinician portals.
care-visit-brief.user: People with a new or fluctuating chronic condition who need to give a clinician an accurate, short history of symptoms, triggers, and what changed between appointments.
care-visit-brief.distinct: The output is a truthful appointment handoff built from intentionally tiny inputs, not another comprehensive symptom database.
care-visit-brief.workaround: Try a notes app, paper journal, spreadsheet, or a broad health tracker; reconstruct the story from memory at the visit.

caregiver-last-action.title: Caregiver Last Action
caregiver-last-action.description: See the latest baby-care action before the next handoff.
caregiver-last-action.why: See the last baby-care action for a clear caregiver handoff.
caregiver-last-action.detail: A locally synced PWA for two devices: one-tap event start/stop, prominent last-action board, correction history, and encrypted QR pairing. Non-goals: medical guidance, developmental predictions, cloud accounts, community features.
caregiver-last-action.user: Two or more baby caregivers handing off feed, sleep, medicine, and diaper timing who need one unambiguous answer to ‘what happened last, and when did it end?’
caregiver-last-action.distinct: A handoff instrument, not a full baby journal; the product deliberately privileges the next caregiver’s immediate question.
caregiver-last-action.workaround: Text a partner, check a shared app timeline, or infer from memory while tired.

catch-photo-log.title: Catch Photo Log
catch-photo-log.description: Offline PWA that reads optional photo EXIF, then prompts for species, rig, bait/lure, water conditions, line/anchor setup, and private location precision…
catch-photo-log.why: Log fishing catches, photos, and the setup that worked.
catch-photo-log.detail: Offline PWA that reads optional photo EXIF, then prompts for species, rig, bait/lure, water conditions, line/anchor setup, and private location precision; exports CSV/PDF. Non-goals: fish identification, bite prediction, social feed, public maps, or regulatory advice.
catch-photo-log.user: An angler who takes a catch photo and needs a fast, private record of where/when it happened plus the tackle and setup facts useful on the next trip.
catch-photo-log.distinct: It is a private learning log for rig/context, not another public catch map or AI fish-ID wrapper.
catch-photo-log.workaround: Camera roll plus notes, spreadsheet, a social catch app, or re-entering GPS/date manually.

change-checkpoint-manifest.title: Change Checkpoints
change-checkpoint-manifest.description: Record Git changes, check results, and rollback notes in local checkpoints.
change-checkpoint-manifest.why: Save a signed record of code and checks.
change-checkpoint-manifest.detail: A CLI that records a named checkpoint from git state, selected commands and their exit status, then writes a signed JSON/Markdown manifest with a verified restore command. Non-goals: source hosting, chat retention, or automatic rollback in production.
change-checkpoint-manifest.user: Teams accepting rapid agent or developer edits who need a durable checkpoint tying a workspace state, tests, and rollback instructions together.
change-checkpoint-manifest.distinct: It makes validation context portable across agents and editors instead of offering yet another undo button.
change-checkpoint-manifest.workaround: Use git commits/stashes, CI links, screenshots, and chat transcripts that are disconnected from one another.

change-diff-inbox.title: Change Diff Inbox
change-diff-inbox.description: A self-hostable watcher with CSS selectors, structured-data extraction, noise thresholds, and a compact semantic diff inbox. Non-goals: browser automation…
change-diff-inbox.why: Watch chosen parts of a page and review the changes that matter.
change-diff-inbox.detail: A self-hostable watcher with CSS selectors, structured-data extraction, noise thresholds, and a compact semantic diff inbox. Non-goals: browser automation farm, scraping bypass, or generic newsletter monitoring.
change-diff-inbox.user: Developers monitoring documentation, vendor status pages, or dashboards who need meaningful page changes rather than raw screenshots or email noise.
change-diff-inbox.distinct: It makes engineering-relevant, structured changes reviewable rather than merely reporting that pixels changed.
change-diff-inbox.workaround: Visualping/Distill checks, RSS, and manual provider-changelog reading.

checklist-evidence-binder.title: Proofbook
checklist-evidence-binder.description: Offline PWA with repeatable check cards, required evidence slots, completion/sign-off timestamps, overdue view, and a read-only evidence-bundle export.…
checklist-evidence-binder.detail: Offline PWA with repeatable check cards, required evidence slots, completion/sign-off timestamps, overdue view, and a read-only evidence-bundle export. Non-goals: regulated template library, certification advice, employee surveillance, or enterprise permissions.
checklist-evidence-binder.user: A tiny regulated or safety-conscious business that must repeat checks and show a client, inspector, or manager the supporting evidence later.
checklist-evidence-binder.distinct: It is an evidence-first checklist binder, not a generic task manager or an AI compliance wrapper.
checklist-evidence-binder.workaround: Recurring calendar tasks plus folders, spreadsheet checklists, chat reminders, and assembling proof only when asked.

chore-proof-calendar.title: Done Here
chore-proof-calendar.description: Track recurring household chores with notes and a compact calendar history.
chore-proof-calendar.why: Record recurring household chores with notes, photos, due dates, and a compact calendar history.
chore-proof-calendar.detail: Offline PWA with named recurring chores, a one-tap completion event, optional photo/note, last-done and next-due display, and ICS/PDF history export. Non-goals: points economies, child surveillance, chat, payroll-style fairness scoring, or cloud accounts.
chore-proof-calendar.user: Households that need recurring chores to have a visible completion history and a compact calendar record, not just an overdue task badge.
chore-proof-calendar.distinct: The core output is a calm proof-of-completion timeline, not task gamification or an all-purpose family platform.
chore-proof-calendar.workaround: Repeating reminders, whiteboards, shared task apps, arguments over memory, and checking off tasks without retaining meaningful history.

chore-receipt.title: Chore Receipt
chore-receipt.description: Record shared chores when they get done and see what is due next.
chore-receipt.why: Share chores and record when each is done.
chore-receipt.detail: Local-network/offline PWA with a household invite QR, unassigned shared chores, one-tap completion receipt, repeat-after option, and neutral history. Non-goals: gamified points, surveillance, parental controls, payroll, or chat.
chore-receipt.user: Roommates and families who do not care who does a recurring task, but need a trusted low-friction record that it was done and when it becomes due again.
chore-receipt.distinct: It minimizes blame and account overhead by recording the outcome, not turning chores into a gamified productivity platform.
chore-receipt.workaround: Assign chores to one person, message a group chat, use a whiteboard, or maintain a cloud task board.

chore-rulebook.title: Chore Rulebook
chore-rulebook.description: Rotate shared household chores, explain each assignment, and keep a local completion history.
chore-rulebook.why: Rotate recurring household chores, explain each assignment, and keep a local completion history.
chore-rulebook.detail: Offline shared-device PWA with named people, chores, interval/effort, rotation or fixed-owner rule, a 'why assigned' explanation, and a local history export. Non-goals: points, rewards, surveillance, chat, or account-based family social features.
chore-rulebook.user: A household sharing recurring chores who needs transparent assignment rules and a lightweight completion history, without gamifying domestic work or requiring every member to create an account.
chore-rulebook.distinct: Its value is explainable allocation rules and effort balance, not a prettier chore checklist or reward system.
chore-rulebook.workaround: Whiteboards, rotating verbal agreements, shared reminders, or a generic family task app whose assignments gradually become opaque.

ci-outage-witness.title: CI Outage Witness
ci-outage-witness.description: A GitHub CLI extension that snapshots run metadata, job transitions, available logs, runner diagnostics, GitHub status components, and retry lineage into one…
ci-outage-witness.why: Capture a redacted evidence bundle for one opaque GitHub Actions incident.
ci-outage-witness.detail: A GitHub CLI extension that snapshots run metadata, job transitions, available logs, runner diagnostics, GitHub status components, and retry lineage into one redacted incident bundle. Non-goals: replacing CI, auto-retrying jobs, or claiming root cause from insufficient evidence.
ci-outage-witness.user: Maintainers of critical GitHub Actions pipelines who need an evidence bundle that distinguishes a repository failure, runner failure, and platform degradation when logs are delayed or absent.
ci-outage-witness.distinct: It is an after-the-fact diagnostic receipt for a single CI incident, not an uptime monitor or CI dashboard.
ci-outage-witness.workaround: Refresh GitHub status, rerun jobs, inspect scattered runner journals, paste screenshots into incidents, or wait for a provider acknowledgement.

ci-provider-failover-drill.title: CI Provider Failover Drill
ci-provider-failover-drill.description: Prove one GitHub Actions job runs on an independent Docker runner.
ci-provider-failover-drill.why: Turn a CI job into a checked local command before an outage.
ci-provider-failover-drill.detail: CLI that converts an explicitly selected CI job into a pinned container command, verifies required files/secrets/network assumptions, and generates a local plus generic runner drill report. Non-goals: a CI service, a universal workflow converter, secrets storage, or automatic provider cutover.
ci-provider-failover-drill.user: A GitHub Actions-dependent maintainer who needs to know whether critical checks and releases can run elsewhere during a provider outage or migration.
ci-provider-failover-drill.distinct: It tests recoverability from CI dependency, rather than competing to host CI.
ci-provider-failover-drill.workaround: Wait out outages, keep undocumented Jenkins/CircleCI scripts, or manually rerun release commands on a laptop.

claim-ready-homebook.title: Claim-Ready Homebook
claim-ready-homebook.description: Offline PWA for item photos, value/date/serial/receipt, container and room location, plus an encrypted export that creates a readable PDF/CSV claim packet.…
claim-ready-homebook.why: Keep a private, portable record of belongings and export claim-ready evidence.
claim-ready-homebook.detail: Offline PWA for item photos, value/date/serial/receipt, container and room location, plus an encrypted export that creates a readable PDF/CSV claim packet. Non-goals: submitting claims, valuation guarantees, cloud backup, or insurance advice.
claim-ready-homebook.user: A renter or homeowner who wants an insurance-ready, portable record of belongings, serials, receipts, and storage locations before a stressful loss.
claim-ready-homebook.distinct: It produces an owner-controlled claim packet, not a hosted inventory catalogue or claims intermediary.
claim-ready-homebook.workaround: Phone photos, folders of receipts, a generic inventory app, and a rushed reconstruction after a loss.

claim-source-trail.title: Claim Source Trail
claim-source-trail.description: Connect each claim to its source, exact location, and why the evidence matters.
claim-source-trail.why: Record each claim, its source, exact location, and why the evidence matters.
claim-source-trail.detail: Privacy-first web app with a four-field claim card, DOI/URL/author citation metadata, page/section locator, counterevidence flag, and export to Markdown/CSV. Non-goals: scraping paywalled sources, automatic fact checking, essay generation, or a reference manager replacement.
claim-source-trail.user: Undergraduate humanities and social-science students learning digital research workflows who need to practice attaching a claim to an exact source location and a reason it supports the claim.
claim-source-trail.distinct: It teaches evidentiary reasoning at the claim level instead of becoming an AI essay writer or another bibliography manager.
claim-source-trail.workaround: Keep a document of copied quotes, use Zotero notes with loose annotations, or add citations only when drafting the final essay.

classroom-algorithm-cards.title: Classroom Algorithm Cards
classroom-algorithm-cards.description: A static generator for printable role cards, instruction cards, challenge cards, and a one-page facilitation guide for 20–40 minute sequencing/debugging games.…
classroom-algorithm-cards.why: Build and print a complete 20–40 minute unplugged sequencing and debugging activity for elementary classrooms.
classroom-algorithm-cards.detail: A static generator for printable role cards, instruction cards, challenge cards, and a one-page facilitation guide for 20–40 minute sequencing/debugging games. Non-goals: a full computer-science curriculum, student accounts, or AI-generated lesson plans.
classroom-algorithm-cards.user: An elementary teacher or volunteer teaching a one-off computing lesson who needs printable, collaborative, unplugged activities that make sequencing and debugging visible.
classroom-algorithm-cards.distinct: It serves the overlooked one-off, unplugged lesson with multiple-valid-answer facilitation rather than competing with a year-long coding platform.
classroom-algorithm-cards.workaround: Improvise a PB&J demo, download random worksheets, or use a screen-based coding game that may not fit a single classroom period.

clean-family-coop-room.title: Together Room
clean-family-coop-room.description: A two-device PWA with three original, turn-based co-op microgames, six-digit room codes, reconnect support, and no account. Non-goals: open chat, UGC…
clean-family-coop-room.why: Play three small remote co-op games with a child.
clean-family-coop-room.detail: A two-device PWA with three original, turn-based co-op microgames, six-digit room codes, reconnect support, and no account. Non-goals: open chat, UGC, matchmaking, payments by children.
clean-family-coop-room.user: A parent and child who want a 10-minute remote co-op activity without ads, logins, tracking, or an ongoing game-service commitment.
clean-family-coop-room.distinct: A deliberately bounded family activity room, not a social gaming platform.
clean-family-coop-room.workaround: Search app stores, tolerate ads/permissions, or persuade a technically skilled parent to host a game.

client-catalogue-request.title: Client Catalogue Request
client-catalogue-request.description: Turn repeat orders into clear quote requests from a private client catalogue.
client-catalogue-request.why: Share a private catalogue and receive quote requests without running an online store.
client-catalogue-request.detail: A shareable, passwordless client catalogue imported from CSV with request-for-quote basket, POA items, stock note, and CSV/PDF handoff to the seller. Non-goals: checkout, public marketplace SEO, fulfillment, or inventory accounting.
client-catalogue-request.user: A tiny B2B seller that already maintains a product list and needs approved clients to request a quote or reorder without a full ecommerce store.
client-catalogue-request.distinct: It is a request layer between a PDF catalogue and a commerce stack, not a Shopify clone.
client-catalogue-request.workaround: Accept email/WhatsApp orders, send a PDF catalogue, then re-key product lines into an invoice or ERP.

client-offboarding-kit.title: Closeout Kit
client-offboarding-kit.description: Build client handoff packets with asset owners, access checks, support dates, and acknowledgement.
client-offboarding-kit.why: Build a secure, portable client closeout packet without storing credentials.
client-offboarding-kit.detail: Local wizard for asset list, owners, links, transfer/revoke actions, support window, and client acknowledgement; exports a static HTML/PDF packet. Non-goals: password vault, Git host, CMS migration, remote access transfer, or file hosting.
client-offboarding-kit.user: A freelance developer or web studio finishing a client engagement who needs a clear, non-secret handoff of assets, ownership, access actions, and client acknowledgement.
client-offboarding-kit.distinct: It is a security-conscious closeout artifact that links to systems of record rather than pretending to replace them.
client-offboarding-kit.workaround: Email a zip and a loose document, send credentials in chat, maintain a checklist in a project manager, then answer follow-up access questions for months.

client-request-catalog.title: Client Request Catalog
client-request-catalog.description: Create private client catalogs that collect contact details, selected offers, and notes.
client-request-catalog.detail: A branded single-page catalog with client-specific visibility, fixed-price or Request a Quote buttons, stock note, and a request inbox exportable to CSV/PDF. Non-goals: payment processing, public marketplace discovery, warehouse management, and full ecommerce.
client-request-catalog.user: A tiny service or goods business that wants existing clients to request a priced service, POA item, or repeat order without a full ecommerce shop.
client-request-catalog.distinct: It sits before the quote, serving repeat clients without turning a service business into an ecommerce implementation project.
client-request-catalog.workaround: Take repeat requests by WhatsApp/email, circulate a PDF price list, or build a full online store that does not fit quote-first work.

client-request-quote-sheet.title: Request Sheet
client-request-quote-sheet.description: A static, shareable service/product request form with allowed items, quantities, free-text requirements, and a downloadable quote-draft CSV/PDF for the owner.…
client-request-quote-sheet.why: Build a focused service request sheet and turn repeat-client selections into a quote-ready draft.
client-request-quote-sheet.detail: A static, shareable service/product request form with allowed items, quantities, free-text requirements, and a downloadable quote-draft CSV/PDF for the owner. Non-goals: checkout, live inventory, client accounts, payment collection, CRM, or automatic quote acceptance.
client-request-quote-sheet.user: A service business with repeat clients who needs clients to request a priced or price-on-ask quote without exposing a full storefront or forcing a portal migration.
client-request-quote-sheet.distinct: It captures the request-to-quote handoff without turning into another retail site, CRM, or invoicing platform.
client-request-quote-sheet.workaround: Take requests by email or WhatsApp, copy line items into a quote, or build a storefront/API integration that is excessive for a few services or custom jobs.

clipboard-lan-bridge.title: Clipboard LAN Bridge
clipboard-lan-bridge.description: Move short text and links between your nearby devices without a cloud service.
clipboard-lan-bridge.why: Send clipboard text and files between nearby devices on your local network.
clipboard-lan-bridge.detail: Paired tray/mobile apps using local discovery and end-to-end encrypted transfer, with a one-tap send action, expiry, size/type allowlist, and visible receiving-device approval. Non-goals: clipboard surveillance, image/file sync, cloud relay, or clipboard history manager.
clipboard-lan-bridge.user: People moving short text and links between their own nearby phone, Linux, macOS, and Windows machines who want a deliberate, local-only handoff.
clipboard-lan-bridge.distinct: It is an intentional short-lived local handoff, not covert clipboard synchronization or another file-transfer suite.
clipboard-lan-bridge.workaround: Send a message to oneself, use a shared text file, cloud clipboard, QR codes, or heavyweight phone-link suites.

cloud-exit-evidence.title: Cloud Exit Evidence
cloud-exit-evidence.description: Check an offline cloud copy for missing, old, changed, or excluded files before trusting it.
cloud-exit-evidence.why: Compare a cloud export with an offline folder and find missing, old, changed, or excluded files.
cloud-exit-evidence.detail: A local CLI that compares a cloud-provider export/listing or sync manifest with an offline destination, classifies coverage by folder/type/date, records excluded paths, and emits an exit-readiness report. Non-goals: downloading from accounts, acting as a sync daemon, or bypassing OS permissions.
cloud-exit-evidence.user: People keeping a local fallback for cloud files who need an evidence-backed answer to whether their physical copy is complete enough to rely on.
cloud-exit-evidence.distinct: It produces a falsifiable exit-readiness report across existing tools rather than becoming yet another cloud-sync client.
cloud-exit-evidence.workaround: Use a NAS, external drive, rclone, or vendor sync app and assume that the local folder is complete.

code-echo.title: Code Echo
code-echo.description: Read selected code aloud one syntax chunk at a time.
code-echo.why: Read selected code aloud in short syntax chunks for developers and learners who lose their place.
code-echo.detail: A browser extension for documentation and code-review pages that reads a selected line/token with programmable punctuation and identifier pronunciation, shows one syntax chunk at a time, and offers a one-key replay history. Non-goals: IDE replacement, code generation, LLM explanations, or dyslexia diagnosis.
code-echo.user: Dyslexic developers and learners who need to inspect identifiers, punctuation-heavy syntax, and unfamiliar snippets without losing their place or relying on a generic screen reader mode.
code-echo.distinct: It is a deterministic, code-aware reading aid rather than a novelty font or an AI coding assistant.
code-echo.workaround: Turn on generic text-to-speech, magnify the IDE, copy snippets into another reader, or rely on autocomplete and spellcheck.

code-graph-explorer.title: Browser-based interactive call/dependency graph explorer for local codebases (Sourcetrail successor)
code-graph-explorer.description: Trace calls, imports, and source through unfamiliar codebases without uploading source.
code-graph-explorer.why: Trace functions, calls, imports, and source in a local code graph for unfamiliar codebases.
code-graph-explorer.detail: v1 is a static web app: drag a folder (File System Access API) or run `npx codegraph` to index; tree-sitter-wasm extracts definitions, calls and imports per file for TS/JS, Python and Go; the UI shows symbol search, a depth-limited focus graph (callers/callees/imports for the selected node), and the source with clickable references, plus JSON export of the index. Not in v1: cross-file type resolution beyond name+import heuristics, C/C++, editing, LSP integration, or hosted/collaborative indexes.
code-graph-explorer.user: Engineer onboarding to or refactoring an unfamiliar multi-file codebase who wants to open a folder and click through functions, callers, callees and module dependencies visually, without a server, IDE plugin or SaaS.
code-graph-explorer.distinct: Not a Sourcetrail rebuild in Qt nor an AI summarizer; it is the first web-native, multi-language, no-server implementation of the specific linked-graph interaction people keep naming.
code-graph-explorer.workaround: IDE 'find references' one hop at a time, Sourcetrail forks (desktop, limited languages), code2flow/Tach (module-level, single language), Sourcegraph (hosted/enterprise), asking an LLM.

code-listen-cursor.title: Code Listen Cursor
code-listen-cursor.description: Hear selected code with local speech that names symbols and indentation.
code-listen-cursor.why: Listen to selected code as intelligible structure.
code-listen-cursor.detail: A VS Code extension that reads selected code or the current line using language-aware punctuation rules, exposes cursor-follow and repeat shortcuts, and supports a personal pronunciation map. Non-goals: code generation, cloud voice cloning, IDE replacement, or code upload.
code-listen-cursor.user: A developer with reading fatigue, dyslexia, low vision, or an auditory workflow who needs an editor selection read aloud as intelligible code while maintaining cursor-level control.
code-listen-cursor.distinct: It solves listening to the current code structure and cursor context, not generic document narration.
code-listen-cursor.workaround: Use generic OS text-to-speech that pronounces punctuation poorly, copy code into another app, or only enlarge the entire editor.

code-path-lens.title: Code Path Lens
code-path-lens.description: An LSP/tree-sitter CLI and static viewer that starts at a symbol, follows a bounded call/type/data path, and emits a source-linked graph with explicit…
code-path-lens.why: Trace a bounded, source-linked path around one symbol.
code-path-lens.detail: An LSP/tree-sitter CLI and static viewer that starts at a symbol, follows a bounded call/type/data path, and emits a source-linked graph with explicit unresolved edges. Non-goals: code generation, cloud indexing, or natural-language answers.
code-path-lens.user: Developers reviewing an unfamiliar code path who need a small, deterministic view of the relevant callers, callees, types, and data boundaries instead of navigating an entire repository.
code-path-lens.distinct: It packages a bounded evidence-backed code journey, rather than becoming generic semantic search or an LLM explanation layer.
code-path-lens.workaround: Jump through IDE references, grep identifiers, open many tabs, or ask an agent for an unverified explanation.

collection-bulk-curator.title: Collection Batch Desk
collection-bulk-curator.description: Stage bulk catalog edits before export, then download patch and undo CSV files.
collection-bulk-curator.why: Stage collection edits, export a patch CSV, and undo them when needed.
collection-bulk-curator.detail: A local batch-review workspace that accepts a catalog export plus thumbnails, filters a subset, stages tag/location/condition edits, and outputs a patch CSV with undo manifest. Non-goals: collection hosting, image recognition, or direct account automation.
collection-bulk-curator.user: Collectors with hundreds of physical items who need to apply a reviewed tag, location, condition, or collection change to a chosen subset without losing context.
collection-bulk-curator.distinct: The product is a visual, reversible batch-change layer over existing catalogs rather than a replacement catalog.
collection-bulk-curator.workaround: Export to CSV, use spreadsheet fill-down, or open individual records repeatedly and hope a broad selection was correct.

collection-escape-hatch.title: Collection Escape Hatch
collection-escape-hatch.description: Compare Postman exports before moving to Bruno or Hoppscotch, then find missing requests, auth, scripts, and variables.
collection-escape-hatch.why: Compare API client exports before moving a team to another tool.
collection-escape-hatch.detail: A local CLI that reads Postman v2.1 plus one target export (initially Bruno/Hoppscotch), checks requests, folders, variables, auth, scripts, examples, and body sizes, then emits a Markdown/JSON migration report. Non-goals: another API client, cloud sync, or executing production requests.
collection-escape-hatch.user: An API developer moving a team off Postman who needs to prove that collections, environments, auth, scripts, and examples survived the move before changing the team's daily client.
collection-escape-hatch.distinct: It validates a migration between API clients instead of competing to be the API client.
collection-escape-hatch.workaround: Try several clients, import a copy, manually spot-check requests, or fall back to curl and hand-maintained files.

collection-import-reconciler.title: Catalog Reconciler
collection-import-reconciler.description: Local drag-and-drop CSV/JSON preflight that maps columns, normalizes identifiers, reports added/changed/missing/colliding rows, and emits a reviewed import…
collection-import-reconciler.why: Compare catalog files and export a reviewed import file.
collection-import-reconciler.detail: Local drag-and-drop CSV/JSON preflight that maps columns, normalizes identifiers, reports added/changed/missing/colliding rows, and emits a reviewed import file. Non-goals: hosting a collection database, scraping marketplaces, or automatic deletion.
collection-import-reconciler.user: Collectors moving a personal catalog between spreadsheets, Homebox, Koillection, or a new system who need to import without silently creating or renumbering records.
collection-import-reconciler.distinct: It is a reversible import-diff gate, not another collection catalog.
collection-import-reconciler.workaround: Back up a CSV, import into a copy, manually compare counts and identifiers, then repair records or retain the old spreadsheet.

collector-pressure-lab.title: Collector Pressure Lab
collector-pressure-lab.description: Test a local OpenTelemetry Collector to find when telemetry queues, slows, or drops.
collector-pressure-lab.why: Test a bounded telemetry sample against a local Collector and find where requests queue, slow, or drop.
collector-pressure-lab.detail: CLI loads a Collector config and a bounded OTLP/OTLP-like traffic sample, replays configurable bursts against a local collector, records queue/latency/drop behavior, and emits tuning hypotheses. Non-goals: an observability backend, a production traffic generator, or automatic config writes.
collector-pressure-lab.user: A self-hosting engineer running OpenTelemetry who needs to know whether a collector configuration will queue, shed, or overload under bursty telemetry before a production incident.
collector-pressure-lab.distinct: It is a configuration pressure experiment, not a telemetry store or another Grafana distribution.
collector-pressure-lab.workaround: Copy a Helm/Compose example, guess queue and batch settings, watch dashboards after deployment, then tune during overload.

color-context.title: Color Context
color-context.description: A local image/PDF viewer with sampled-color callouts, high-contrast texture overlays, user labels, and exportable annotated screenshots. Non-goals: diagnosing…
color-context.why: Add durable labels and high-contrast textures to color-only cues in local images and PDFs.
color-context.detail: A local image/PDF viewer with sampled-color callouts, high-contrast texture overlays, user labels, and exportable annotated screenshots. Non-goals: diagnosing color vision, recoloring third-party live UIs, or claiming universal color correction.
color-context.user: People with color-vision deficiency who need to understand charts, status indicators, and marked-up documents when color alone carries important meaning.
color-context.distinct: It helps users record and recover the meaning of a specific cue, rather than merely simulating color blindness or applying a global tint.
color-context.workaround: Use OS color filters, ask a colleague, take a screenshot into a simulator, or avoid interfaces that rely on color.

color-meaning-audit.title: Signal Check
color-meaning-audit.description: Check chart and dashboard signals that rely on color alone.
color-meaning-audit.why: Check charts and status dashboards for meaning carried only by color before you act.
color-meaning-audit.detail: Browser extension that samples the visible page/screenshot, detects repeated color-only legend/status distinctions, simulates selected deficiencies locally, and overlays a plain-language warning with label/shape/position alternatives. Non-goals: medical diagnosis, automatic recoloring of all sites, or design-system replacement.
color-meaning-audit.user: Color-blind knowledge workers who need to tell whether a chart, status dashboard, or UI uses color as the only carrier of meaning before they act on it.
color-meaning-audit.distinct: It audits meaning in the current task context for the affected reader, rather than applying another global color filter.
color-meaning-audit.workaround: Turn on an OS filter, ask a colleague, use glasses, or hope that contrast and labels are sufficient.

color-meaning-lens.title: Color Meaning Lens
color-meaning-lens.description: A browser extension that lets users map page colors to patterns and short labels (for example PASS, WARN, FAIL), with a per-site eyedropper and keyboard…
color-meaning-lens.why: Add patterns and short labels to colors on a web page.
color-meaning-lens.detail: A browser extension that lets users map page colors to patterns and short labels (for example PASS, WARN, FAIL), with a per-site eyedropper and keyboard toggle. Non-goals: medical color correction, claiming to identify every semantic color, altering source data, or image editing.
color-meaning-lens.user: A color-blind technical worker who needs status, diffs and charts to convey their meaning without depending on red, green or yellow alone.
color-meaning-lens.distinct: It overlays semantic redundancy at the point of use instead of applying a one-size-fits-all color filter.
color-meaning-lens.workaround: Use system color filters, memorize position, inspect raw text, buy color-filter glasses, or avoid visual QA work.

color-signal-lens.title: Color Signal Lens
color-signal-lens.description: Distinguish screenshot status colors with labels, patterns, or blue-orange colors.
color-signal-lens.why: Make screenshot status colors easier to tell apart with labels, patterns, and blue-orange colors.
color-signal-lens.detail: A desktop color-picker/lens that samples a selected region and overlays configurable patterns, labels, or blue/orange remapping for detected status colors. Non-goals: medical diagnosis, whole-screen color management, or modifying other apps' data.
color-signal-lens.user: People with color-vision differences who need software status, diffs, and charts to remain distinguishable without globally distorting their screen.
color-signal-lens.distinct: It makes color-only status legible at the moment of work, instead of applying a blunt global screen filter.
color-signal-lens.workaround: Enable broad OS filters, change app themes where available, or infer meaning from position and text.

color-status-labeler.title: Color Status Labeler
color-status-labeler.description: Label color-only dashboard statuses with readable words and patterns.
color-status-labeler.why: Add words and patterns to color-only dashboard and map statuses.
color-status-labeler.detail: Browser extension with a user-trained picker: sample two or more recurring status colors on a site, assign labels/patterns, and overlay a compact legend on matching elements. Non-goals: certifying WCAG compliance, changing server data, or image editing.
color-status-labeler.user: People with color-vision deficiency who need browser dashboards and maps to expose status without having to infer red/green or yellow/green meaning.
color-status-labeler.distinct: It augments the user's live interface with redundant meaning instead of merely simulating a color-vision condition for designers.
color-status-labeler.workaround: Use OS color filters, ask another person, zoom in, or avoid color-dependent interfaces.

comic-reference-sheet-board.title: Continuity Board
comic-reference-sheet-board.description: Local board with character reference slots, named attributes, prop checklist, 4–12 panel shot cards, and print/PDF export. Non-goals: image generation, style…
comic-reference-sheet-board.why: Plan character, prop, and shot continuity before you draw.
comic-reference-sheet-board.detail: Local board with character reference slots, named attributes, prop checklist, 4–12 panel shot cards, and print/PDF export. Non-goals: image generation, style imitation, public galleries, collaborative server.
comic-reference-sheet-board.user: Tabletop groups and hobby comic makers who need to keep character appearance, props, and panel intent consistent across a short story.
comic-reference-sheet-board.distinct: It addresses continuity before art is made, avoiding a thin generative-comic wrapper.
comic-reference-sheet-board.workaround: Keep folders of reference images, retype long prompts, or make a giant whiteboard and manually crop it.

compliance-evidence-pack.title: Deadline Packet
compliance-evidence-pack.description: Organize filing-period evidence gaps, files, and questions for accountant review.
compliance-evidence-pack.why: Gather filing evidence and export an accountant packet.
compliance-evidence-pack.detail: A local-first checklist builder with filing-period folders, attachments, a missing-evidence list, and a zipped/PDF index for accountant handoff. Non-goals: calculating tax, submitting returns, legal advice, OCR-as-truth, or government integrations.
compliance-evidence-pack.user: Freelancers earning cross-border income who need a calm, accountant-ready packet of invoices, receipts, deadline notes, and unanswered questions for a specific filing period.
compliance-evidence-pack.distinct: It organizes evidence and questions for human review rather than pretending to automate compliance or being a thin OCR/LLM wrapper.
compliance-evidence-pack.workaround: Keep spreadsheets, scattered scans, calendar reminders, and a WhatsApp/email conversation with an accountant; compile files hurriedly near deadlines.

comprehensible-input-log.title: Comprehensible Input Log
comprehensible-input-log.description: An offline log where users save a source, duration/pages, self-rate understanding, record up to three recurring unknown words, and get a trend view plus a…
comprehensible-input-log.why: Log language input that fits your current level.
comprehensible-input-log.detail: An offline log where users save a source, duration/pages, self-rate understanding, record up to three recurring unknown words, and get a trend view plus a simple next-source target. Non-goals: automatic transcription, language-level certification, and content hosting.
comprehensible-input-log.user: A language self-learner using books, podcasts, and videos who needs to choose material near their level and see whether input is becoming understandable without a gamified course.
comprehensible-input-log.distinct: It helps learners calibrate their own real-world input selection, not serve another closed library or pretend to assess fluency.
comprehensible-input-log.workaround: Guess from content labels, keep notes in a spreadsheet, rely on a platform’s opaque level, or consume material that is much too difficult.

concept-case-bridge.title: Concept Case Bridge
concept-case-bridge.description: Local case-card editor: author a compact scenario, tag the technical concept and domain signal, hide the decision, and review with a 'why not the alternative?'…
concept-case-bridge.why: Practice choosing technical concepts in realistic business cases. Private, local, and offline.
concept-case-bridge.detail: Local case-card editor: author a compact scenario, tag the technical concept and domain signal, hide the decision, and review with a 'why not the alternative?' field. Non-goals: domain-content marketplace, automatic case generation, or certification testing.
concept-case-bridge.user: Professionals learning both a technical stack and an unfamiliar business domain who need to practice choosing the right concept in a realistic domain case.
concept-case-bridge.distinct: The atomic unit is a transfer decision with a counterexample, not a flashcard or generated reading passage.
concept-case-bridge.workaround: Keep separate domain notes, wait for real work exposure, or ask an LLM to invent examples that are difficult to trust or revisit.

confidential-file-handoff.title: Confidential File Handoff
confidential-file-handoff.description: Create a protected ZIP and handoff sheet without uploading your files.
confidential-file-handoff.why: Pack sensitive files into an encrypted ZIP with clear recipient instructions.
confidential-file-handoff.detail: A local wizard that creates an encrypted ZIP, generates a recipient-specific plain-language handoff sheet and two-channel password instructions, and tracks a manual acknowledgement checklist. Non-goals: hosting files, claiming E2EE where it is absent, identity verification, or legal compliance certification.
confidential-file-handoff.user: People sending tax, medical, legal, or credential files to non-technical recipients who need a simple, truthful, one-time handoff procedure.
confidential-file-handoff.distinct: It improves the human handoff and truthful threat-model communication around existing transfer methods rather than operating a new file-sharing service.
confidential-file-handoff.workaround: Email attachments, Google Drive, a password in a second channel, Signal, Bitwarden Send, or improvised password-protected archives.

config-apply-witness.title: Apply Witness
config-apply-witness.description: A plugin-based CLI with one initial Supabase adapter that records a config input hash, fetches safe readback, and produces field-level applied/unknown/changed…
config-apply-witness.why: Verify declared Supabase settings and export a field-by-field receipt.
config-apply-witness.detail: A plugin-based CLI with one initial Supabase adapter that records a config input hash, fetches safe readback, and produces field-level applied/unknown/changed receipts. Non-goals: applying configuration, storing provider tokens, or becoming an IaC framework.
config-apply-witness.user: Small teams wiring hosted developer platforms who need proof that declared configuration fields were actually accepted and applied, rather than trusting a success message or a partial diff.
config-apply-witness.distinct: It validates the outcome of an apply, rather than adding another configuration authoring layer.
config-apply-witness.workaround: Read provider dashboards after each deploy, compare rendered CLI output manually, or discover a missing setting in production.

config-drift-timeline.title: Config Drift Timeline
config-drift-timeline.description: A local CLI that ingests redacted dotenv/YAML/JSON snapshots from named environments, normalizes values, and emits a time-ordered semantic drift report with an…
config-drift-timeline.why: Show when staging and production configuration drifted and who introduced it.
config-drift-timeline.detail: A local CLI that ingests redacted dotenv/YAML/JSON snapshots from named environments, normalizes values, and emits a time-ordered semantic drift report with an allowlist. Non-goals: secret management, deployment, or continuous remote polling.
config-drift-timeline.user: Platform engineers responsible for staging and production who need to explain when a meaningful configuration difference appeared and who introduced it.
config-drift-timeline.distinct: It supplies drift provenance and semantics, rather than another configuration store or a generic diff command.
config-drift-timeline.workaround: Compare checked-in files by hand, copy settings between repositories, or discover a missing environment variable during an incident.

config-rationale-guard.title: Config Rationale Guard
config-rationale-guard.description: A CLI that pairs strict JSON/YAML/TOML with adjacent rationale annotations, validates schema and annotation targets, and renders a PR diff of changed…
config-rationale-guard.why: Keep configuration decisions reviewable beside strict JSON, YAML, and TOML with an offline CLI.
config-rationale-guard.detail: A CLI that pairs strict JSON/YAML/TOML with adjacent rationale annotations, validates schema and annotation targets, and renders a PR diff of changed decisions. Non-goals: inventing a new configuration language, secret storage, or an LLM config writer.
config-rationale-guard.user: Maintainers of agent, CI, and developer-tool configuration who need configuration decisions and exceptions to remain visible, valid, and reviewable as settings files evolve.
config-rationale-guard.distinct: It governs the decision trail around configuration, not merely configuration syntax or generated docs.
config-rationale-guard.workaround: Add unofficial `_comment` keys, keep a disconnected README, or accept undocumented edits that reviewers cannot safely interpret.

context-cloze-vocab.title: Context Cloze
context-cloze-vocab.description: Paste a word list, add each sentence, and practise every missing word.
context-cloze-vocab.why: Practise vocabulary by filling gaps in sentences.
context-cloze-vocab.detail: Local-first web app that accepts a pasted word list and user-supplied example sentences, schedules typed cloze recall, and shows confusion pairs. Non-goals: dictionary licensing, AI chat tutoring, or a language course.
context-cloze-vocab.user: Independent language learners who know many word meanings but need to retrieve the right word in a sentence.
context-cloze-vocab.distinct: The unit of practice is productive sentence retrieval from a learner's own material, not another card deck or LLM wrapper.
context-cloze-vocab.workaround: Learners hand-write cloze cards, search for example sentences, or use generic generated exercises.

context-vocabulary-capture.title: Keep the Sentence
context-vocabulary-capture.description: Save phrases with source sentences to review later in Chromium.
context-vocabulary-capture.why: Save a phrase with its source sentence, then review it in your browser.
context-vocabulary-capture.detail: Browser extension saves selected phrase, surrounding two sentences, URL/title, language, and a learner-written gloss; a daily offline review asks for the phrase in that exact context. Non-goals: machine translation service, scraped content library, generated exercises, or account requirement.
context-vocabulary-capture.user: Language learners reading real web content who need to save a word together with its original context, meaning, and later retrieval cue without breaking reading flow.
context-vocabulary-capture.distinct: The twist is retaining the learner's own source sentence and retrieval history, rather than another translator, flashcard app, or AI-generated vocabulary feed.
context-vocabulary-capture.workaround: Use browser translate, copy words into Anki, take screenshots, or save an isolated dictionary definition.

cookbook-print-run.title: Dinner Binder
cookbook-print-run.description: Print a timed cooking packet from your own Markdown or JSON recipe files.
cookbook-print-run.why: Turn owned recipe files into a timed cooking packet with one recipe per printed sheet.
cookbook-print-run.detail: A static offline web app that accepts Markdown/JSON recipe files, selects recipes and servings, creates a paginated print packet with ingredient checkboxes, consolidated prep timeline, and optional allergen notes. Non-goals: web recipe import, nutrition calculation, shopping delivery, or hosted accounts.
cookbook-print-run.user: Households with digital recipe collections who need a clean, reliable printable cooking packet for a week, trip, or screen-free kitchen.
cookbook-print-run.distinct: The output is a dependable, selected cooking run—not a recipe database with a print button bolted on.
cookbook-print-run.workaround: Print browser pages with ads/layout noise, take screenshots, or manually format a document before a trip or meal plan.

cooldown-registry-proxy.title: Single-binary package registry proxy that enforces dependency cooldowns at the network layer
cooldown-registry-proxy.description: Block too-new npm, PyPI, and Cargo releases through one self-hosted registry proxy.
cooldown-registry-proxy.why: Block npm, PyPI, and Cargo packages until their release cooldown ends.
cooldown-registry-proxy.detail: v1 is one static binary (Go or Rust) exposing npm-registry, PyPI simple-index and Cargo sparse-index endpoints that proxy to upstream, cache tarballs, and refuse (HTTP 404/451 with a clear message) any version whose upstream publish time is younger than a configurable age unless listed in an exclusions file with expiry; it also refuses versions present in a periodically pulled OSV/GitHub-advisory malware list and logs every refusal. Ships a docker-compose example and a one-line client config snippet per package manager. It deliberately does not do auth/users, private package hosting, code scanning, a UI, or Maven/Go/Composer in v1 (Composer is the first follow-up given the open request).
cooldown-registry-proxy.user: Platform/security engineer at a 5-200 person team who must guarantee that no npm/PyPI/crates/Composer package younger than N days reaches any dev machine or CI runner, without trusting every developer's local package-manager config.
cooldown-registry-proxy.distinct: Every existing cooldown implementation is client-side or a per-machine interception proxy; this moves policy to a single org choke point that covers all ecosystems and all machines and can be run by a small team in five minutes, which neither Verdaccio, sakimori nor Artifactory offers.
cooldown-registry-proxy.workaround: Per-developer npmrc/pnpm/bun/uv settings (client-side, bypassable, absent for Composer/Go/Maven), Aikido safe-chain wrapper, StepSecurity PR check (npm-only, GitHub-only), or a full Artifactory/Nexus install.

couch-creatures.title: Couch Creatures
couch-creatures.description: A 2–4 player, 8–12 minute shared-screen rescue game: players use two-key keyboard lanes or scan a local QR to use one-thumb phone controls, herd shy creatures…
couch-creatures.detail: A 2–4 player, 8–12 minute shared-screen rescue game: players use two-key keyboard lanes or scan a local QR to use one-thumb phone controls, herd shy creatures through three changing habitats, and finish with a group postcard. Each run shuffles creature traits, weather, and route hazards. Non-goals: chat, user accounts, endless progression, ads, and competitive matchmaking.
couch-creatures.user: A parent, older sibling, or two children sharing one laptop/TV who want a gentle cooperative game that starts instantly and does not need accounts, purchases, or separate controllers.
couch-creatures.distinct: It is cooperative local play deliberately designed around the devices people already have, not a controller-dependent party-game collection.
couch-creatures.workaround: Install Steam games, buy or map controllers, sift through mobile free-to-play titles, or give up when coordination games become too chaotic.

couch-crew.title: Couch Crew
couch-crew.description: A one-screen, 3–6 player 18-minute heist: driver, lookout, hacker, loader, and dispatcher use two-button phone controls through three escalating missions.…
couch-crew.detail: A one-screen, 3–6 player 18-minute heist: driver, lookout, hacker, loader, and dispatcher use two-button phone controls through three escalating missions. Non-goals: a game platform, voice chat, accounts, or a user-generated-content SDK.
couch-crew.user: Friends in one room who want a 20-minute cooperative party game where every phone has a meaningful, different role.
couch-crew.distinct: The unit is an asymmetric cooperative run, not another trivia pack or a generic party-game portal.
couch-crew.workaround: Buy Jackbox packs, pass controllers around, or settle for competitive microgames with a TV browser.

couch-play-preflight.title: Room Ready
couch-play-preflight.description: Local-first web host plus phone join page that runs a capability check, reports mixed-controller compatibility, supports a no-install practice screen, and…
couch-play-preflight.why: Check every phone, controller and display before your group game starts.
couch-play-preflight.detail: Local-first web host plus phone join page that runs a capability check, reports mixed-controller compatibility, supports a no-install practice screen, and creates a printable/TV join card. Non-goals: game catalogue, matchmaking, accounts, or voice chat.
couch-play-preflight.user: Hosts of family, classroom, and team party games who need every phone/controller/display on the same local session before guests are waiting.
couch-play-preflight.distinct: It removes the social setup failure before a game begins rather than competing with party-game content.
couch-play-preflight.workaround: Open the game, circulate a QR code, troubleshoot each phone individually, and fall back to one familiar commercial party title.

creative-cartridge.title: Creative Cartridge
creative-cartridge.description: A downloadable PWA bundle with six tiny local activities (sound painting, shape stories, camera-free stop-motion cards, rhythm pads), a parent PIN for…
creative-cartridge.why: Make six offline activities for a child on a family computer.
creative-cartridge.detail: A downloadable PWA bundle with six tiny local activities (sound painting, shape stories, camera-free stop-motion cards, rhythm pads), a parent PIN for cartridge selection, and an offline health check. Non-goals: browser filtering, accounts, ads, analytics, or an app store.
creative-cartridge.user: Parents setting up an old computer for a 4–7-year-old who want a finite, offline creative play space rather than an internet feed.
creative-cartridge.distinct: It is a deliberately finite creative environment, not another educational-content platform or kids’ browser.
creative-cartridge.workaround: Install a child-focused Linux distribution, bookmark websites, download scattered games, or hand over a tablet with restricted browsing.

creative-tech-demo-recorder.title: Demo Loop
creative-tech-demo-recorder.description: Record a browser interaction, mark its response, and export a portfolio video and poster.
creative-tech-demo-recorder.why: Capture a portfolio-ready interaction demo in one short, local-first take.
creative-tech-demo-recorder.detail: Browser recorder that captures a selected tab plus optional mic, lets the maker mark one interaction beat and one caption, and exports a short WebM and poster image. Non-goals: cloud hosting, multi-track editing, analytics, AI video generation.
creative-tech-demo-recorder.user: Creative-technology students needing a credible 20–45 second proof-of-interaction for a portfolio, even when their prototype is fragile.
creative-tech-demo-recorder.distinct: It is tuned to showing an interaction’s cause and effect, not a generic screencast service.
creative-tech-demo-recorder.workaround: Screen-record many takes with OS tools, trim in a video editor, or show a fragile live link.

critical-alert-lane.title: Critical Alert Lane
critical-alert-lane.description: Keep critical Android reminders repeating until you snooze or acknowledge them.
critical-alert-lane.why: Keep critical reminders repeating until you acknowledge them on Android.
critical-alert-lane.detail: Android app with an on-device list of recurring critical reminders, repeat-until-acknowledged behavior, configurable quiet hours, and an export/import file. Non-goals: shared calendars, task management, cloud sync, or AI prioritization.
critical-alert-lane.user: An Android user overwhelmed by notifications who needs a tiny offline lane for a few reminders that repeat until explicitly handled.
critical-alert-lane.distinct: It deliberately refuses to be another calendar: acknowledgement reliability is the whole job.
critical-alert-lane.workaround: Turn on Do Not Disturb, add repeated calendar events, rely on default app reminders, or leave the phone on silent.

css-cause-map.title: CSS Cause Map
css-cause-map.description: Rank CSS rules and parent elements shaping a selected element’s size, position, or gap.
css-cause-map.why: Find the CSS rules and parent elements most likely causing an element's size, position, or unwanted gap.
css-cause-map.detail: Browser extension adds an element picker, captures computed layout plus ancestor constraints, ranks the CSS properties contributing to selected dimensions/offsets, and exports a scrubbed HTML/JSON report. Non-goals: editing CSS, visual regression testing, remote page inspection, or LLM diagnosis.
css-cause-map.user: A frontend developer diagnosing a live layout defect who needs a compact explanation of which CSS rule, ancestor, or dynamic DOM change caused an element's final size, offset, or gap.
css-cause-map.distinct: It produces deterministic causal evidence over a live DOM instead of adding a thin chat layer to DevTools.
css-cause-map.workaround: Toggle rules in DevTools, inspect computed styles/box model manually, add temporary outlines, and compare screenshots or DOM snapshots.

csv-import-cleanroom.title: CSV Import Cleanroom
csv-import-cleanroom.description: Prepare strict CSV imports locally, validate each row, explain rejects, and reuse mapping recipes.
csv-import-cleanroom.why: Clean a CSV with visible rules and explanations for rejected rows.
csv-import-cleanroom.detail: A local CSV tool with side-by-side source/target columns, named transforms for dates/currency/IDs, validation rules, rejected-row explanations, and a reusable JSON recipe. Non-goals: direct SaaS credentials, database ETL, automatic data inference, or LLM transformations.
csv-import-cleanroom.user: Operations staff and solo administrators preparing a messy spreadsheet for a strict SaaS import template who need a repeatable, auditable conversion without writing Python or damaging the original file.
csv-import-cleanroom.distinct: The primary artifact is a human-reviewable, repeatable import recipe—not a spreadsheet clone or broad ETL platform.
csv-import-cleanroom.workaround: Edit the only copy in Excel, use brittle formulas, ask an engineer for a script, or repeatedly upload trial files until an importer accepts them.

csv-import-contract.title: CSV Import Contract
csv-import-contract.description: Prepare a repeatable CSV import plan for migration teams.
csv-import-contract.why: Prepare a repeatable CSV import plan for a system migration.
csv-import-contract.detail: A local PWA that profiles CSV/XLSX parsing, proposes a column map and deterministic validations, lets users define transformations, and exports a JSON contract, cleaned preview, and human-readable handoff report. Non-goals: cloud ETL, database connectors, LLM data repair, or executing production imports.
csv-import-contract.user: Implementation consultants and operations staff preparing legacy CSV/XLSX exports for a system migration who need a repeatable, reviewable import contract rather than one-off spreadsheet cleanup.
csv-import-contract.distinct: It creates a portable agreement about parsing and mapping, rather than simply being another spreadsheet or generic data-cleaning interface.
csv-import-contract.workaround: Open files in Excel, use regex/find-replace, test ten rows in the target system, and keep undocumented per-client cleanup steps.

csv-keyed-diff.title: CSV Keyed Diff
csv-keyed-diff.description: Offline web app that accepts two CSVs, lets users choose one or more key columns, detects adds/removes/field changes, resolves duplicate keys, and exports a…
csv-keyed-diff.why: Export by business key and export an explainable, field-level change report.
csv-keyed-diff.detail: Offline web app that accepts two CSVs, lets users choose one or more key columns, detects adds/removes/field changes, resolves duplicate keys, and exports a filtered change report. Non-goals: database connectors, cleansing automation, or cloud storage.
csv-keyed-diff.user: An implementation or operations worker who must compare two customer CSV exports by business key and explain row/column changes without a database or spreadsheet gymnastics.
csv-keyed-diff.distinct: It is a reconciliation report generator, not a spreadsheet, generic diff viewer, or LLM data-cleaning wrapper.
csv-keyed-diff.workaround: VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, conditional formatting, text diff, Power Query, or ad hoc scripts.

cycle-block-animator.title: Cycle Blocks
cycle-block-animator.description: A browser timeline that imports numbered PNGs, defines cyclic blocks and offsets, previews the resulting loop, and exports a constrained sprite sheet plus…
cycle-block-animator.why: Block and budget-safe sprite sheets, locally in your browser.
cycle-block-animator.detail: A browser timeline that imports numbered PNGs, defines cyclic blocks and offsets, previews the resulting loop, and exports a constrained sprite sheet plus JSON. Non-goals: raster drawing, skeletal animation, asset marketplace, or game engine integration beyond generic metadata.
cycle-block-animator.user: 2D animators exporting game loops who need to repeat or offset a block of frames without copying hundreds of drawings, then ship a web-safe sprite sequence.
cycle-block-animator.distinct: It joins non-destructive cyclic timing to budget-aware export, not another general animation package.
cycle-block-animator.workaround: Duplicate frames in an art editor, manually build sprite sheets, and discover texture-size or loading failures in the engine.

cycle-legal-profile-check.title: Cycle Legal Check
cycle-legal-profile-check.description: Check planned GPX tracks for mapped bicycle, e-bike, and speed-pedelec access conflicts before riding.

cycle-legal-profile-check.workaround: Trust a generic bicycle profile, research restrictions separately, or discover an illegal segment while riding.

daily-safe-to-spend.title: Today Money

daily-safe-to-spend.user: People who budget manually and do not want bank sync, but need a trustworthy answer to what can be spent today after upcoming obligations.
daily-safe-to-spend.distinct: It answers one high-frequency decision conservatively, rather than cloning a full envelope-budget suite or wrapping an LLM around transactions.
daily-safe-to-spend.workaround: YNAB/Actual, Google Sheets, mentally subtracting bills, or downloading transactions into a larger finance package.

data-change-impact-card.title: Data Change Impact Card

data-engine-switchboard.why: Check a Pandas-to-Polars migration on local, bounded sample fixtures.

db-access-receipts.description: A local proxy/CLI with named allowlisted query templates, row/column caps, mandatory human confirmation for novel queries, and signed JSON audit receipts.…

db-access-receipts.detail: A local proxy/CLI with named allowlisted query templates, row/column caps, mandatory human confirmation for novel queries, and signed JSON audit receipts. Non-goals: natural-language-to-SQL, agent orchestration, or credential management platform.

delivery-acceptance-receipt.workaround: Email attachments, cloud-drive share links, screenshots, and a manually written invoice reminder.

deposit-deadline-bridge.description: Keep deposit and final balance dates intact when quotes become invoices.
