exam-deadline-map.why: Turn an exported flashcard deck into a realistic, time-capped revision calendar for your exam.
exam-deadline-map.detail: A local web app importing Anki CSV/review counts, an exam date, and daily minutes to produce a review/new-card calendar with overload warnings. Non-goals: replacing Anki, inventing card content, or proctoring.
exam-deadline-map.user: A self-directed learner with an exam date who needs a realistic day-by-day revision plan without turning every deck up to maximum intensity for months.
exam-deadline-map.distinct: It is a constrained revision calendar over existing recall history, not another flashcard client or generic to-do list.
exam-deadline-map.workaround: Raise Anki desired retention by hand, make a spreadsheet, or cram the backlog in the final week.

explain-then-check.title: Explain Then Check
explain-then-check.description: A local prompt runner: choose a concept, record or type an explanation under headings (what, why, failure case), mark missing pieces, and schedule only those…
explain-then-check.why: Practice explaining what, why, and failure cases—then retry only what you missed.
explain-then-check.detail: A local prompt runner: choose a concept, record or type an explanation under headings (what, why, failure case), mark missing pieces, and schedule only those missing pieces for another attempt. Non-goals: answer grading, generated lectures, or shared classrooms.
explain-then-check.user: Technical self-learners who can recognize flashcards but need short, deliberate practice explaining a concept, mechanism, and trade-off in their own words.
explain-then-check.distinct: It trains generative explanation without pretending an LLM can certify understanding.
explain-then-check.workaround: Write free-form notes, explain aloud with no record, make more cards, or rely on a chatbot to ask improvised questions.

explanation-lab.title: Explanation Lab
explanation-lab.description: Practise hard ideas with four prompts, then revisit them after seven days.
explanation-lab.why: Record explanations, examples, and counterexamples, then revisit the ones that need work.
explanation-lab.detail: Offline prompt cards for 'explain', 'draw a boundary', 'give an example', and 'find a counterexample', with dated self-recordings/text and a revisit queue. Non-goals: AI evaluation, plagiarism detection, grading, or a knowledge base.
explanation-lab.user: Students learning abstract STEM or programming concepts who need repeated practice explaining a mechanism, assumption, and counterexample in their own words.
explanation-lab.distinct: It makes explanation and counterexample generation a learner action, rather than outsourcing explanation to a chatbot.
explanation-lab.workaround: Keep free-form notes, rubber-duck to a friend, answer forum posts, or ask an LLM to explain the idea back.

export-receipt.title: Export Receipt
export-receipt.description: Check a service export before access ends and save a local receipt of files, dates, gaps, and warnings.
export-receipt.why: Record what was included in a data export.
export-receipt.detail: A local web app with pluggable archive inspectors for common ZIP/JSON/CSV exports; it inventories counts, attachments, date ranges, parse errors, hashes, and creates a signed HTML/JSON receipt with a retest checklist. Non-goals: credential login, scraping, automatic account migration, or hosted storage.
export-receipt.user: People leaving or backing up online services who need to know whether an export is complete, intelligible, and reusable before they lose access.
export-receipt.distinct: It verifies an export rather than promising impossible universal extraction or becoming another cloud backup product.
export-receipt.workaround: Request a ZIP, inspect a few files manually, store it unopened, or write a bespoke parser for a single service.

eye-comfort-profiles.title: Eye Comfort Profiles
eye-comfort-profiles.description: Save comfortable reading settings for each website in Chromium.
eye-comfort-profiles.why: Save readable font, spacing, line width, contrast, and focus-band settings for every website.
eye-comfort-profiles.detail: A browser extension with named per-site profiles, a live readability preview, font fallbacks, line-width/spacing controls, and an optional reading focus band. Non-goals: vision testing, blue-light medical claims, or forcing a single dyslexia font.
eye-comfort-profiles.user: People with astigmatism, low vision, or reading fatigue who need a repeatable per-site reading layout rather than re-adjusting browser zoom and display settings every session.
eye-comfort-profiles.distinct: It packages individualized, repeatable reading geometry rather than prescribing one font or replacing the browser reader mode.
eye-comfort-profiles.workaround: Change browser zoom, toggle a theme, use OS magnification, or accept unreadable line lengths and contrast on a site-by-site basis.

family-archive-check.title: Family Archive Check
family-archive-check.description: Check family photos and videos against an independent copy before handoff.
family-archive-check.why: Check whether family photos and videos have a readable second copy.
family-archive-check.detail: Desktop app that inventories chosen folders and mounted backup targets; checks counts, hashes sampled media, reads EXIF/date coverage, produces a portable recovery manifest and printable handoff sheet. Non-goals: hosting photos, facial recognition, or cloud sync.
family-archive-check.user: A household archivist who needs to know that a photo/video collection has complete, readable, independently recoverable copies before handing it to family.
family-archive-check.distinct: It is a recovery-readiness verifier and family handoff artifact, not another photo manager or backup engine.
family-archive-check.workaround: People juggle cloud albums, external drives, checksums, manual spreadsheets, and periodic exports.

family-digital-dossier.title: Family Digital Dossier
family-digital-dossier.description: Map essential family records without storing passwords or document contents.
family-digital-dossier.why: Record for family or an executor.
family-digital-dossier.detail: An offline encrypted template that records institutions, document locations, renewal dates, emergency contacts, and executor instructions; it generates a review checklist and a printable sealed-cover sheet. Non-goals: password storage, legal advice, will generation, or automated account access.
family-digital-dossier.user: Adults who want a trusted family member or executor to locate essential digital records during illness or death without handing over their entire password vault today.
family-digital-dossier.distinct: It fills the practical inventory-and-handoff gap around password managers instead of competing as one.
family-digital-dossier.workaround: Leave a paper notebook, share a master-password hint, maintain a private encrypted text file, or rely on a password manager's emergency feature alone.

family-handoff-calendar.title: Family Handoff Calendar
family-handoff-calendar.description: Offline PWA importing/exporting ICS, with named household members, handoff/pickup tags, a next-48-hours responsibility board, and a printable week sheet. Non-go
family-handoff-calendar.detail: Offline PWA importing/exporting ICS, with named household members, handoff/pickup tags, a next-48-hours responsibility board, and a printable week sheet. Non-goals: messaging, location tracking, school integrations, accounts, or automatic calendar hosting.
family-handoff-calendar.user: Two-parent households juggling school, work, pickups, and activities who need to see who is responsible at each handoff without committing their family schedule to Google or Apple.
family-handoff-calendar.distinct: It layers responsibility and handoffs on top of portable calendar files instead of replacing calendar infrastructure.
family-handoff-calendar.workaround: Shared Google/Apple calendars, group chat, a wall calendar, or generic task apps.

family-meal-lanes.title: Family Meal Lanes
family-meal-lanes.description: Plan individual and shared meals for each person on one private weekly board.
family-meal-lanes.why: Plan family meals in a shared weekly board that works offline.
family-meal-lanes.detail: Offline shared-device PWA with a seven-day grid, named local lanes, shared-meal links, prep labels, printable view, and an exportable JSON file. Non-goals: recipes, grocery ordering, nutrition scoring, accounts, or real-time cloud collaboration.
family-meal-lanes.user: A household planning a week of meals for different people who needs to see who a meal is for, what is shared, and what prep overlaps without signing everyone into a meal service.
family-meal-lanes.distinct: The distinctive primitive is person and shared-meal lanes, not another recipe catalog.
family-meal-lanes.workaround: Put names in meal titles, maintain separate calendars, message family members, or use multiple overlapping meal plans.

family-weekboard.title: Weekboard
family-weekboard.description: Plan a family week without a shared cloud account.
family-weekboard.why: Plan a family week and export it to calendars.
family-weekboard.detail: An offline PWA weekly board with people/lane colors, recurring events, printable view, and standard ICS import/export; sharing is an explicit encrypted file/QR handoff. Non-goals: email invitations, cloud sync, chat, contacts, or a CalDAV server.
family-weekboard.user: Cross-platform families who need a simple shared weekly view without committing their household schedule to Google, Apple, or a new subscription account.
family-weekboard.distinct: It is a deliberately constrained family-facing calendar surface, not another hosted calendar provider.
family-weekboard.workaround: Google Calendar, Apple Family Sharing, paper calendars, or testing/self-hosting several CalDAV products.

feed-later-bridge.title: Feed Later Bridge
feed-later-bridge.description: A local-first web/extension pair that imports a user-designated RSS/Atom saved-items feed, deduplicates entries, lets the user mark/annotate a compact queue…
feed-later-bridge.why: Turn an RSS or Atom saved-items feed into a private, finishable, exportable reading queue.
feed-later-bridge.detail: A local-first web/extension pair that imports a user-designated RSS/Atom saved-items feed, deduplicates entries, lets the user mark/annotate a compact queue, and exports OPML/Markdown/JSON. Non-goals: article scraping at scale, social feeds, recommendations, or hosted accounts.
feed-later-bridge.user: RSS readers who mark articles for later but do not want a separate proprietary read-later silo or a manual copy/paste routine.
feed-later-bridge.distinct: It is a standards-based handoff bridge, not a new reader or attention-maximizing content feed.
feed-later-bridge.workaround: Use Instapaper/Pocket plus a reader, manually save links again, depend on a service-specific integration, or abandon one workflow.

field-time-invoice-proof.title: Work Receipt
field-time-invoice-proof.description: Record billable work sessions and create a self-reported weekly client receipt.
field-time-invoice-proof.why: Log freelance work and create a weekly client receipt.
field-time-invoice-proof.detail: A local PWA with start/stop/manual sessions, project/outcome notes, optional links to commits/files, and a branded weekly PDF receipt for attachment to an invoice. Non-goals: employee surveillance, keystroke capture, screenshots, payroll, automatic activity inference, or invoicing.
field-time-invoice-proof.user: Freelancers billing for modern knowledge work who need an honest, privacy-preserving client-readable record of what was done and when, including AI-assisted work.
field-time-invoice-proof.distinct: It creates a humane invoice attachment for outcome-based explanation, not another timer or invasive monitoring product.
field-time-invoice-proof.workaround: Run a timer, estimate after the fact, infer time from Git branches, or produce a manually written status update alongside an invoice.

file-change-space-check.title: File Change Space Check
file-change-space-check.description: Desktop CLI that scans source/destination metadata, lets users select a conflict policy, estimates net bytes and temporary headroom, and emits a deterministic…
file-change-space-check.why: Check whether a local copy will fit and resolve conflicts before moving it.
file-change-space-check.detail: Desktop CLI that scans source/destination metadata, lets users select a conflict policy, estimates net bytes and temporary headroom, and emits a deterministic action manifest. Non-goals: file transfer UI, cleanup recommendations, or deleting anything.
file-change-space-check.user: Someone copying, extracting, or reorganizing a large local folder who needs a correct free-space and conflict estimate before starting a long operation.
file-change-space-check.distinct: It plans a file operation under explicit policies instead of becoming a file manager or cleaner.
file-change-space-check.workaround: Estimate folder size in a file manager, start copying, then cancel or manually clear space when conflicts and duplication change the required capacity.

finish-one-pantry.title: Finish One Pantry
finish-one-pantry.description: Offline mobile PWA with a pinned shelf of recurring packages and one Finish button that decrements a simple reserve count and adds an item to a local list at…
finish-one-pantry.why: List pantry packages to replace when you finish them.
finish-one-pantry.detail: Offline mobile PWA with a pinned shelf of recurring packages and one Finish button that decrements a simple reserve count and adds an item to a local list at the chosen threshold. Non-goals: barcode database, receipt OCR, expiry tracking, recipes, or household accounting.
finish-one-pantry.user: A household that buys repeat packages (milk, rice, detergent) and wants a low-effort way to know when a replacement belongs on the list.
finish-one-pantry.distinct: It deliberately rejects exhaustive pantry inventory in favor of a single sustainable replenishment signal.
finish-one-pantry.workaround: Maintain a detailed inventory briefly, write a separate shopping note when something runs out, or discover the shortage during meal preparation.

finite-foundry.title: Finite Foundry
finite-foundry.description: Plan six factory routes in five-minute shifts and finish a complete free campaign.
finite-foundry.why: Plan factory routes and finish a six-level campaign.
finite-foundry.detail: A 90-minute factory campaign in six chapters. Set a 5-minute production plan, leave it running, return to solve one new routing constraint, then dismantle the final machine for a credits ending. Each run randomizes available contracts. Non-goals: prestige, real-time offline accrual, energy timers, ads, or in-game purchases.
finite-foundry.user: Incremental-game players who enjoy optimizing a production loop but want to finish a satisfying campaign in one or two evenings without microtransactions or perpetual prestige.
finite-foundry.distinct: It makes idle a deliberate planning cadence with a finale, directly answering the cited complaints instead of adding a nicer cash shop.
finite-foundry.workaround: Play free clickers that demand constant checks, prestige early, and sell boosts, or abandon the game once the next upgrade loses meaning.

firebase-environment-doctor.title: Firebase Environment Doctor
firebase-environment-doctor.description: Check Firebase projects before you deploy.
firebase-environment-doctor.why: Check the Firebase project, sign-in, emulators, and rules files before a deploy.
firebase-environment-doctor.detail: A local CLI that reads Firebase project files and runs explicit read-only checks to output a shareable diagnostic card with project identity, emulator/cloud targets, rules hash, auth status, and suggested next checks. Non-goals: database browsing, credential repair, or deploying configuration.
firebase-environment-doctor.user: Firebase developers who work from the terminal and need a preflight diagnosis of active project, credentials, emulator state, rules, and CLI reachability before debugging application data.
firebase-environment-doctor.distinct: It validates the development environment before debugging, rather than becoming another Firestore UI or Firebase replacement.
firebase-environment-doctor.workaround: Switch among Firebase Console, firebase CLI diagnostics, shell environment inspection, and emulator logs; often discover the wrong project only after a risky command.

first-move-friends.title: First Move Friends
first-move-friends.description: A turn-based 4x4 lantern-placement duel. An invite link seats two players; the first three moves animate one legal objective at a time, then the board opens ful
first-move-friends.detail: A turn-based 4x4 lantern-placement duel. An invite link seats two players; the first three moves animate one legal objective at a time, then the board opens fully. A 6-10 minute run differs through one public goal card and a shuffled tile order. Non-goals: global matchmaking, chat, ratings, or large game library.
first-move-friends.user: Casual pairs who want an invitation-only browser tile game they can understand by playing the first turn, with no sign-up, ads, or rulebook wall.
first-move-friends.distinct: The product is the embedded first-match tutorial and quick rematch loop, not a general board-game catalog.
first-move-friends.workaround: Read a rules page, watch a tutorial, join a complex board-game site, or abandon the invitation after one confusing turn.

five-minute-heist.title: Five-Minute Heist
five-minute-heist.description: Plan five moves, dodge looping guards, and steal today’s museum piece.
five-minute-heist.detail: One daily 5x5 museum heist: plan a sequence of five moves around deterministic guard loops, then watch it execute. A run differs by daily gallery layout, guard pattern, and optional loot constraint. Finish produces a spoiler-free path glyph. Non-goals: infinite levels, real-time action, hints for sale, or login streaks.
five-minute-heist.user: Solo browser players looking for a polished daily break that starts instantly, takes about five minutes, and has a score worth sharing without becoming another word-game clone.
five-minute-heist.distinct: It transfers the daily five-minute promise to a plan-then-watch stealth puzzle, rather than cloning word guessing or manufacturing streak anxiety.
five-minute-heist.workaround: Play Wordle-like games, social feeds, or a mobile game during a break; share only a text score afterward.

flag-removal-map.title: Flag Removal Map
flag-removal-map.description: Review completed feature flags with provider, usage, and code evidence.
flag-removal-map.why: Map completed feature flags before removing them.
flag-removal-map.detail: CLI accepts a provider export and repositories, finds SDK/config references, records optional evaluation counts from a local export, classifies a flag as keep/remove/review, and creates a Markdown removal plan. Non-goals: serving flags, changing code automatically, or collecting user analytics.
flag-removal-map.user: A lean engineering team that has shipped a feature flag and now needs a safe, evidence-based checklist to remove the flag and every code/config reference once the rollout is complete.
flag-removal-map.distinct: It connects deployment evidence to code cleanup; it is not a feature-flag service.
flag-removal-map.workaround: Search the repository manually, rely on a flag provider's creation date, file a cleanup ticket, and hope no SDK/config reference remains.

flag-stale-guard.title: Flag Stale Guard
flag-stale-guard.description: Find expired release flags and block removal until source references are gone.
flag-stale-guard.why: Find old feature flags, assign owners, and prepare their removal.
flag-stale-guard.detail: GitHub Action and local CLI that inventories configured flags, finds call sites, requires owner/expiry metadata, opens a removal checklist after expiry, and blocks deletion when a flag still has live references. Non-goals: remote flag evaluation, targeting, analytics, or SDK replacement.
flag-stale-guard.user: A maintainer of a small application who uses release flags and kill switches but needs to know which flags have become permanent, dead, or unsafe to remove.
flag-stale-guard.distinct: It cleans up the lifecycle around any flag provider instead of becoming another flag-delivery service.
flag-stale-guard.workaround: Spreadsheets, TODO comments, manual searches, or expensive feature-management products.

flaky-test-casefile.title: Flaky Test Casefile
flaky-test-casefile.description: Playwright reporter that packages retries, normalizes timing noise, clusters matching failures, and renders a static casefile. Non-goals: a cloud test runner…
flaky-test-casefile.why: Group flaky Playwright retries and find the first divergence.
flaky-test-casefile.detail: Playwright reporter that packages retries, normalizes timing noise, clusters matching failures, and renders a static casefile. Non-goals: a cloud test runner, visual-regression service, or autonomous test repair.
flaky-test-casefile.user: Teams using Playwright in CI who need to turn intermittent failures into compact, comparable evidence instead of a pile of reruns and screenshots.
flaky-test-casefile.distinct: It organizes existing evidence around an intermittent failure signature rather than replacing Playwright or adding AI-generated guesses.
flaky-test-casefile.workaround: Rerun CI, upload traces/videos, and manually compare screenshots and logs across runs.

flex-meal-templates.title: Flex Meal Templates
flex-meal-templates.description: Adjust repeat-meal portions and compare each log with saved nutrition ranges.
flex-meal-templates.why: Save flexible meal templates with serving sizes, swaps, and nutrition bands.
flex-meal-templates.detail: Offline template editor for 10–30 recurring meals: base ingredients, adjustable serving multiplier, substitutions, per-meal calorie/macro bands, and CSV export. Non-goals: food search, barcode lookup, recipe scraping, or meal-plan generation.
flex-meal-templates.user: A person reusing meals while changing portion sizes who needs each meal template to remain editable at logging time and fit a meal-specific nutrition budget.
flex-meal-templates.distinct: It solves the template-versus-real-portion gap instead of attempting to replace a full nutrition database.
flex-meal-templates.workaround: Duplicate a meal, edit ingredients from scratch, or maintain a separate spreadsheet of portions and macro targets.

flex-practice-queue.title: Flex Practice Queue
flex-practice-queue.description: Build short flashcard rounds without changing your flashcard schedule.
flex-practice-queue.why: Choose the next item in a practice list.
flex-practice-queue.detail: Offline queue builder that imports a CSV of prompts, lets users tag 'warm-up', 'weak', and 'today', runs timed mixed rounds, and never changes source-card scheduling. Non-goals: SRS replacement, shared decks, or automatic difficulty inference.
flex-practice-queue.user: Learners whose available study time arrives in short, irregular windows and who need to choose useful practice without breaking a formal scheduler.
flex-practice-queue.distinct: It adds an intentional rehearsal lane alongside scheduling rather than competing to be another flashcard scheduler.
flex-practice-queue.workaround: Reset cards, make duplicate decks, ignore a scheduler, or choose practice at random.

flipbook-trace.title: Flipbook Trace
flipbook-trace.description: Turn a short video into a numbered PNG pack and printable PDF trace sheet.
flipbook-trace.why: Choose a local video, pick frames, and export numbered PNGs or a printable tracing sheet.
flipbook-trace.detail: Local browser app: choose a local video, trim 1–5 seconds, select FPS and threshold/edge preview, export numbered PNGs and a PDF contact sheet. Non-goals: cloud video hosting, style-transfer AI, publishing platform.
flipbook-trace.user: Short-form video creators who want to turn their own clip into a hand-drawn flipbook study without uploading it to an editing service.
flipbook-trace.distinct: It prepares a traceable animation exercise; it is not a video editor or a generative-video wrapper.
flipbook-trace.workaround: Manually extract video frames, import them as layers in Krita/Procreate, then trace or print them.

floorplan-text-dsl.title: Text-to-floor-plan: a Markdown-like DSL that renders scaled SVG/PDF blueprints
floorplan-text-dsl.description: Turn floor-plan text into scaled SVG, PDF, or PNG drawings.
floorplan-text-dsl.why: Draw a scaled floor plan from text and export it as SVG, PDF, or PNG.
floorplan-text-dsl.detail: Static split-pane editor: left a small DSL (units, scale, wall from/to thickness, door/window on wall at offset, label, dimension line), right live SVG; export SVG/PDF at scale (e.g. 1:50 on A3) and PNG; share via URL hash or file. No 3D, no furniture catalog, no DXF import, no collaboration.
floorplan-text-dsl.user: DIYers, renters, small landlords and engineers who want a scaled 2D floor plan or simple blueprint by typing wall/door/window coordinates, not by fighting CAD UIs; job: produce a clean, dimensioned SVG/PDF.
floorplan-text-dsl.distinct: Domain-specific text language for floor plans is a genuine gap between generic diagram DSLs and GUI CAD.
floorplan-text-dsl.workaround: Hand drafting; abusing OpenSCAD/Pikchr/Asymptote; heavyweight FreeCAD/LibreCAD; paid Chief Architect/Bricscad.

focus-flow-map.title: Focus Flow Map
focus-flow-map.description: Record where Tab moves and export a local focus route report.
focus-flow-map.why: Record where Tab moves through a webpage, review jumps and loops, and export a local issue report.
focus-flow-map.detail: Browser extension that records a user-initiated tab/shift-tab session locally, renders a numbered focus map with element labels and viewport jumps, and exports a reproducible issue packet. Non-goals: automated crawling, a general test suite, or collecting pages remotely.
focus-flow-map.user: Keyboard-only, RSI-affected users and the teams supporting them who need to see whether a website's tab order reaches usable controls without hidden jumps or traps.
focus-flow-map.distinct: It turns the lived keyboard route into evidence, rather than producing another static rule score.
focus-flow-map.workaround: Tab through a page by hand, use browser devtools, report the problem with screenshots, or switch to a mouse/assistant.

focus-lens.title: Focus Lens
focus-lens.description: Keep keyboard focus visible in dense web apps with per-site view controls and named waypoints.
focus-lens.why: Make keyboard focus clearer and save reading settings for each site.
focus-lens.detail: A browser extension with large high-contrast focus indicator, temporary reading lane, per-site zoom/contrast presets, user-defined named focus waypoints, and an exportable shortcut cheat sheet. Non-goals: screen-reader replacement, computer-vision surveillance, AI interpretation, or bypassing site security.
focus-lens.user: Knowledge workers with low vision who use browser-heavy enterprise apps and need predictable magnification, focus visibility, and keyboard orientation on sites that provide poor accessibility support.
focus-lens.distinct: It improves orientation in hostile web apps through deterministic user controls, not an unreliable visual-AI assistant.
focus-lens.workaround: Use OS magnification, browser zoom, screen readers, voice control, or ask an employer for accommodations; each breaks down on dense web UIs or inconsistent focus order.

focus-resume-card.title: Focus Resume Card
focus-resume-card.description: A local browser extension that makes a one-card checkpoint containing current URL, selected text, optional screenshot, elapsed focus block, and a required five-
focus-resume-card.detail: A local browser extension that makes a one-card checkpoint containing current URL, selected text, optional screenshot, elapsed focus block, and a required five-to-twelve-word next action; reopening presents only that card before tabs. Non-goals: task management, time surveillance, gamification, or LLM-generated plans.
focus-resume-card.user: Developers with ADHD who need to resume an interrupted task from a small, concrete next action instead of rebuilding context from tabs, chat, and an open-ended task list.
focus-resume-card.distinct: It is an interruption-recovery primitive, not another backlog, Pomodoro timer, or AI productivity wrapper.
focus-resume-card.workaround: Keep many tabs open, write generic to-do items, re-read commits and chat after an interruption, or overbuild a personal planning system.

focus-study-sprint.title: Focus Study Sprint
focus-study-sprint.description: Practice recalling answers in short study sessions.
focus-study-sprint.why: Practise your own questions in a timed session and review what you missed.
focus-study-sprint.detail: A PWA where users paste 5–30 prompts, choose 5/10/20 minutes, answer in a distraction-free loop, and receive a private session recap with no streak or leaderboard. Non-goals: generated lessons, social feeds, and habit nudges.
focus-study-sprint.user: A student or self-learner who wants short, calm, active-recall sessions without streaks, rewards, feeds, or an AI content firehose.
focus-study-sprint.distinct: The product constraint is intentional absence of engagement loops and generated content, not a thinner Duolingo clone.
focus-study-sprint.workaround: Use a Pomodoro timer beside Anki/Quizlet, dismiss reward screens, or abandon apps that optimize streaks.

folder-recipe-switcher.title: Folder Recipe
folder-recipe-switcher.description: Save photo editor profiles beside folders and export local import checklists.
folder-recipe-switcher.why: Save editor profiles beside photo folders, check inherited recipe files, and export an import checklist.
folder-recipe-switcher.detail: A local utility that writes a versioned `.photo-recipe.json` beside a folder, records camera/source heuristics and recommended editor profile/style, previews inherited rules, and exports an import checklist. Non-goals: changing RAW pixels, replacing an editor, or cloud asset management.
folder-recipe-switcher.user: Photographers moving through mixed shoots, camera sources, and archive folders who need an inspectable default processing recipe per folder without accidentally applying it across unrelated work.
folder-recipe-switcher.distinct: It makes folder intent portable and auditable instead of hiding another editor's state in a catalogue.
folder-recipe-switcher.workaround: Apply a profile repeatedly, keep notes in folders, use filename conventions, or accidentally inherit settings from the previous shoot.

forge-sync.title: Continuous org-wide GitHub → Forgejo/Codeberg/GitLab mirror with issue and PR metadata sync
forge-sync.description: Mirror GitHub organizations to another forge with issues, pull-request history, and a JSON archive.
forge-sync.why: Mirror a GitHub organization to Forgejo, Codeberg, or GitLab and keep a local JSON archive.
forge-sync.detail: v1: single binary/Docker with config `source: github org X → target: forgejo instance Y`; polls for new repos, creates them on the target, keeps branches/tags mirrored, and syncs issues, labels, milestones and PR discussions one-way (GitHub → forge) with idempotent ID mapping and an audit log; exports the same data to a git-tracked JSON archive. Not in v1: bidirectional review relay (experimental flag only), CI translation, wikis/projects, or GitLab as a source.
forge-sync.user: Maintainer or small org hedging against GitHub lock-in who wants every repo in their GitHub org (including newly created ones) mirrored to a self-hosted forge, with issues/PR comments carried along and, during migration, contributions flowing back.
forge-sync.distinct: Existing tools are either one-shot migrators or code-only backups; continuous org-wide discovery plus issue/PR metadata in a forge-neutral archive is the exact missing piece each thread names.
forge-sync.workaround: Per-repo Forgejo pull mirrors (manual, code only), gickup (backup-oriented), one-shot migration importers, multiple git remotes by hand.

freelancer-agent-context.title: Client Context Firewall
freelancer-agent-context.description: Keep each client’s sources, rules, and delivery records in a separate local workspace.
freelancer-agent-context.why: Keep each client’s sources, rules, and delivery record in one local workspace.
freelancer-agent-context.detail: Desktop companion that launches named client workspaces with scoped connectors, encrypted local context bundles, redaction rules, and a deliverable provenance export. Non-goals: employee surveillance, hosted source-code storage, or a new IDE.
freelancer-agent-context.user: Freelance developers juggling client engagements with AI tools who need to preserve their own voice while preventing context, accounts, and deliverables from bleeding between clients.
freelancer-agent-context.distinct: It protects the working boundary of a client engagement rather than being a generic AI chat organizer.
freelancer-agent-context.workaround: Separate browser profiles, manually swap API keys, keep notes in disconnected folders, and hope the active chat has the right client context.

freeze-capsule.title: Freeze Capsule
freeze-capsule.description: Capture Linux freeze clues before a reboot erases them.
freeze-capsule.why: Package a project so it can be reopened later.
freeze-capsule.detail: Deb/RPM-installable watchdog that snapshots bounded system/graphics/process context to an encrypted local capsule on watchdog timeout or a user hotkey, then renders a redacted bug-report bundle. Non-goals: remote support, kernel modification, or automated bug filing.
freeze-capsule.user: Desktop Linux users who need a useful evidence bundle after a freeze, before they reboot and lose the clues needed to identify a graphics, kernel, or app trigger.
freeze-capsule.distinct: It turns fragmented post-crash commands into an automatically preserved local evidence capsule, not another crash-reporting SaaS.
freeze-capsule.workaround: Users reboot, later copy journalctl output, set up SSH/netconsole only after learning the hard way, or post incomplete logs.

freezer-life-ledger.title: Freezer Life Ledger
freezer-life-ledger.description: Barcode/name entry, one-tap Open/Freeze/Finish actions, best-before date, location, and a ‘use next’ list. Non-goals: retailer integrations, recipe scraping…
freezer-life-ledger.why: Track opened, frozen, and finished packages privately on your device.
freezer-life-ledger.detail: Barcode/name entry, one-tap Open/Freeze/Finish actions, best-before date, location, and a ‘use next’ list. Non-goals: retailer integrations, recipe scraping, nutrition calculations, multi-user accounts.
freezer-life-ledger.user: A household cook who freezes part of packages and needs to know what is open, frozen, and worth using first.
freezer-life-ledger.distinct: Models the state of an opened package rather than trying to be a complete pantry, grocery, recipe, and nutrition suite.
freezer-life-ledger.workaround: Write dates on bags, keep a rough freezer list, or perform several manual stock state changes in Grocy.

frequency-feel.title: Frequency Feel
frequency-feel.description: Offline interactive page with a safe synthetic sound, draggable filter/EQ controls, synchronized frequency response, before/after loudness-matched playback…
frequency-feel.why: Hear and see what a filter changes with a safe synthesized loop and a live frequency-response map.
frequency-feel.detail: Offline interactive page with a safe synthetic sound, draggable filter/EQ controls, synchronized frequency response, before/after loudness-matched playback, and shareable parameter links. Non-goals: mastering, uploading user audio, medical/hearing claims, and AI mixing.
frequency-feel.user: A beginner sound designer who wants to hear and see what a filter/EQ setting changes before committing it to a track or game effect.
frequency-feel.distinct: It makes signal behavior tangible through controlled listening rather than being another generic visualizer or audio effect rack.
frequency-feel.workaround: Trial-and-error, external EQ charts, spectrum analyzers, and repeatedly rendering/listening to clips.

friend-file-drop.title: Friend File Drop
friend-file-drop.description: Send files directly between devices and keep a receipt.
friend-file-drop.why: Send private files between phones and computers, with no account.
friend-file-drop.detail: A browser-based WebRTC transfer room with a six-word code, explicit file manifest and hash, resumable same-LAN fallback, and a sender/receiver completion receipt. Non-goals: persistent cloud storage, social accounts, or content discovery.
friend-file-drop.user: People sending a few private files to friends or family on mixed devices who need a linkless, low-friction transfer with a clear receipt that it finished.
friend-file-drop.distinct: The compact transfer receipt and no-account mixed-device handoff are the product, not another cloud drive.
friend-file-drop.workaround: Use AirDrop only where possible, upload to Drive/Dropbox/WeTransfer, send a chat attachment, or compress and email files.

function-flow-canvas.title: Function Flow Canvas
function-flow-canvas.description: A local CLI using an installed language server to emit one self-contained HTML canvas for a selected symbol: inbound/outbound calls, type hops, source…
function-flow-canvas.why: Map one function's callers, callees, types, and source into a private, self-contained HTML canvas.
function-flow-canvas.detail: A local CLI using an installed language server to emit one self-contained HTML canvas for a selected symbol: inbound/outbound calls, type hops, source snippets, and collapsible depth. Non-goals: repository-wide AI search, code editing, or hosted code indexing.
function-flow-canvas.user: Engineers onboarding to an unfamiliar service who need to follow one request path across functions, files, and types without opening an unbounded set of editor tabs.
function-flow-canvas.distinct: It is a constrained code-reading artifact, not another IDE, code graph database, or LLM codebase chat.
function-flow-canvas.workaround: Use editor go-to-definition/back stacks, manually split tabs, draw temporary diagrams, or ask a teammate for a tour.

future-skills-portfolio.title: Future Skills Portfolio
future-skills-portfolio.description: Build a portfolio from printable math and computing challenges for ages 10–16.
future-skills-portfolio.why: Build a private portfolio with printable math and computing challenges for ages 10–16.
future-skills-portfolio.detail: A printable/static challenge deck for ages 10–16: each card has a build/explain/critique task, material limits, reflection prompts, and a parent/peer rubric; families can create and share local decks. Non-goals: career prediction, AI tutoring, child social network, or data collection.
future-skills-portfolio.user: A parent or home-school educator unsure how to develop a child's math/CS strengths in an AI-rich world and needing concrete, human-reviewable challenges rather than predictions about careers.
future-skills-portfolio.distinct: It turns an abstract AI-era anxiety into varied human capabilities demonstrated through artifacts, not an AI course for children.
future-skills-portfolio.workaround: Continue with standard worksheets/coding courses, follow AI news anxiously, or assemble disconnected projects and competitions.

game-logic-tiles.title: Game Logic Tiles
game-logic-tiles.description: Change five game rules and see each turn across ten beginner puzzles.
game-logic-tiles.why: Build and test small game rules with editable puzzle tiles.
game-logic-tiles.detail: Static web app with grid puzzles, editable rule tiles (move, collide, collect, timer, score), a step button, and shareable challenge seeds. Non-goals: freeform programming, user-created asset marketplace, multiplayer, or LLM tutor.
game-logic-tiles.user: Puzzle-loving beginners who want to learn game-state and rule logic by changing small playable systems before being asked to learn a programming language or engine.
game-logic-tiles.distinct: It teaches the causal model of game rules through constrained experiments, not another visual-programming canvas.
game-logic-tiles.workaround: Follow tutorials verbatim, wrestle with a general-purpose engine, or use Scratch projects whose logic and UI are not organised as a teachable system.

game-night-score-ledger.title: Game Night Score Ledger
game-night-score-ledger.description: A share-by-QR PWA: host enters players, scoring increments, optional lap threshold, and team totals; guests can view but not edit; export CSV/image. Non-goals…
game-night-score-ledger.why: Track teams, rounds, and scores during board-game nights.
game-night-score-ledger.detail: A share-by-QR PWA: host enters players, scoring increments, optional lap threshold, and team totals; guests can view but not edit; export CSV/image. Non-goals: game rules engines, BGG catalog sync, chat, ratings, or ads.
game-night-score-ledger.user: A board-game host running games with score tracks that wrap, teams, or many rounds who needs an auditable scoreboard that does not interrupt play.
game-night-score-ledger.distinct: A session instrument for awkward physical scoreboards, not a collection database or generic score-counter clone.
game-night-score-ledger.workaround: Paper, borrowed counters, a generic calculator, or a large all-purpose collection app.

game-text-beacon.title: Game Text Beacon
game-text-beacon.description: A Windows/Linux desktop overlay that takes a user-drawn or gamepad-positioned region on hotkey, reads it locally, and queues speech without intercepting game in
game-text-beacon.detail: A Windows/Linux desktop overlay that takes a user-drawn or gamepad-positioned region on hotkey, reads it locally, and queues speech without intercepting game input. Non-goals: gameplay automation, anti-cheat bypass, multiplayer overlays, or cloud screenshots.
game-text-beacon.user: Blind and low-vision PC players who need an on-demand way to read a dialogue, menu, or objective from games that lack screen-reader support.
game-text-beacon.distinct: Its gamepad-aware, intentional capture model targets unsupported visual text rather than promising full automated game accessibility.
game-text-beacon.workaround: Use OCR tools not designed for games, magnify the display, rely on a companion, or skip inaccessible titles.

garden-care-map.title: Garden Care Map
garden-care-map.description: Map garden beds, plants, care notes, and water lines in one private offline record.
garden-care-map.why: Map garden beds, care notes, and irrigation lines on one offline canvas.
garden-care-map.detail: Offline canvas for beds/containers, plant labels, dated care notes, and simple irrigation line segments with length totals. Non-goals: plant identification, disease diagnosis, weather prediction, seed marketplace, or social sharing.
garden-care-map.user: Small-space gardeners who need to remember what is planted where, what care happened there, and how irrigation physically reaches each bed.
garden-care-map.distinct: It joins care history to the actual garden geometry, not an AI plant identifier or a decorative garden-design app.
garden-care-map.workaround: Use a generic plant reminder app plus a hand-drawn bed sketch, photos, and a separate irrigation diagram.

gaze-calibration-card.title: Gaze Calibration Card
gaze-calibration-card.description: Compare your gaze-controlled pointer across nine targets before a demanding task.
gaze-calibration-card.why: Check a gaze pointer against nine targets before a demanding task.
gaze-calibration-card.detail: A local calibration companion that runs a 30-second nine-target check, reports directional error and dwell reliability, stores user-approved posture/setup notes, and exports a support-friendly report. Non-goals: cursor control, medical eye tracking, cloud analytics, or replacing a hardware vendor driver.
gaze-calibration-card.user: A person relying on eye input with changing posture, wheelchair position, glasses, or fatigue who needs to know quickly whether gaze control is reliable enough before a frustrating interaction.
gaze-calibration-card.distinct: It validates usable gaze input before an interaction instead of offering yet another gaze-control implementation.
gaze-calibration-card.workaround: Repeatedly recalibrate the full eye tracker, adjust the monitor/chair, ask a helper, or try to continue through inaccurate clicks.

gesture-game-replay.title: Gesture Replay Kit
gesture-game-replay.description: NPM library and local viewer that records only timestamped pose/hand landmarks, replays them at chosen speed, compares gesture rules, and exports a scrubbed…
gesture-game-replay.why: Trace, replay gestures, and compare deterministic rules without retaining video.
gesture-game-replay.detail: NPM library and local viewer that records only timestamped pose/hand landmarks, replays them at chosen speed, compares gesture rules, and exports a scrubbed fixture. Non-goals: camera surveillance, identity recognition, cloud video storage, or a game engine.
gesture-game-replay.user: Indie game and classroom-toy makers using a webcam as input who need to tune a gesture game from recorded landmark traces without retaining children's or players' video.
gesture-game-replay.distinct: It makes unusual camera input testable and privacy-preserving rather than creating another gesture-controlled game.
gesture-game-replay.workaround: Retest in front of a webcam, keep raw clips, add ad-hoc debug overlays, or write one-off scripts for MediaPipe output.

gesture-gameplay-calibrator.title: MoveMap
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.description: Local browser app: define 1–3 pose checkpoints, collect 10 examples, show live confidence/history, and export a JSON threshold profile. Non-goals: OS key…
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.why: Test webcam gestures locally, replay them for false triggers, and export a profile for your game.
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.detail: Local browser app: define 1–3 pose checkpoints, collect 10 examples, show live confidence/history, and export a JSON threshold profile. Non-goals: OS key injection, surveillance, cloud video storage, multiplayer game engine.
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.user: Webcam-motion game makers and players who need to test whether a body gesture can be recognized reliably in a real room before mapping it to a game action.
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.distinct: It validates and communicates gesture reliability rather than pretending to be a universal controller.
gesture-gameplay-calibrator.workaround: Write one-off MediaPipe scripts, tweak thresholds in source, and install virtual-camera or input-emulation software.

gh-account-autoswitch.title: Automatic per-repo GitHub account selection for the `gh` CLI
gh-account-autoswitch.description: Choose the right GitHub account for each repository before running gh.
gh-account-autoswitch.why: Choose the right signed-in GitHub account for each repo.
gh-account-autoswitch.detail: v1: a small Go binary installed as a `gh` shim (or via `gh extension install`) that reads `~/.config/gh-accounts.toml` rules (remote host/org/owner regex, directory glob → account), resolves the repo from cwd, obtains the token via `gh auth token --user`, and execs the real `gh` with `GH_TOKEN` scoped to that process only (never mutating global state); `which` explains the decision and `init` generates rules from `gh auth status`. Not in v1: managing git identities, SSH keys, or hosts beyond GitHub/GHES.
gh-account-autoswitch.user: Developer with separate work and personal GitHub accounts (and increasingly, multiple concurrent coding-agent sessions) who wants `gh` to use the right account based on the repo's remote/org/directory, the way git's `includeIf` does.
gh-account-autoswitch.distinct: A policy layer upstream deliberately declined, and the per-process token model (rather than a global switch) solves the concurrency problem that even the upstream feature request does not address.
gh-account-autoswitch.workaround: Manual `gh auth switch`, per-directory GH_TOKEN via direnv, shell aliases, or separate machines/containers.

gha-dry-run-planner.title: No-execution GitHub Actions workflow planner: which jobs/steps will run for a given event, and why
gha-dry-run-planner.description: Plan GitHub Actions jobs and steps before pushing, without running the workflow.
gha-dry-run-planner.why: Plan a GitHub Actions workflow before you push. See which jobs and steps will run or skip in your browser.
gha-dry-run-planner.detail: v1: `ghaplan --event pull_request --base main --head feat --paths src/a.ts` prints a tree of workflows → jobs → steps with run/skip decisions and the reason (path filter, branch filter, `if:` value, matrix cell) plus warnings for secrets/permissions used; the same engine runs in a static web page with an event form. Implements the GitHub expression language and contexts (github, inputs, matrix, needs, env) with declared unknowns. Not in v1: executing steps, fetching remote reusable workflows (local only), composite-action internals, or other CI systems.
gha-dry-run-planner.user: Developer editing .github/workflows who wants instant, local feedback on triggers, path filters, `if:` conditions, matrix expansion, `needs` ordering and expression values before pushing — without Docker or running anything.
gha-dry-run-planner.distinct: act and its successors try to *run* CI locally and fail on environment fidelity; this answers the cheaper, more common question ('will this even trigger, and what will run?') that no tool answers, and it is what the 'validate/dry-run' commenters literally asked for.
gha-dry-run-planner.workaround: Push-and-pray with `[skip ci]` noise, act (heavy images, environment drift), actionlint (syntax/types only), reading the GitHub UI after the fact.

git-forge-exit-drill.title: Git Forge Exit Drill
git-forge-exit-drill.description: Test a GitHub move before cutover with local evidence.
git-forge-exit-drill.why: Test a GitHub move with local evidence and target maps before cutover.
git-forge-exit-drill.detail: CLI that inventories a GitHub repository via supplied exports/API token, creates a local encrypted evidence archive, maps artifacts to GitLab/Gitea/Forgejo capabilities, and emits a migration drill checklist. Non-goals: hosting a forge, automatic cutover, webhook forwarding, or scraping private content without authorization.
git-forge-exit-drill.user: A small team considering a move from GitHub who wants a tested answer to ‘can we preserve our repositories, pull-request history, releases, issues, and build provenance and still work next Monday?’
git-forge-exit-drill.distinct: It measures an exit’s operational completeness instead of offering another Git forge or a superficial repository mirror.
git-forge-exit-drill.workaround: Mirror Git repositories only, export data manually, keep a spreadsheet of missing artifacts, or postpone leaving because migration feels irreversible.

git-stage-lines.title: Non-interactive, line-range staging for git (and for coding agents)
git-stage-lines.description: Stage exact Git lines from scripts or coding agents without interactive prompts.
git-stage-lines.why: Stage selected Git lines from scripts and coding agents without an interactive patch prompt.
git-stage-lines.detail: v1: `git stage-lines path/to/file.ts:12-18,40 other.py:3` computes the working-tree vs index diff, builds a minimal patch containing only the requested lines (context handled correctly; deletions addressed by original line numbers with a `-` prefix), and applies it with `git apply --cached`; `--unstage` and `--dry-run` print the patch; installs as a git subcommand with Node and Python wrappers for agent toolkits. Not in v1: interactive UI, commit splitting, or history rewriting.
git-stage-lines.user: Developer or coding agent who wants to stage exactly lines 12-18 and 40 of a file from a script or one command instead of driving `git add -p`'s interactive hunk editor.
git-stage-lines.distinct: Not a porcelain around `add -p`; it is the missing non-interactive primitive the interactive tools are built on, exposed with an explicit line-range grammar.
git-stage-lines.workaround: `git add -p` with manual hunk editing (`e`), `git gui` line staging, GitButler (GUI), or hand-crafting a patch for `git apply --cached`.

github-dependency-exit.title: GitHub Exit Inventory
github-dependency-exit.description: Map GitHub dependencies before changing forges.
github-dependency-exit.why: List what you need before moving away from GitHub.
github-dependency-exit.detail: A read-only CLI that inventories repositories, Actions, webhooks, GitHub Apps/OAuth references, packages, branch rules, and issue links, then writes a migration checklist with alternatives marked as verified or unknown. Non-goals: executing migration, mirroring private code, or hosting git.
github-dependency-exit.user: Small software teams considering a GitHub fallback who need to know which repository, CI, OAuth, release, and integration dependencies make a move costly.
github-dependency-exit.distinct: It helps teams quantify and plan portability without cloning GitHub or another forge.
github-dependency-exit.workaround: Clone repositories, list Actions and apps manually, search documentation, and learn missing integrations during a migration.

google-photos-delta-archive.title: Photo Delta Archive
google-photos-delta-archive.description: Archive downloaded Google Takeout exports locally and restore checked snapshots.
google-photos-delta-archive.why: Export on your computer and restore any saved snapshot.
google-photos-delta-archive.detail: A desktop CLI that ingests successive user-downloaded Takeout archives, normalizes sidecars, de-duplicates by content plus metadata, builds a dated delta ledger, and verifies restore samples. Non-goals: scraping Google Photos, circumventing revoked APIs, or replacing the photo library.
google-photos-delta-archive.user: Google Photos users who want a restorable, incremental local archive even when the provider API and Takeout workflow do not support it cleanly.
google-photos-delta-archive.distinct: It works with sanctioned exports and produces an auditable delta, rather than pretending revoked APIs can be restored.
google-photos-delta-archive.workaround: Repeated full Takeout exports, fragile browser automation, or switching photo libraries and hoping the migration is complete.

gpu-vram-burnin.title: VRAM Burn-in Kit
gpu-vram-burnin.description: Signed Windows/Linux desktop utility that selects a GPU, runs bounded fill/copy/readback and shader-pattern passes, temperature-aware retries, and exports a sig
gpu-vram-burnin.detail: Signed Windows/Linux desktop utility that selects a GPU, runs bounded fill/copy/readback and shader-pattern passes, temperature-aware retries, and exports a signed JSON/HTML casefile. Non-goals: overclocking, repair, mining or driver tuning.
gpu-vram-burnin.user: PC builders and local-AI operators who need a repeatable, bootable-or-desktop test that finds intermittent GPU VRAM faults before trusting a card with long jobs.
gpu-vram-burnin.distinct: It produces a memory-specific diagnostic receipt rather than being another benchmark chart or GPU tuner.
gpu-vram-burnin.workaround: Run a game benchmark, stress a model, inspect vendor telemetry, or replace hardware based on suspicion.

gpx-cue-audit.title: Cue Audit
gpx-cue-audit.description: Offline GPX linter that detects sharp same-road turns, close overlapping/reversed segments, long no-cue stretches, and missing directionality; emits a printable
gpx-cue-audit.detail: Offline GPX linter that detects sharp same-road turns, close overlapping/reversed segments, long no-cue stretches, and missing directionality; emits a printable cue-review sheet. Non-goals: live navigation, route generation, or map editing.
gpx-cue-audit.user: Cyclists exporting GPX for unfamiliar or out-and-back rides who need to find missing turns and ambiguous overlapping track direction before sharing a route.
gpx-cue-audit.distinct: It validates shareable route instructions rather than offering another basemap or cycling computer.
gpx-cue-audit.workaround: Inspect GPX manually, add waypoints by hand, carry a separate cue sheet, or zoom/pan while riding.

guest-booking-confirm.title: Guest Booking Confirm
guest-booking-confirm.description: Confirm guest appointments after owner approval, without guest accounts.
guest-booking-confirm.why: Request, confirm, reschedule, and remember guest appointments without creating an account.
guest-booking-confirm.detail: A mobile-first booking page with no account, owner-approved time requests, single-use confirm/reschedule/cancel links, ICS attachment, and a local reminder checklist. Non-goals: payments, staff rota optimization, marketing CRM, or automated SMS sending.
guest-booking-confirm.user: A microbusiness taking appointments from people who should not need to create an account, and who need a clear confirmation/reminder trail.
guest-booking-confirm.distinct: It treats guest confirmation state as the product, rather than adding another full scheduling platform.
guest-booking-confirm.workaround: Ask clients to register, take bookings by phone/WhatsApp, or connect a calendar and SMS service through Zapier.

guided-inking-overlay.title: Ink Guides
guided-inking-overlay.description: Draw perspective and curved guides over private references, then export a clean guide layer.
guided-inking-overlay.why: Draw reusable perspective fans and curved guides over private references, then export clean SVG.
guided-inking-overlay.detail: A transparent browser/canvas overlay where a user saves guide scenes, adjusts fan density/rotation and spline offsets, imports a reference image, and exports SVG/PNG guide layers. Non-goals: painting engine, image generation, or a substitute for an illustration app.
guided-inking-overlay.user: Comic and concept artists who need reusable rotated perspective and curved parallel guides while inking, including on lightweight tablet/browser setups.
guided-inking-overlay.distinct: It is a guide instrument that works beside an art app, not a paint-program clone.
guided-inking-overlay.workaround: Create many manual assistants, rotate the canvas repeatedly, draw guide layers, or switch to a more expensive desktop editor.

haptic-beat-relay.title: Haptic Beat Relay
haptic-beat-relay.description: Send vibration beat cues to a friend and score their returned taps.
haptic-beat-relay.detail: A host page loads a local beat loop; a second device joins with a six-character code and receives vibration cues, taps back on-beat, and shows a shared accuracy meter. Non-goals: music streaming, competitive matchmaking, payments, or social graph.
haptic-beat-relay.user: Friends and rhythm-game makers who want a simple way to turn a phone/controller into tactile beat cues and small responsive music games without an online service.
haptic-beat-relay.distinct: It supplies tactile, multi-device music interaction primitives rather than a content catalogue or a generic multiplayer framework.
haptic-beat-relay.workaround: Use inaccessible commercial rhythm games, custom game-engine code, or audio-only metronomes with no tactile adaptation.

headless-scheduler.title: Headless, Tailwind-native calendar/scheduler library with free resource-timeline views
headless-scheduler.description: Build calendar and resource timeline UIs with headless TypeScript scheduling logic.
headless-scheduler.why: Build calendar and resource timeline views with TypeScript.
headless-scheduler.detail: v1 (npm, framework-agnostic core + React adapter): day/week/month views with continuous vertical month scrolling, a horizontal resource-timeline view (hours/days), event drag/resize/create via pointer events, keyboard navigation and ARIA grid roles, Temporal/date-fns adapters, and a Tailwind example theme. Not in v1: Vue/Svelte adapters, recurrence expansion (accept pre-expanded events), iCal parsing, printing, or a hosted builder.
headless-scheduler.user: Product engineer building booking, staffing or planning UIs in React/Vue/Svelte who needs resource timelines and continuous-scroll month views styled with their own design system, without FullCalendar Premium or Schedule-X Premium licences.
headless-scheduler.distinct: Headless + Tailwind-first + free resource timeline is the combination neither incumbent will offer because it is their paid tier; the strategy mirrors how TanStack Table displaced styled grids.
headless-scheduler.workaround: Pay FullCalendar Premium/Schedule-X Premium/Bryntum/DHTMLX, fight FullCalendar CSS overrides, or hand-roll a grid with date-fns and CSS grid.

health-export-cleaner.title: Health Export Cleaner
health-export-cleaner.description: Clean health exports locally before sharing by removing identifiers, locations, unwanted records, and precise times.
health-export-cleaner.why: Clean a health export before sharing it.
health-export-cleaner.detail: Browser-only tool that reads a supported health CSV/XML export, selects date range and record types, drops identifiers/GPS/routes, bins timestamps, previews row counts, and writes a provenance note with the cleaned file. health-export-cleaner.user: Wearable users who want to keep, move, or share a bounded slice of their own health data while removing precise location, identifiers, and fields they did not intend to disclose.
health-export-cleaner.distinct: It is a data-minimization and portability tool, not another health dashboard or data broker.
health-export-cleaner.workaround: Send the full Apple Health/fitness export, manually edit CSVs, or give another app account-level access.

health-visit-packet.title: Health Visit Packet
