health-visit-packet.detail: Browser-only packet builder: paste/import selected values, attach source/date, add questions and a medication list, then generate a printable PDF and encrypted local bundle. Non-goals: OCR automation, record scraping, clinical interpretation, provider messaging, or emergency decision support.
health-visit-packet.user: Patients preparing for an appointment who need a compact, accurate packet of their own labs, medicines, questions, and observations from scattered portals.
health-visit-packet.distinct: It is a preparation and handoff artifact, not a universal health-data platform.
health-visit-packet.workaround: Open several portals during the visit, carry screenshots, or manually assemble a document in Notes/Word.

hearing-mode-notes.title: Hearing Mode Notes
hearing-mode-notes.description: Offline Android app with one-tap place tags, mode/volume notes, optional manual sound-comfort rating, and a lock-screen reminder of the last successful setup.…
hearing-mode-notes.why: Record which hearing-aid mode and volume worked at each place on your device.
hearing-mode-notes.detail: Offline Android app with one-tap place tags, mode/volume notes, optional manual sound-comfort rating, and a lock-screen reminder of the last successful setup. Non-goals: controlling hearing aids, sound amplification, hearing tests, or medical advice.
hearing-mode-notes.user: Hearing-aid wearers who change listening modes by place and need a quick, private record of what setting actually worked.
hearing-mode-notes.distinct: It is an experiential memory aid around device modes, not another hearing-aid controller or a medical app.
hearing-mode-notes.workaround: Memorize settings, take generic notes, repeatedly open a manufacturer app, or leave a suboptimal mode active.

hex-daily-notebook.title: Hex Daily Notebook
hex-daily-notebook.description: A static PWA serving one deterministic daily hex deduction puzzle, an unlimited local pencil layer with eraser, keyboard alternatives, archive after a delay…
hex-daily-notebook.why: Solve a daily hex puzzle with a private pencil layer.
hex-daily-notebook.detail: A static PWA serving one deterministic daily hex deduction puzzle, an unlimited local pencil layer with eraser, keyboard alternatives, archive after a delay, and no sign-in. Non-goals: leaderboard, user chat, gambling mechanics, or copied newspaper puzzle formats.
hex-daily-notebook.user: People who enjoy a short free web puzzle each day and prefer to think with pen-like marks and spatial grids rather than word-game clones.
hex-daily-notebook.distinct: The core is an original hex spatial-deduction notebook, not a word-game clone or a generic whiteboard.
hex-daily-notebook.workaround: Play word puzzles, print grid puzzles, use a generic whiteboard, or keep scratch paper beside a daily game.

hifi-sketch-check.title: Sketch Density Check
hifi-sketch-check.description: CLI that runs a sketch through a small local device matrix, records frame-time/input-lag traces and golden frames, then writes a plain-language publish card.…
hifi-sketch-check.why: Check creative coding sketches on dense phone and tablet screens.
hifi-sketch-check.detail: CLI that runs a sketch through a small local device matrix, records frame-time/input-lag traces and golden frames, then writes a plain-language publish card. Non-goals: remote device farm, source-code generation, analytics tracker, or visual editor.
hifi-sketch-check.user: Creative-coding teachers and artists publishing interactive sketches who need to know whether a work will render and respond correctly on the high-density phone/tablet displays their audience actually uses.
hifi-sketch-check.distinct: It is a publish-readiness diagnostic for interactive art, not a creative-coding framework or a screenshot test service.
hifi-sketch-check.workaround: Test on the author’s laptop, add a pixel-ratio guess, or wait for audience bug reports with no reproducible performance context.

home-care-evidence.title: Home Care Evidence
home-care-evidence.description: Local PWA with a maintenance card containing the observed issue, photos, vendor/DIY note, receipt attachment, due interval, and printable one-page history.…
home-care-evidence.why: Keep the reason, repair proof, and next due date for every home-care item together on your device.
home-care-evidence.detail: Local PWA with a maintenance card containing the observed issue, photos, vendor/DIY note, receipt attachment, due interval, and printable one-page history. Non-goals: contractor marketplace, inspection diagnosis, smart-home integrations, or cloud storage.
home-care-evidence.user: A homeowner turning an inspection finding or completed repair into a repeatable maintenance record that another household member can understand years later.
home-care-evidence.distinct: It preserves maintenance evidence and context, rather than being another task list or home-service lead generator.
home-care-evidence.workaround: Keep an inspection PDF, scattered photos, invoices, calendar reminders, and a vague to-do item in different locations.

home-maintenance-receipts.title: Home Maintenance Receipts
home-maintenance-receipts.description: Offline log of appliance/system, completed task, date, provider, cost optional, next-due date, and attachment hash/link; generate a one-page-per-system PDF repo
home-maintenance-receipts.detail: Offline log of appliance/system, completed task, date, provider, cost optional, next-due date, and attachment hash/link; generate a one-page-per-system PDF report. Non-goals: contractor booking, automated diagnosis, insurance claims filing, or smart-home control.
home-maintenance-receipts.user: Households that need to remember recurring upkeep and prove what was done, when, and with which documents when selling, insuring, or simply troubleshooting a home.
home-maintenance-receipts.distinct: It treats completed-work evidence and portable reports as the product, rather than a broad home inventory or reminder app.
home-maintenance-receipts.workaround: Calendar reminders plus email search, paper binders, photo albums, and a generic drive folder.

home-service-history.title: House Receipt
home-service-history.description: Offline PWA with a single job receipt: component/location, completion date, cost, contractor, warranty expiry, photos, and next service date; export as a PDF…
home-service-history.why: Keep a private, portable history of home repairs, warranties, costs and photos—right on your device.
home-service-history.detail: Offline PWA with a single job receipt: component/location, completion date, cost, contractor, warranty expiry, photos, and next service date; export as a PDF or encrypted archive. Non-goals: contractor marketplace, repair diagnosis, insurance claims, or smart-home integration.
home-service-history.user: Homeowners who need a durable, shareable history of maintenance work, warranties, costs, and photos when a repair recurs or a contractor asks what happened before.
home-service-history.distinct: It makes a completed maintenance job a portable evidence packet instead of becoming another sprawling home-management database.
home-service-history.workaround: Notes, email receipts, photos, task-manager completions, spreadsheets, and paper folders.

home-service-passbook.title: Home Service Passbook
home-service-passbook.description: Track home service work, due dates, and proof in a private browser passbook.
home-service-passbook.why: Track home maintenance with notes, receipts, and repeat schedules.
home-service-passbook.detail: Offline PWA with assets/areas, repeat-every vs repeat-after schedules, completion notes/photo/receipt reference, and a printable history. Non-goals: IoT control, contractor marketplace, automated diagnosis, or warranty claims.
home-service-passbook.user: Households that want to remember recurring home care and retain proof of what was done, without tying maintenance to appliance-cloud apps.
home-service-passbook.distinct: It treats maintenance history as household-owned paperwork, separate from surveillance-prone appliance control.
home-service-passbook.workaround: Use vendor apps, calendar reminders, a spreadsheet, receipts in email, or a generic to-do list that cannot model completion-relative recurrence.

hotkey-runbook.title: Hotkey Runbook
hotkey-runbook.description: Tray/menubar launcher reading signed local YAML runbooks, prompting for typed parameters, showing dry-run text, executing locally, and retaining redacted comman
hotkey-runbook.detail: Tray/menubar launcher reading signed local YAML runbooks, prompting for typed parameters, showing dry-run text, executing locally, and retaining redacted command history. Non-goals: remote orchestration, secret vault, or low-code automation cloud.
hotkey-runbook.user: Operators and developers who repeatedly execute internal maintenance steps and need a fast keyboard-first launcher with local, reviewable runbooks.
hotkey-runbook.distinct: It makes safe repeatable operational steps the unit of interaction, not a general command palette.
hotkey-runbook.workaround: Shell history, wiki pages, Raycast/PowerToys snippets, and manually copied command sequences.

house-history-pack.title: House History Pack
house-history-pack.description: Keep every home record ready for service calls and handovers.
house-history-pack.why: Keep a history of work done on a home.
house-history-pack.detail: An offline PWA for assets, service events, next-due tasks, warranty expiry, attached local files, and a selectable PDF/ZIP house-history pack. Non-goals: contractor marketplace, home valuation, smart-home control, or automated legal compliance advice.
house-history-pack.user: A homeowner who needs one durable history of appliances, seasonal work, repairs, warranties, permits, and contractor notes that can be handed to a buyer or service person.
house-history-pack.distinct: The core deliverable is a portable proof/history pack, not a generic task reminder app.
house-history-pack.workaround: Folders of receipts/manuals, email search, a calendar reminder, a spreadsheet, or starting a new note for every repair.

how-it-runs.title: How It Runs: 5-minute browser simulators of everyday jobs and systems, built to explain 'what do you actually do?' to kids
how-it-runs.description: Run water, power, and bakery systems with controls, results, and faults.
how-it-runs.why: Run water, power, and bakery browser simulations with three controls and five stages.
how-it-runs.detail: One shared engine (flow graph of tanks/queues/valves rendered in 2D) and three original systems at launch: municipal water treatment, a small power grid, and a bakery production line. Loop: adjust 3–4 levers, watch throughput/quality/cost meters, hit a target, unlock the 'what if' fault (storm, demand spike). 'Watch' mode auto-plays with captions. No accounts; state in URL. Deliberately NOT: full tycoon economy, multiplayer, LLM narration, accurate engineering fidelity beyond intuition.
how-it-runs.user: Parents in technical/industrial jobs (and teachers) who want a hands-on, kid-safe way to show how a system like a refinery, water plant or power grid works — and a passive 'watch it run' mode.
how-it-runs.distinct: PhET explains physics concepts; this explains socio-technical systems and jobs, with a watch-mode and a shared engine so the series compounds instead of being one-off hobby projects.
how-it-runs.workaround: YouTube explainers (passive, ads), PhET (science concepts, not jobs/systems), one-off hobby sims.

humane-practical-exams.title: Humane Practical Exams
humane-practical-exams.description: Self-hostable web app for a timed task brief, local artifact upload, candidate-written work log, checkpoint hashes, and assessor rubric with an exportable…
humane-practical-exams.why: Run open-book practical exams with evidence and clear rubrics.
humane-practical-exams.detail: Self-hostable web app for a timed task brief, local artifact upload, candidate-written work log, checkpoint hashes, and assessor rubric with an exportable assessment record. Non-goals: webcam monitoring, browser lockdown, identity verification, or AI cheating detection.
humane-practical-exams.user: An instructor or training provider assessing practical technical skills who wants credible evidence without invasive remote-proctoring surveillance.
humane-practical-exams.distinct: It makes assessable work visible while deliberately refusing the surveillance features that caused the reported harm.
humane-practical-exams.workaround: Use webcam/room surveillance, locked-down browsers, live screen share, or unstructured take-home work that is difficult to assess consistently.

ics-intake-checker.title: ICS Intake Checker
ics-intake-checker.description: Check an ICS file for import risks, choose fixes, and download a copy for your calendar app.
ics-intake-checker.why: Check calendar files before importing them.
ics-intake-checker.detail: Browser-local drag-and-drop ICS inspector with readable event preview, timezone/recurrence validation, duplicate fingerprinting, and calendar-specific export choices. Non-goals: calendar hosting, scheduling links, or account sync.
ics-intake-checker.user: People receiving event files from schools, clinics, conferences, and vendors who need to safely preview, fix, and route an .ics file before it pollutes the wrong calendar.
ics-intake-checker.distinct: It is a calendar-file preflight and repair utility, not another calendar interface.
ics-intake-checker.workaround: Email the file to oneself, add a subscription URL, edit raw ICS by hand, or import into a throwaway calendar first.

ics-to-phone-calendar.title: Paste-an-ICS, get one-tap add-to-calendar links (iPhone-safe)
ics-to-phone-calendar.description: Repair ICS invites and open them in Apple, Google, or Outlook calendars.
ics-to-phone-calendar.why: Repair an ICS invite and download it for Apple Calendar or open it in Google and Outlook.
ics-to-phone-calendar.detail: Static page: drop or paste an .ics; it parses locally, lists events, validates/repairs common defects (missing DTEND, bad TZID, CRLF), and renders per-event 'Add to Apple/Google/Outlook' links plus a 'download fixed .ics' and a shareable QR. No accounts, no server storage of calendar contents. Does not sync, host recurring feeds, or send invitations.
ics-to-phone-calendar.user: iPhone users (and people sending them invites) who receive .ics attachments or downloads that iOS 18 shows but will not import; job: get the event into their calendar in one tap.
ics-to-phone-calendar.distinct: Solves the consumer-side 'I have the file' problem instead of the marketer-side 'make a button' problem, with local validation/repair of the file itself.
ics-to-phone-calendar.workaround: Email the .ics to yourself and open in Mail; drag file from Files into Calendar while holding; import into Gmail/Outlook and let it sync; retype events by hand.

idempotency-rehearsal.title: Idempotency Rehearsal
idempotency-rehearsal.description: A local CLI/test-library that sends a declared event sequence to an HTTP handler, records outbound effects through adapters, and asserts one logical effect per…
idempotency-rehearsal.why: Test that duplicate webhooks create one business effect.
idempotency-rehearsal.detail: A local CLI/test-library that sends a declared event sequence to an HTTP handler, records outbound effects through adapters, and asserts one logical effect per idempotency key. Non-goals: webhook delivery infrastructure, queues, or production event storage.
idempotency-rehearsal.user: Backend engineers handling webhooks or workflow triggers who need to prove duplicate, delayed, and out-of-order events do not create a second business action.
idempotency-rehearsal.distinct: The output is an executable idempotency proof for an application handler, not a hosted webhook gateway.
idempotency-rehearsal.workaround: Write one-off curl scripts, encode behavior in IDs, add temporary database checks, or discover duplicate side effects in production.

identity-migration-map.title: Identity Migration Map
identity-migration-map.description: A local manifest generator taking declared identifier mappings plus filesystem/config/database read-only exports and producing dependency hits, owner…
identity-migration-map.why: Inventory every dependent file, record, and integration before changing a user identifier.
identity-migration-map.detail: A local manifest generator taking declared identifier mappings plus filesystem/config/database read-only exports and producing dependency hits, owner checklists, and a rollback ledger. Non-goals: changing accounts, provisioning identity, SSO, or automated database writes.
identity-migration-map.user: A self-hoster or small-team administrator changing a user identifier who needs to inventory every dependent path, record, and integration before a rename.
identity-migration-map.distinct: It plans and evidences an identity handoff without becoming an IAM product.
identity-migration-map.workaround: Create a new account, copy selected data, grep configuration/databases, or leave a legacy identity in place indefinitely.

import-mapping-replay.title: Import Mapping Replay
import-mapping-replay.description: Replay customer CSV imports and inspect mapped values, errors, and source rows.
import-mapping-replay.why: Replay customer CSV imports into a reviewed output file and error report before upload.
import-mapping-replay.detail: CLI with a simple declarative mapping file, local CSV transforms, deterministic sample/output diff, validation rules, and a rollback manifest of source rows. Non-goals: connectors, scheduled ETL, warehouse modeling, cloud storage, or automatic imports into third parties.
import-mapping-replay.user: An implementation engineer repeatedly loading customer CSVs into a template-based SaaS who needs transformations to be reviewable, rerunnable, and reversible.
import-mapping-replay.distinct: It is a narrow, evidence-producing import replay tool, not another ETL platform or spreadsheet replacement.
import-mapping-replay.workaround: Excel cleanup, one-off Python scripts, YAML pipelines, or paid ETL products that are too broad for a single import template.

import-transform-ledger.title: Import Transform Ledger
import-transform-ledger.description: A local web app that compares source/target CSV headers, records mapping and deterministic transforms, previews rejects/duplicates, and exports a recipe plus…
import-transform-ledger.why: Map, clean, validate, and document CSV imports entirely in your browser.
import-transform-ledger.detail: A local web app that compares source/target CSV headers, records mapping and deterministic transforms, previews rejects/duplicates, and exports a recipe plus output/checksum report. Non-goals: connecting to SaaS accounts, automatic semantic mapping, or a data warehouse.
import-transform-ledger.user: Implementation consultants and operations staff loading CSV data into business systems who need repeatable mapping, cleanup, and an audit trail without writing a bespoke script.
import-transform-ledger.distinct: It makes a human-reviewed import recipe and rejection ledger the product, rather than another general spreadsheet or ETL service.
import-transform-ledger.workaround: Use Excel/Power Query with undocumented edits, maintain fragile scripts, or hand-clean every new supplier export.

importance-weighted-review.title: Importance Weighted Review
importance-weighted-review.description: A local CSV/Anki-export policy editor that maps tags or numeric fields such as frequency, exam weight, and safety criticality to review targets, then previews…
importance-weighted-review.why: Turn your own card fields into a transparent, importance-weighted review policy—privately in your browser.
importance-weighted-review.detail: A local CSV/Anki-export policy editor that maps tags or numeric fields such as frequency, exam weight, and safety criticality to review targets, then previews added workload and exports settings. Non-goals: proprietary corpus ranking or medical advice.
importance-weighted-review.user: A learner maintaining a large mixed-value deck who needs common, high-impact concepts to receive more reliable recall than long-tail facts.
importance-weighted-review.distinct: It adds transparent value weighting to an existing scheduler instead of claiming an opaque model knows what a learner should study.
importance-weighted-review.workaround: Split decks manually, tag important facts, or set one blunt desired-retention target for everything.

in-class-draft-ticket.title: In-Class Draft Ticket
in-class-draft-ticket.description: Record students' in-class drafting choices without surveillance.
in-class-draft-ticket.why: Create short class sessions where students record claims, evidence, revisions.
in-class-draft-ticket.detail: Teacher PWA generates a session code and a short draft ticket: claim, evidence location, revision choice, and exit reflection; students submit pseudonymous tickets and the teacher exports a session sheet. Non-goals: AI detection, webcam proctoring, keystroke logging, or blocking other software.
in-class-draft-ticket.user: Writing teachers who need a humane way to document authentic in-class drafting after AI has made take-home written work hard to assess.
in-class-draft-ticket.distinct: It makes a lightweight pedagogical process artifact rather than policing students with AI detection or lockdown controls.
in-class-draft-ticket.workaround: Handwritten drafts, LockDown Browser, oral defenses, Google Docs history, or more proctored exams.

incident-boundary-replay.title: Boundary Replay
incident-boundary-replay.description: Record failed HTTP requests, remove selected secrets, and replay them on localhost.
incident-boundary-replay.why: Capture redacted web exchanges and replay them as a local mock.
incident-boundary-replay.detail: A sidecar/CLI that captures opted-in HTTP or webhook exchanges, applies field-level redaction, pairs them with trace IDs, and exports a runnable local mock fixture. Non-goals: traffic interception by default, production replay, or a tracing backend.
incident-boundary-replay.user: Backend engineers diagnosing production failures across queues, webhooks, and third-party APIs who need a scrubbed reproduction at the service boundary.
incident-boundary-replay.distinct: The artifact is a safe reproduction bundle at an integration boundary, not another APM dashboard.
incident-boundary-replay.workaround: Correlate traces and logs manually, copy sanitized curl commands into tickets, or retry against production-adjacent systems.

incident-fingerprint-preview.title: Fingerprint Preview
incident-fingerprint-preview.description: A CLI/library that imports redacted event JSON, evaluates a small fingerprint-rule DSL, and reports split/merge deltas with representative frames. Non-goals…
incident-fingerprint-preview.why: Preview how incident fingerprint rules split or merge events.
incident-fingerprint-preview.detail: A CLI/library that imports redacted event JSON, evaluates a small fingerprint-rule DSL, and reports split/merge deltas with representative frames. Non-goals: error ingestion, alert delivery, or a replacement incident tracker.
incident-fingerprint-preview.user: Engineers tuning error grouping rules who need to see exactly how a proposed fingerprint would split or merge real incident samples before changing alert volume in production.
incident-fingerprint-preview.distinct: It is a pre-deploy grouping test bench, not a hosted error-monitoring clone.
incident-fingerprint-preview.workaround: Edit server-side rules, wait for new events, inspect raw stacks, and undo the change if groups become noisier.

infra-test-evidence.title: Infra Test Evidence
infra-test-evidence.description: Convert OpenTofu and Terraform tests into redacted evidence reviewers can inspect locally.
infra-test-evidence.why: Collect test evidence from infrastructure checks for a release review.
infra-test-evidence.detail: A CLI that converts OpenTofu/Terraform test JSON into JUnit plus a static evidence page containing case inputs, assertion paths, redacted plan summaries, and provenance. Non-goals: running Terraform, storing state, or cloud test analytics.
infra-test-evidence.user: Infrastructure-module maintainers who need a compact, reviewable record of IaC test cases, plans, assertions, and failures in CI systems that only understand generic test reports.
infra-test-evidence.distinct: It is an IaC evidence adapter rather than a generic test dashboard or another Terraform runner.
infra-test-evidence.workaround: Transform JSON with one-off scripts, paste plan output into CI logs, or publish an empty JUnit shell that discards useful assertion context.

installer-release-doctor.title: Installer Release Doctor
installer-release-doctor.description: Check installer artifacts and release evidence before publishing to package channels.
installer-release-doctor.why: Check installer files before publishing a release.
installer-release-doctor.detail: CLI reads release artifacts and a declarative channel manifest, runs local checks for archive layout, signatures, SBOM/provenance, package metadata and installer upgrade paths, then emits GitHub Actions annotations and a channel matrix. Non-goals: credential storage, package hosting, code signing service or a new package manager.
installer-release-doctor.user: CLI authors who need to ship a signed, installable release across package channels without becoming experts in every distribution system.
installer-release-doctor.distinct: It checks and explains installer release readiness rather than trying to replace every package builder or registry.
installer-release-doctor.workaround: Hand-write packaging per platform, ship an archive with curl instructions, or abandon a channel after CI failures.

integration-changelog-watch.title: Integration Changelog Watch
integration-changelog-watch.description: Track vendor release notes and create action cards with owners, versions, and checks.
integration-changelog-watch.why: Watch vendor changelogs and flag the updates that match your rules.
integration-changelog-watch.detail: CLI plus optional static dashboard that watches explicit vendor changelog/RSS URLs, stores content hashes, matches human-authored keyword rules, and opens a Markdown action card with owner and local verification command. Non-goals: scraping behind logins, automatic code changes, LLM summaries, payload monitoring, or a generic alerting service.
integration-changelog-watch.user: An engineer responsible for payments, auth, analytics, or messaging integrations who needs a concise, owned action list when a vendor announces a relevant breaking change.
integration-changelog-watch.distinct: It operationalizes announced vendor changes, rather than duplicating observed-payload contract-drift monitoring.
integration-changelog-watch.workaround: Subscribe to vendor blogs/RSS, hope someone reads email, keep a spreadsheet, or discover changes via incident.

intent-voice-macros.title: Say the Action
intent-voice-macros.description: Browser extension with on-device speech recognition where available, a visible command palette, 10 user-approved DOM actions per site, and a confirmation step f
intent-voice-macros.detail: Browser extension with on-device speech recognition where available, a visible command palette, 10 user-approved DOM actions per site, and a confirmation step for submit/delete/navigation. Non-goals: whole-phone control, arbitrary code execution, hidden background listening, or agentic browsing.
intent-voice-macros.user: People with limited keyboard/mouse access who need a small, trustworthy voice-command layer for a few repeatable browser or coding actions.
intent-voice-macros.distinct: It makes a tiny user-auditable action grammar, not a thin wrapper around a general AI agent.
intent-voice-macros.workaround: Use platform voice access, dictation plus manual correction, bespoke automation, or an on-screen keyboard.

internal-event-ledger.title: Internal Event Ledger
internal-event-ledger.description: Review and retain low-priority webhook events in a self-hosted ledger.
internal-event-ledger.detail: Self-hosted receiver with endpoint aliases, event fingerprints, searchable timeline, acknowledge/archive state, daily digest, and JSON/CSV export. Non-goals: webhook retries, workflow automation, incident paging, or a Slack replacement.
internal-event-ledger.user: A solo developer or small product team that needs to review non-urgent operational events without letting them disappear inside Slack channels.
internal-event-ledger.distinct: It is a calm audit inbox for informational events, not a quiet-hours rule engine or a generic webhook proxy.
internal-event-ledger.workaround: Dedicated Slack channels, email, Notion/Airtable, or an expensive observability product with alert rules.

interview-recall-deck.title: Interview Recall Deck
interview-recall-deck.description: Recall real work examples in short, private interview rehearsals.
interview-recall-deck.why: Turn real projects into cards and rehearse your work examples for interviews in short, pausable rounds.
interview-recall-deck.detail: An offline PWA that turns a user’s own projects into short prompt/evidence cards, supports a timed but pausable voice-or-text rehearsal, and surfaces a one-page pre-interview recall sheet. Non-goals: generating false experience, diagnosing ADHD, scoring candidates, video surveillance or recruiter integrations.
interview-recall-deck.user: A job seeker with ADHD who needs a low-pressure, repeatable way to prepare and retrieve their own experience examples under interview stress.
interview-recall-deck.distinct: It supports truthful recall of a person’s own work rather than becoming an interview-answer generator or a generic task manager.
interview-recall-deck.workaround: Use generic flashcards, cram notes, ask an LLM to invent answers, or keep scattered documents that are hard to retrieve under pressure.

inventory-promise-hold.title: Stock Promise
inventory-promise-hold.description: Prevent duplicate stock promises with timed shared holds for one location.
inventory-promise-hold.detail: A small local-network web app for a shared SKU list: staff create a timed, visible soft hold with customer/order note; a supervisor converts, releases, or expires it; CSV export records the outcome. Non-goals: e-commerce storefronts, warehouse management, purchasing, accounting sync, or multi-warehouse forecasting.
inventory-promise-hold.user: A small distributor or reseller taking orders in parallel who needs to avoid promising the same scarce item twice while an order is still being entered.
inventory-promise-hold.distinct: It is the missing pre-save promise layer, not a clone of a storefront, POS, or full inventory system.
inventory-promise-hold.workaround: Tell staff to refresh inventory manually, save incomplete orders, write temporary reservations in chat/spreadsheets, or use a heavyweight ERP customization.

invoice-evidence-pack.title: Invoice Packet
invoice-evidence-pack.description: Build invoice packets, flag missing evidence, and export ZIP, PDF, or JSON backups of packets and templates.
invoice-evidence-pack.why: Build complete, verifiable invoice evidence packets privately in your browser.
invoice-evidence-pack.detail: Offline pack builder with configurable checklist templates, file hashes, missing-item flags, accountant notes, and ZIP/PDF manifest export. Non-goals: tax advice, filing submission, OCR extraction, or storing documents in a vendor cloud.
invoice-evidence-pack.user: Cross-border freelancers and tiny firms who need to assemble the exact invoice, work proof, payment proof, and accountant notes requested for a filing or client review.
invoice-evidence-pack.distinct: It organizes evidence around one business event instead of trying to replace bookkeeping or a chartered accountant.
invoice-evidence-pack.workaround: A folder per invoice, named PDFs, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc WhatsApp coordination with an accountant.

invoice-handoff-sheet.title: Invoice Handoff Sheet
invoice-handoff-sheet.description: Keep delivery proof, invoice details, payment instructions, and follow-ups in one client handoff.
invoice-handoff-sheet.why: Make a project handoff sheet with acceptance and payment details.
invoice-handoff-sheet.detail: A static-web generator for a signed project handoff page: milestones, acceptance links/files, invoice identifier, due date, payment instructions, and an exportable follow-up log. Non-goals: payment processing, automated collections, credit scoring, legal notices, or CRM.
invoice-handoff-sheet.user: Freelancers and small agencies who need a clear, non-confrontational record of what was delivered, invoiced, due, and followed up before a client payment becomes a dispute.
invoice-handoff-sheet.distinct: The core object is an auditable delivery-and-payment handoff, not another invoice generator or debt-collection bot.
invoice-handoff-sheet.workaround: Send an invoice PDF and follow-up emails, track milestones in a separate project tool, and manually reconstruct what the client received when payment is late.

invoice-send-ledger.title: Send-Date Ledger
invoice-send-ledger.description: Record client invoice send dates in one local record.
invoice-send-ledger.why: Record issued, sent, due, and paid dates for client invoices.
invoice-send-ledger.detail: Offline invoice issue register: import or enter a PDF/amount, record draft, issued, sent, due, and paid events, and export a monthly ledger. Non-goals: accounting ledger, tax calculation, or payment gateway.
invoice-send-ledger.user: Freelancers who draft an invoice while work evolves and need the issued date, due date, and sent version to remain unambiguous.
invoice-send-ledger.distinct: It is a chronology guardrail around existing invoices, not another invoice creator.
invoice-send-ledger.workaround: Edit dates by hand in an invoice app or duplicate a draft just before emailing it.

ios-review-gate.title: iOS Review Gate
ios-review-gate.description: Check an iOS archive and release plan, then print a Markdown review packet.
ios-review-gate.why: Check iOS release metadata, screenshots, privacy answers, and queue timing.
ios-review-gate.detail: CLI that reads an IPA/archive metadata export and release YAML, checks version/build consistency, screenshot/localization completeness, privacy-manifest declarations and produces a dated Markdown submission packet. Non-goals: submitting on a user's behalf, bypassing Apple review, analytics or release hosting.
ios-review-gate.user: Small iOS teams that need a local, reviewable release packet and realistic queue plan before submitting builds to App Review.
ios-review-gate.distinct: It is a release decision record and preflight gate, not another build-upload service.
ios-review-gate.workaround: Maintain a spreadsheet, inspect App Store Connect manually, and find missing metadata or wrong build numbers late in the submission.

journey-failure-receipts.title: Journey Failure Receipts
journey-failure-receipts.description: Capture failed Playwright assertions as scrubbed local HTML receipts.
journey-failure-receipts.why: Capture a scrubbed receipt when a Playwright soft assertion fails, before later test steps change the page.
journey-failure-receipts.detail: An npm Playwright reporter/helper that captures screenshot, selected DOM/accessibility snapshot, console errors, network summary, and masked form state at each configured soft assertion, then emits one static receipt per failure. Non-goals: hosted monitoring, test orchestration, or visual-regression replacement.
journey-failure-receipts.user: Teams using Playwright for critical user journeys who need the exact visual and DOM state at each failed soft assertion, not only the page state after the test finishes.
journey-failure-receipts.distinct: It improves the evidence granularity of existing browser tests instead of offering another synthetic-monitoring dashboard.
journey-failure-receipts.workaround: Capture a final trace/video, add ad-hoc screenshots around assertions, rerun a flaky flow interactively, or inspect a page that has already moved past the failure.

keyboard-route-check.title: Keyboard Route Check
keyboard-route-check.description: Record keyboard focus routes and export reports of possible focus problems.
keyboard-route-check.why: Record a keyboard route and export possible focus problems.
keyboard-route-check.detail: A browser extension that records a user-run Tab/Shift+Tab path, names each focused element, flags loops/skips/invisible focus, and exports a shareable route report. Non-goals: automatic WCAG certification, synthetic browser testing, or replacing manual testing.
keyboard-route-check.user: Keyboard-only users and small web teams who need to prove the route through an interactive page is coherent before it becomes a production accessibility defect.
keyboard-route-check.distinct: It turns a human keyboard journey into evidence, not another static lint wrapper.
keyboard-route-check.workaround: Manually tab through a page, run a generic accessibility scanner, or find the problem after keyboard users report it.

kid-code-missions.title: Kid Code Missions
kid-code-missions.description: Practice ordering instructions and fixing mistakes with short family missions.
kid-code-missions.why: Give children small coding missions to complete.
kid-code-missions.detail: Printable/PWA mission deck with one household-object challenge, one tiny browser simulation, and a parent prompt per mission; progress is local stickers only. Non-goals: chatbots, code generation, online communities, or a full coding curriculum.
kid-code-missions.user: Parents and tutors introducing ages 7–13 to programming who need short, interest-led missions that teach sequencing and debugging before syntax-heavy courses.
kid-code-missions.distinct: It is a compact facilitation tool for computational habits, not a clone of a block-programming environment or an AI coding tutor.
kid-code-missions.workaround: Start with Scratch, YouTube tutorials, worksheets, or prematurely jump into Python/AI tools.

kind-recall.title: Kind Recall
kind-recall.description: Offline PWA for 20–100 user-entered words: schedule short typed or spoken recall prompts in personal contexts, show a forgiving return queue after lapses, and r
kind-recall.detail: Offline PWA for 20–100 user-entered words: schedule short typed or spoken recall prompts in personal contexts, show a forgiving return queue after lapses, and record confidence separately from correctness. Non-goals: a language course, content marketplace, or chatbot.
kind-recall.user: An adult language learner who wants vocabulary to become usable in conversation without punitive streak mechanics.
kind-recall.distinct: It treats lapse recovery and context-rich production as the product, instead of adding gamification to flashcards.
kind-recall.workaround: Use Anki/Quizlet/Duolingo streaks, set reminders, and hope that repeated recognition becomes recall in real situations.

kitchen-table.title: Kitchen Table: ad-free, account-free classic family board games across phones in the same room or async
kitchen-table.description: Play three family board games on separate phones without accounts or ads.
kitchen-table.why: Play a pawn race, dots and boxes, or five dice on separate phones.
kitchen-table.detail: Room-code lobby; v1 ships three public-domain games with original art: a Parcheesi/Ludo-style race, a dots-and-boxes, and a simple dice-score game. Realtime when together, async when apart (push-free: the link re-opens the game state). Core loop: roll/place → next player → short game (10–20 min). Deliberately NOT: matchmaking with strangers, chat, ranking, cosmetics store.
kitchen-table.user: Couples and parents who want to play Ludo/Parcheesi-style or simple card-and-dice games with a partner or kids on separate phones without ads, IAP or tracking.
kitchen-table.distinct: Board Game Arena minus 99% of the catalogue and all the accounts; app-store family games minus the ads. The distinct promise is 'link, not app; family, not strangers'.
kitchen-table.workaround: Lichess (chess only), Polytopia, self-hosting hobby projects, or tolerating ads.

knowledge-boundary-map.title: Knowledge Boundary Map
knowledge-boundary-map.description: Map claims and prerequisites, then test explanations with a private 90-second teach-back.
knowledge-boundary-map.why: Test what you can explain with a private prerequisite map and 90-second teach-backs.
knowledge-boundary-map.detail: Static web app with a node map: add a claim and prerequisites, do a 90-second teach-back, then mark ‘explain’, ‘recognize’, or ‘blocked’ with a next probe. Non-goals: automatic truth checking, web scraping, and social feeds.
knowledge-boundary-map.user: A self-learner who has consumed a topic but needs to distinguish recognition from an explanation they can actually produce.
knowledge-boundary-map.distinct: It is an explicit boundary-and-prerequisite rehearsal surface, not another knowledge base or generic quiz generator.
knowledge-boundary-map.workaround: Keep an ever-growing notes system, reread material, or ask a friend/teacher to quiz them.

knowledge-handoff-bundle.title: Knowledge Handoff Bundle
knowledge-handoff-bundle.description: A CLI that turns a YAML checklist and local files/URLs into a static handoff site with manifest, link checks, ownership fields, expiry warnings, and a…
knowledge-handoff-bundle.why: Turn a YAML checklist into a verified project handoff.
knowledge-handoff-bundle.detail: A CLI that turns a YAML checklist and local files/URLs into a static handoff site with manifest, link checks, ownership fields, expiry warnings, and a recipient acknowledgement export. Non-goals: wiki hosting, crawling private systems, or AI summarization.
knowledge-handoff-bundle.user: A departing project owner or small team handing work to someone else who needs a durable, browseable package showing the current source of truth, linked files, and unresolved gaps.
knowledge-handoff-bundle.distinct: It is a portable, verifiable handoff artifact rather than another knowledge base.
knowledge-handoff-bundle.workaround: Send a wiki link collection, shared drive folder, and a free-form handover document; recipients discover expired links and absent context later.

knowledge-note-bridge.title: Knowledge Note Bridge
knowledge-note-bridge.description: A local Markdown-to-Anki bridge with stable card IDs, a dry-run diff, explicit archive/rename handling, and a reversible history-preservation report.…
knowledge-note-bridge.why: Preview and safely sync Markdown cards to Anki without losing review history.
knowledge-note-bridge.detail: A local Markdown-to-Anki bridge with stable card IDs, a dry-run diff, explicit archive/rename handling, and a reversible history-preservation report. Non-goals: a note-taking app, cloud sync service, or automatic card generation.
knowledge-note-bridge.user: Working self-learners who capture technical and business-domain knowledge in Markdown but need card updates without destroying existing review history.
knowledge-note-bridge.distinct: It is an integrity layer for learner-owned source notes and review history, not another Markdown flashcard syntax.
knowledge-note-bridge.workaround: Manually edit Anki, regenerate decks and lose history, or keep duplicate source material in notes and cards.

kube-permission-evidence.title: Kube Permission Evidence
kube-permission-evidence.description: A read-only CLI that collects RBAC objects, evaluates a bounded subject/resource matrix, and creates a Markdown/JSON evidence packet listing every binding and…
kube-permission-evidence.why: Trace Kubernetes access and export audit evidence.
kube-permission-evidence.detail: A read-only CLI that collects RBAC objects, evaluates a bounded subject/resource matrix, and creates a Markdown/JSON evidence packet listing every binding and rule that grants access. Non-goals: admission control, remediation, or cluster scanning as a service.
kube-permission-evidence.user: Kubernetes operators preparing audits or permission changes who need a readable proof of effective access without making cluster mutations.
kube-permission-evidence.distinct: The output is an auditor-readable causal proof of access, not another RBAC editor or policy framework.
kube-permission-evidence.workaround: Export RBAC YAML, inspect bindings manually, run scattered kubectl auth checks, and capture shell screenshots for auditors.

lan-family-dayboard.title: LAN Family Dayboard
lan-family-dayboard.description: Static web dayboard that reads manually imported ICS files or a user-run LAN feed, renders a big today/tomorrow view and chores, and prints a weekly sheet.…
lan-family-dayboard.why: Share local family calendars and chores without accounts.
lan-family-dayboard.detail: Static web dayboard that reads manually imported ICS files or a user-run LAN feed, renders a big today/tomorrow view and chores, and prints a weekly sheet. Non-goals: hosted calendar sync, messaging, contacts, or a proprietary display device.
lan-family-dayboard.user: A household that wants a shared tablet or e-ink display for today's events and responsibilities without creating cloud accounts for every family member.
lan-family-dayboard.distinct: It is a no-account ambient display, not a replacement cloud calendar or a family social network.
lan-family-dayboard.workaround: Share Google/Apple calendars, keep a paper calendar, or use a family-organizer subscription and deal with account invitations.

last-lap-breakout.title: Last Lap Breakout
last-lap-breakout.description: Finish an eight-minute Breakout run by choosing seven modifiers.
last-lap-breakout.why: Clear eight arcade laps and finish the run.
last-lap-breakout.detail: Eight fixed 60-second laps of paddle-and-orb play. After each lap choose one of three readable modifiers; lap eight is a designed boss and ends the run with a shareable build string. Non-goals: meta-progression, ads between laps, battle pass, or infinite survival.
last-lap-breakout.user: People on a short break who want a run-based action game they can finish in under ten minutes, with meaningful build choices but no endless grind.
last-lap-breakout.distinct: It commits to a visible eight-minute ending, rather than using roguelite upgrades to prolong a familiar arcade game indefinitely.
last-lap-breakout.workaround: Open a roguelite with a 30–60 minute commitment, play an unstructured arcade high-score game, or use a mobile app.

learning-objective-loop.title: Objective Loop
learning-objective-loop.description: Plan recall reviews around clear learning objectives.
learning-objective-loop.why: Plan recall reviews around learning objectives with an inspectable schedule.
learning-objective-loop.detail: Offline PWA where users enter objectives and evidence links, attach manually written short-answer prompts, log confidence/correctness, and see a simple explainable next-review queue. Non-goals: LLM card generation, content ingestion, or social feeds.
learning-objective-loop.user: A self-learner using AI and other materials who needs questions and review scheduling tied to stated learning objectives, rather than a generic chat history.
learning-objective-loop.distinct: It connects intentional objectives to recall evidence, instead of being a thin chat wrapper or another card generator.
learning-objective-loop.workaround: Ask a chatbot for quizzes, manually make Anki cards, or use course checklists that do not adapt to demonstrated recall.

led-layout-checker.title: LED Layout Checker
led-layout-checker.description: Plan LED paths, check current and power points, then export a labeled layout before soldering.
led-layout-checker.why: Plan LED strips, power, and data paths.
led-layout-checker.detail: Static planner: draw strips/pixels, set controller and supply locations, animate data direction, calculate approximate current per segment, flag missing injection assumptions, and export a labeled SVG. Non-goals: electrical certification, firmware flashing, mains-voltage advice, remote control.
led-layout-checker.user: Hobbyists planning a large addressable-LED art installation who need to sketch segments, trace data direction, and catch power-injection mistakes before buying or soldering.
led-layout-checker.distinct: It is a pre-build reasoning aid for creative LED art, not a WLED dashboard or generic circuit simulator.
led-layout-checker.workaround: Draw diagrams by hand, use spreadsheets, rely on community advice, and discover data direction or voltage drop while assembling.

legacy-app-rescue.title: Legacy App Rescue
legacy-app-rescue.description: Record APK evidence before an old Android device disappears.
legacy-app-rescue.why: Inventory old Android apps and save what you need before an upgrade.
legacy-app-rescue.detail: Desktop CLI that inventories user-supplied APKs and an attached Android device, records hashes/signers/SDK requirements, exports allowed app data where Android permits, and writes a reproducible preservation manifest. Non-goals: APK distribution, DRM removal, cracking, or re-signing third-party copyrighted apps.
legacy-app-rescue.user: A person preserving an old Android app or game they legally own who needs to inventory its package, save data, dependencies, and device compatibility without hunting untrusted APK sites.
legacy-app-rescue.distinct: It preserves evidence and migration options for software a user already has, rather than becoming an APK marketplace.
legacy-app-rescue.workaround: Users search random APK repositories, use old devices, make screenshots, and repeatedly retry signing/refresh tools.

lesson-code-room.title: Lesson Code Room
lesson-code-room.description: Run one shared coding exercise and see learner progress without student accounts.
lesson-code-room.why: Run a small HTML, CSS, or JavaScript exercise through one class link.
lesson-code-room.detail: Hosted room with a teacher-created HTML/CSS/JS exercise, one join link, browser sandbox, run/reset, and anonymous progress states. Non-goals: Java/C++ execution, grading, proctoring, repositories, or video conferencing.
lesson-code-room.user: Teachers and tutors running live remote coding lessons who need one low-setup shared exercise space with visible learner progress.
lesson-code-room.distinct: It intentionally solves the first ten minutes of a live lesson instead of recreating an IDE, LMS, or monitoring product.
lesson-code-room.workaround: Share Replit links, screen-share a local IDE, distribute files, or run separate video and coding tools.

lesson-tab-card.title: Lesson Tab Card
lesson-tab-card.description: Make a clear guitar lesson card during the lesson.
lesson-tab-card.why: Write guitar tab, check it, and print or share a playing card.
lesson-tab-card.detail: Static web editor with a keyboard-first mini syntax, six-string chord/grid preview, validation, printable PNG/SVG, and shareable encoded URL. Non-goals: copyrighted song libraries, full-score layout, playback, or user accounts.
lesson-tab-card.user: Guitar teachers and self-teaching players who need to type a quick, legible chord/scale handout during a lesson and share it as a compact card.
lesson-tab-card.distinct: It is deliberately a lesson handout format, not a replacement notation suite or a tab database.
lesson-tab-card.workaround: Draw diagrams by hand, fight a full notation editor, or paste plaintext tabs into chat/docs.

lift-receipt-log.title: Set Receipt
lift-receipt-log.description: Log lifts in this browser and keep workout receipts, even offline.
lift-receipt-log.why: Log a lifting set in one line and keep an offline workout receipt.
lift-receipt-log.detail: Offline PWA with a text grammar for sets (for example, 225x5), editable exercise aliases, rest timer, and a shareable/printable receipt containing volume, duration, and PRs. Non-goals: exercise video library, meal plans, social challenges, or AI coaching.
lift-receipt-log.user: Regular lifters who want to record a set as quickly as writing “225x5” in a notebook and retain a compact proof of the workout.
lift-receipt-log.distinct: The product is an ultra-fast immutable workout receipt, not a broad fitness platform.
lift-receipt-log.workaround: Paper notebooks, Notes, spreadsheets, or feature-heavy trackers with paywalls and feeds.

limited-night-planner.title: Limited Night Planner
limited-night-planner.description: Plan pools and rounds from mixed tabletop components.
limited-night-planner.why: Plan a tabletop event with pools, seating, a timer, and a host sheet.
limited-night-planner.detail: Offline PWA with inventory counts, player count, pack/pool assumptions, round timer, seating rotation, and printable host sheet; users write their own compatibility notes. Non-goals: official rules text, card database, matchmaking, or online play.
limited-night-planner.user: Hosts running a casual limited card or tabletop event from a mixed personal collection who need to turn uncertain inventory into a fair, timed, low-friction night.
limited-night-planner.distinct: It plans the physical event from uncertain inventory; it is not another rules wiki, bracket site, or virtual tabletop.
limited-night-planner.workaround: Use a spreadsheet, count components by hand, search rules/forums, and improvise seating, rounds, and timers during the event.

line-take-match.title: Line Take Match
line-take-match.description: Compare recorded voice takes with an approved take in your browser.
line-take-match.why: Compare recorded character lines with an approved voice take. Audio stays on your device.
line-take-match.detail: A local web app that imports creator-owned WAV/MP3 takes, groups them by line, shows loudness, duration, pause, and pitch-range comparison against a selected approved take, and exports a handoff CSV. Non-goals: speech generation, voice cloning, transcription service, or cloud hosting.
line-take-match.user: Indie animators and game creators recording character lines who need to compare takes for level, pace, and emotional consistency without cloning anyone’s voice.
line-take-match.distinct: It improves human creative direction and take selection without being a thin generative-voice wrapper.
line-take-match.workaround: Keep naming conventions and notes, compare waveforms in a DAW, normalize manually, then discover level or pace mismatches in the edit.

linux-kid-lab.title: Linux Kid Lab
linux-kid-lab.description: Pick 20 short creative activities for children on a family Linux computer.
linux-kid-lab.why: Pick 20 short creative activities for children, save progress locally, and keep making offline.
linux-kid-lab.detail: A local-first web launcher with 20 short open activities, parent-selected age bands, no ads, printable progress tokens, and links to installed tools. Non-goals: child profiles in the cloud, surveillance analytics, a replacement curriculum.
linux-kid-lab.user: Parents using Linux who need a calm, age-progressive set of local creative activities after a child outgrows a first educational app.
linux-kid-lab.distinct: Curation and progression across open tools is the product, not another worksheet game.
linux-kid-lab.workaround: Install GCompris, Scratch, browser games, and separate art tools individually, then curate them manually.

linux-learning-station.title: Linux Learning Station
linux-learning-station.description: Start six private offline activities for ages 5–10 on a shared Linux computer; progress stays in the browser.
linux-learning-station.why: Run six offline learning activities for children aged 5–10.
linux-learning-station.detail: Installable offline PWA with six original, local mini-activities (patterns, keyboarding, logic, spelling, number sense, creative drawing), parent-configured age bands, and printable progress code. Non-goals: a content marketplace, cloud profiles, and licensed game aggregation.
linux-learning-station.user: A parent or teacher setting up an older shared Linux computer for 5–10-year-olds who needs offline, age-progressive learning activities without accounts.
linux-learning-station.distinct: It solves local deployment and age progression with original micro-activities rather than cloning a commercial kids’ platform.
linux-learning-station.workaround: Install assorted apps one by one, rely on browser sites, or default to GCompris past its intended level.

listen-back-reader.title: Listen Back Reader
listen-back-reader.description: Replay web sentences one at a time to keep your place.
listen-back-reader.why: Listen to selected articles one sentence at a time in your browser.
listen-back-reader.detail: A privacy-first browser extension that extracts the selected article, speaks one sentence at a time with replay/slow/skip controls, and follows the sentence with a high-visibility focus marker. Non-goals: text rewriting, dyslexia diagnosis, voice cloning, accounts, or cloud text upload.
listen-back-reader.user: Dyslexic readers and people with cognitive fatigue who need a source-faithful read-aloud loop for dense web text without losing their place.
listen-back-reader.distinct: It is a source-anchored retention aid, not another generic text-to-speech reader or an LLM simplifier.
listen-back-reader.workaround: Use browser read-aloud, copy text to a TTS app, or repeatedly restart a paragraph after losing place.

live-figure-deck.title: Live Figure Deck
live-figure-deck.description: A static web editor with formula labels, a 2D plot, parameter sliders, named animation intervals, and export to a self-contained HTML slide or MP4-ready frame…
live-figure-deck.why: Build one clear, formula-driven animated figure and export it as a self-contained slide.
live-figure-deck.detail: A static web editor with formula labels, a 2D plot, parameter sliders, named animation intervals, and export to a self-contained HTML slide or MP4-ready frame sequence. Non-goals: general slideware, CAS, AI lesson authoring, or hosted collaboration.
live-figure-deck.user: Scientists and educators who need a few formula-driven, animated explanatory figures in a talk without adopting a full animation pipeline.
live-figure-deck.distinct: It sits between static charts and a full animation/code studio, optimized for one explainable figure.
live-figure-deck.workaround: Use Beamer/TikZ, hand-code D3 or p5, export a Manim movie, or paste a static image into slides.

living-room-lobby.title: Living Room Lobby: party games for a smart-TV browser where kids without phones and non-English relatives can still play
living-room-lobby.description: Play phone-optional family games on one shared TV.
living-room-lobby.why: Host language-light party games on a TV for people in the same room.
living-room-lobby.detail: Host URL opens on a smart-TV browser (or any screen) with a QR code; games are language-light: a co-op pictionary where the TV shows the drawing, a 'point at the TV' reaction game via phone tilt, and a hot-seat 'pass the phone' guessing round so a 5-year-old can play with a parent's phone. Low-CPU canvas rendering, D-pad-navigable host UI. Deliberately NOT: dozens of games, user-generated packs, remote/online play, voice chat.
living-room-lobby.user: Multi-generational families at holidays who want a Jackbox-style night but have no HDMI PC, kids too young for phones, and relatives whose first language isn't English.
living-room-lobby.distinct: Every incumbent assumes a PC host and one phone per player; this designs for the TV browser and the phone-less kid, and picks language-light mechanics on purpose.
living-room-lobby.workaround: Laptop + HDMI, Jackbox packs ($30 each, phones required, English-centric), AirConsole (subscription), kids watch instead of play.

local-caption-tape.title: Local Caption Tape
local-caption-tape.description: A local desktop app that captions selected system/microphone audio, keeps a rolling encrypted transcript, and exports timestamped Markdown/TXT when explicitly s
local-caption-tape.detail: A local desktop app that captions selected system/microphone audio, keeps a rolling encrypted transcript, and exports timestamped Markdown/TXT when explicitly saved. Non-goals: recording bystanders without consent, automatic meeting joining, cloud summaries, or behavioral analytics.
local-caption-tape.user: Deaf, hard-of-hearing, and attention-variable professionals who need an immediately searchable, private transcript of their own meetings without surrendering recordings to a SaaS notetaker.
local-caption-tape.distinct: The product is a private, ephemeral caption memory rather than an AI meeting-minutes wrapper.
local-caption-tape.workaround: Use Zoom/Meet captions, a cloud meeting bot, manual notes, or vendor-bound transcript exports.

local-data-finder.title: Local Data Finder
local-data-finder.description: Find source records in selected local notes and exports without uploading your archive.
local-data-finder.detail: Local desktop indexer for selected folders and explicit exports (Markdown, HTML, mbox, PDF text), with lexical search, filters, and every result linked to a local source path and extraction timestamp. Non-goals: cloud connectors, LLM chat, surveillance, or automatic deletion.
local-data-finder.user: Professionals with years of notes, correspondence, code, and documents spread across folders and exports who need private cross-source retrieval with an inspectable source trail.
local-data-finder.distinct: It prioritizes private source-grounded recall over an opaque AI layer or another note-taking system.
local-data-finder.workaround: Search each cloud/service separately, manually export archives, or send an entire personal corpus to a hosted AI service.

local-data-workbench.title: Local Data Workbench
local-data-workbench.description: Signed desktop app opening CSV/JSON/Parquet locally, profiling columns, applying named filters/joins/transforms, and saving a portable recipe plus output. Non-g
local-data-workbench.detail: Signed desktop app opening CSV/JSON/Parquet locally, profiling columns, applying named filters/joins/transforms, and saving a portable recipe plus output. Non-goals: cloud warehouse, collaboration, or AI-generated queries.
local-data-workbench.user: Analysts and engineers who need to inspect or reshape a multi-GB CSV, JSON, or Parquet file without uploading it or writing a one-off script.
local-data-workbench.distinct: The durable artifact is a portable local transformation recipe, not another SQL IDE or web spreadsheet.
local-data-workbench.workaround: Upload a sample to a SaaS, use spreadsheets until they fail, or assemble Python/DuckDB commands ad hoc.

local-file-triage.title: Triagebox
local-file-triage.description: Organize a local folder after reviewing every proposed move.
local-file-triage.why: Sort local files into a plan for review.
local-file-triage.detail: Desktop-local app that inventories one folder, proposes deterministic buckets from filename/type/date/metadata, shows every planned rename/move, executes only approved rows, and writes an undo manifest. Non-goals: cloud sync, generative tagging, or replacing DAM systems.
local-file-triage.user: A privacy-conscious person with a messy 1k–10k-file folder who needs to classify it safely without uploading it or letting an opaque tool move files unchecked.
local-file-triage.distinct: It is a reversible file-handoff utility, not an AI auto-organizer: deterministic proposals and an undo receipt are the product.
local-file-triage.workaround: Manual folder sorting, Finder/Explorer search, brittle scripts, or moving a copy into a photo server.

local-finance-export-vault.title: Local Finance Export Vault
local-finance-export-vault.description: Preserve budget exports and build a migration packet in your browser.
local-finance-export-vault.why: Archive budget exports with a clear record of fields.
local-finance-export-vault.detail: Offline vault that imports common budget exports, snapshots an immutable manifest and hashes, maps fields into a documented neutral schema, and produces a readable migration packet. Non-goals: account aggregation, spending advice, bank connectivity, or multi-user cloud sync.
local-finance-export-vault.user: Privacy-minded individuals moving between budgeting tools who need to preserve and inspect their own financial exports before an app, pricing tier, or sync service changes.
local-finance-export-vault.distinct: It protects an exit-ready personal data archive rather than competing to be the user's finance dashboard.
local-finance-export-vault.workaround: Export CSVs into ad-hoc folders, trust a vendor export, or flatten data into a spreadsheet and lose categories, accounts, and reconciliation metadata.

local-model-residency.title: Local Model Residency
local-model-residency.description: Menu-bar/tray app that reads supported local-runtime status endpoints and OS process metrics, shows model load owner, GPU/RAM footprint, reload events and a saf
local-model-residency.detail: Menu-bar/tray app that reads supported local-runtime status endpoints and OS process metrics, shows model load owner, GPU/RAM footprint, reload events and a safe copyable diagnostic bundle. Non-goals: model download, prompt logging, model serving, chat UI or cloud inference.
local-model-residency.user: Privacy-conscious desktop users who run local models but need a plain explanation of model memory residency, unload/reload churn and which local client is consuming GPU/RAM.
local-model-residency.distinct: It makes local-model resource behavior understandable without becoming another model launcher or chat client.
local-model-residency.workaround: Watch Activity Monitor/nvidia-smi, guess at keep-alive settings, or restart clients when a model becomes slow.

local-pdf-forms-signer.title: Browser-local PDF form builder, filler, signer and page editor
local-pdf-forms-signer.description: Fill, sign, and arrange PDFs on your device without uploading files.
local-pdf-forms-signer.why: Fill, sign, add fields, and arrange PDFs on your device without uploading a file.
local-pdf-forms-signer.detail: Static page using pdf-lib/pdf.js: open a PDF, drag text/checkbox/date fields onto pages, fill existing AcroForm fields, draw or type a signature, delete/reorder/rotate pages, then export (optionally flattened). All processing in the browser tab. Deliberately no OCR, no text editing of existing content, no cloud storage, no e-signature legal workflow/audit trail, no DOCX conversion.
local-pdf-forms-signer.user: Individuals and small-office staff who receive PDFs to fill/sign or need to add fillable fields and remove/reorder pages, without an Acrobat Pro licence and without uploading confidential documents to a cloud converter.
local-pdf-forms-signer.distinct: Combines field creation + fill + sign + page ops locally; existing free tools do at most two of those, and the free ones that do more require upload or a server.
local-pdf-forms-signer.workaround: Acrobat Pro subscription; uploading to iLovePDF/Smallpdf; self-hosting Stirling-PDF (needs a server); CLI qpdf/pdftk for page ops; macOS Preview for signing only.

local-records-continuity.title: Continuity Pack
local-records-continuity.description: Build and test encrypted recovery packs for local business records.
local-records-continuity.why: Build encrypted recovery packs for records from self-hosted or local business software, then verify.
local-records-continuity.detail: Local CLI that packages configured export files, hashes and encrypts them, writes a plain-language restore manifest, verifies a target copy, and runs a scheduled dry-read. Non-goals: hosted backup storage, database administration, or vendor-specific restore automation.
local-records-continuity.user: Small businesses using self-hosted or local admin software who need a tested, readable recovery pack for invoices, customers, and business records.
local-records-continuity.distinct: It turns disparate exports into a tested recovery handoff, rather than becoming another backup provider.
local-records-continuity.workaround: Occasional database dump, a cloud-folder copy, or a hosting-provider backup with no documented restore check.

local-sync-observer.title: Local Sync Observer
local-sync-observer.description: Check Syncthing and Nextcloud sync status after offline work without opening files.
local-sync-observer.detail: A local tray app that consumes opt-in read-only status APIs/logs from Syncthing and selected folder sync tools, shows pending/conflict/last-good state, and opens the owning tool for fixes. Non-goals: becoming a sync engine, modifying data, or cloud monitoring.
local-sync-observer.user: Users running local-first mobile and desktop stacks who need one truthful, non-destructive view of whether their folders and devices have actually converged.
local-sync-observer.distinct: It observes and explains convergence across tools rather than competing as yet another sync service.
local-sync-observer.workaround: Open each product's web UI, inspect logs, compare folder timestamps, and wait after reconnecting.

lockfile-age-audit.title: Cross-ecosystem lockfile release-age auditor and CI gate
lockfile-age-audit.description: Audit every locked release date and hold CI when direct or transitive dependencies are too new.
lockfile-age-audit.why: Audit the release age of direct and transitive dependencies already resolved in eight lockfile formats.

log-drain-contract-check.title: Drain Check
log-drain-contract-check.description: Check local log drains for volume, field paths, and sensitive data before forwarding.
log-drain-contract-check.why: Check a bounded local log drain sample before forwarding it.
log-drain-contract-check.detail: A local receiver that accepts a 10-minute drain sample, reports event rate/field types/likely secrets, and generates a forwarding configuration plus retention estimate. Non-goals: long-term log storage, alerting, or log search.
log-drain-contract-check.user: Small platform teams adding managed log drains who need to know a drain's volume, fields, and privacy risk before turning it on continuously.
log-drain-contract-check.distinct: It validates a logging connection before commitment instead of competing as a log destination.
log-drain-contract-check.workaround: Enable a drain, inspect a vendor UI after the fact, estimate costs from provider docs, and manually discover sensitive fields.

log-duplicate-lens.title: Log Duplicate Lens
log-duplicate-lens.description: Find duplicate Loki logs across streams before they inflate alert counts and storage.
log-duplicate-lens.why: Find duplicate Loki logs across streams before they inflate alerts and storage.
log-duplicate-lens.detail: A CLI that samples Loki JSON exports or newline-delimited logs, fingerprints messages with configurable timestamp tolerance, groups cross-stream near-duplicates, estimates volume/alert inflation, and emits label/retry evidence. log-duplicate-lens.user: Operators of Loki or JSON log pipelines who need to quantify accidental duplicate ingestion across streams before it distorts search results, alert counts, and storage cost.
log-duplicate-lens.distinct: It diagnoses a specific amplification failure mode in an existing log stack, rather than becoming another log platform or dashboard.
log-duplicate-lens.workaround: Manually search log windows, infer duplicates from message text, adjust labels/retries, or accept inflated volume and noisy alerts.

log-incident-bundle.title: Log Incident Bundle
log-incident-bundle.description: Create a redacted incident review from logs.
log-incident-bundle.why: Pack selected logs for an incident review.
log-incident-bundle.detail: CLI accepts stdin/files or a deliberately supplied export, time-bounds and correlates records, applies local redaction rules, and emits a self-contained searchable HTML bundle with provenance. Non-goals: log ingestion, live tailing, alerting, retention, or hosted search.
log-incident-bundle.user: A small team debugging an event or service incident that needs to hand a bounded, searchable, redacted slice of logs to a teammate without buying or operating a full logging SaaS.
log-incident-bundle.distinct: It produces an incident-review artifact rather than another log backend, dashboard, or tail viewer.
log-incident-bundle.workaround: grep locally, paste snippets into chat, pay for a logging SaaS, or grant another engineer broad production-log access.

log-scrub-contract.title: Log Scrub Contract
log-scrub-contract.description: A local CLI with JSON/text fixture tests, path/regex/token rules, entropy checks, and a redacted before/after report that can gate CI. Non-goals: collecting…

log-scrub-contract.user: Security-conscious developers forwarding structured logs who need regression-tested proof that configured secrets and personal data are removed before a drain or support bundle leaves their environment.
log-scrub-contract.distinct: It verifies redaction behavior over time instead of being another log viewer or drain.
log-scrub-contract.workaround: Use regexes in a logging library, manually inspect support attachments, or trust vendor-side scrubbing after data has already left the service.

long-markdown-pdf-check.title: Longform PDF Check
long-markdown-pdf-check.description: CLI plus local HTML report that accepts Markdown and a generated PDF, checks heading/TOC targets, internal and external links, code-block overflow, empty…
long-markdown-pdf-check.why: Catch broken links, bookmarks, overflow, blank pages, drift, and metadata before you deliver a long PDF.
long-markdown-pdf-check.detail: CLI plus local HTML report that accepts Markdown and a generated PDF, checks heading/TOC targets, internal and external links, code-block overflow, empty pages, page-count drift, and selected metadata. Non-goals: a Markdown editor or proprietary typesetting engine.
long-markdown-pdf-check.user: Technical writers and consultants exporting long Markdown reports who need a PDF whose table of contents, code blocks, links, page breaks, and metadata survive conversion.
long-markdown-pdf-check.distinct: It is a delivery preflight for generated documents, not a new Markdown-to-PDF converter.
long-markdown-pdf-check.workaround: Trial multiple Pandoc/LaTeX themes, visually inspect dozens of pages, and hand-fix PDF metadata or broken links.

loop-lab.title: Loop Lab
loop-lab.description: Turn a short audio clip into a repeatable practice loop.

loop-lab.user: Beginning electronic-music makers who need to turn a short reference passage into a repeatable, hands-on practice loop without first learning a DAW.
loop-lab.distinct: It is a practice instrument, not another DAW or streaming service.
loop-lab.workaround: Scrub YouTube or a DAW manually, set loop markers, and separately note tempo and observations.

loudness-lens.title: Loudness Lens
loudness-lens.description: Limit sudden peaks in the tab you enable.
loudness-lens.why: See loudness information while playing audio online.
loudness-lens.detail: Browser extension with an explicit enable switch per tab, short look-ahead limiter, gain target, peak/loudness meter, and a panic mute. Non-goals: DRM bypass, recording, background audio interception.
loudness-lens.user: People watching mixed web video, lessons, and music who need a predictable listening level without buying inline audio hardware.
loudness-lens.distinct: A safety control with a meter and per-tab consent, rather than a generic equalizer skin.
loudness-lens.workaround: Ride the system volume, use VLC normalization for files, or buy a compressor/limiter device.

low-motion-profile-switcher.title: Low Motion Profile Switcher
low-motion-profile-switcher.description: A browser extension that applies per-site low-motion profiles: pause nonessential autoplay/animated backgrounds, suppress rapid transforms, retain explicit…
low-motion-profile-switcher.why: Choose a low-motion profile for each website without hiding useful progress and status feedback.
low-motion-profile-switcher.detail: A browser extension that applies per-site low-motion profiles: pause nonessential autoplay/animated backgrounds, suppress rapid transforms, retain explicit progress/status changes, and offer a one-click temporary exception. low-motion-profile-switcher.user: A motion-sensitive computer user who needs a reliable way to reduce distracting or nauseating animation in selected apps and browser tabs without losing useful state changes.
low-motion-profile-switcher.distinct: It is a selective, reversible motion policy layer rather than a global animation kill switch.
low-motion-profile-switcher.workaround: Change global OS settings, hunt through each app’s preferences, abandon a tab, or tolerate the effect because turning off all animation loses helpful feedback.

low-vision-workspace-profiles.title: Workspace Profiles
low-vision-workspace-profiles.description: Save text size, spacing, color, and focus settings for each work site.
low-vision-workspace-profiles.why: Save a readable text, spacing, color, cursor, and focus profile for each work site.
low-vision-workspace-profiles.detail: A browser extension with named profiles per domain: independent text scale, line spacing, contrast, cursor halo and a hotkey to temporarily magnify the focused region. Non-goals: changing employer documents, remote-desktop capture, screen-reader replacement or collecting browsing analytics.
low-vision-workspace-profiles.user: A knowledge worker with declining vision who needs Office, docs, dashboards and browser apps to become readable without losing context every time zoom changes.
low-vision-workspace-profiles.distinct: It treats readable work as a profile of several reversible controls rather than assuming that enlarging every pixel is enough.
low-vision-workspace-profiles.workaround: Use browser zoom, OS magnification, inverted contrast and large fonts, then repeatedly reconfigure sites and lose layout context.

mail-attachment-archive.title: Mail Attachment Archive
mail-attachment-archive.description: Archive MBOX attachments locally, remove duplicates, and record every failure in a verification report.
mail-attachment-archive.why: Index email attachments locally, remove duplicates, and find missing archive files.
mail-attachment-archive.detail: Local desktop app that imports MBOX/IMAP exports, hashes and deduplicates attachments, creates a browsable offline index, and produces a missing/corrupt-item report. Non-goals: hosted email, inbox replacement, or automated deletion from providers.
mail-attachment-archive.user: People leaving or backing up an email account who need a local, deduplicated archive of messages and attachments with evidence that nothing was silently omitted.
mail-attachment-archive.distinct: It verifies attachment integrity and retrievability, rather than merely downloading a mailbox blob.
mail-attachment-archive.workaround: Google Takeout, IMAP export, mail-client folders, or manual download of important attachments.

maintenance-proof-book.title: Maintenance Proof Book
maintenance-proof-book.description: Offline property timeline with repair cards, receipt/photo attachment, part/vendor fields, next-due date, and a single PDF export. Non-goals: contractor…

maintenance-proof-book.detail: Offline property timeline with repair cards, receipt/photo attachment, part/vendor fields, next-due date, and a single PDF export. Non-goals: contractor marketplace, quote prediction, property management, cloud document storage.
