maintenance-proof-book.distinct: A repair record that proves and schedules a decision, rather than a generic task list or contractor lead-gen funnel.
maintenance-proof-book.workaround: Keep a folder of receipts, photos in a camera roll, and future reminders in a calendar with no shared object history.

manuscript-entity-indexer.title: Manuscript Entity Indexer
manuscript-entity-indexer.description: Review manuscript names across multilingual drafts without uploading them.

Non-goals: text generation, training on manuscripts, cloud collaboration or literary judgment.
manuscript-entity-indexer.user: Novelists writing multilingual manuscripts who need a local, lightweight character/place/alias ledger and continuity search without uploading drafts or shipping a giant model.

manuscript-entity-indexer.workaround: Maintain a manual story bible, search chapters by hand, use cloud writing assistants, or attach a large local model to every edit.

markdown-pdf-code-proof.title: Code Proof
markdown-pdf-code-proof.description: Catch code, page overflow, and link defects before releasing a Markdown PDF.
markdown-pdf-code-proof.why: Check a finished Markdown PDF for broken code, page overflow, and internal links before release.
markdown-pdf-code-proof.detail: A local CLI that renders Markdown through a chosen engine, checks PDF annotations and page geometry, flags overflowing/unhighlighted fenced blocks, and emits an HTML proof sheet. Non-goals: a Markdown editor, hosted conversion, or a replacement renderer.
markdown-pdf-code-proof.user: Engineers and technical writers producing long Markdown manuals who need to catch broken code blocks, wrapping, and internal links in the final PDF.
markdown-pdf-code-proof.distinct: The product verifies a PDF delivery contract instead of adding a competing Markdown-to-PDF renderer.
markdown-pdf-code-proof.workaround: Try several converters, tune LaTeX/print CSS by hand, and visually page through PDFs before release.

math-circle-board.title: Math Circle Board
math-circle-board.description: Record partial learner attempts, private notes, and printable recaps for a small math circle.
math-circle-board.why: Run a small math group with problem cards, attempts, and facilitator notes.
math-circle-board.detail: A small-group web app with weekly problem cards, student photo/text attempt uploads, private facilitator notes, tags for strategies tried, and printable session recap. Non-goals: public child social network, adaptive test prep, video calling, or high-stakes grading.
math-circle-board.user: A volunteer running a small enrichment math circle who needs to sequence open-ended problems, see partial attempts, and preserve a lightweight learning record for a handful of students.
math-circle-board.distinct: It records exploratory mathematical thinking and group continuity, not marks, video meetings, or a generic LMS clone.
math-circle-board.workaround: Email PDFs, shared documents, group chat, and a spreadsheet that cannot represent partial strategies or lesson flow.

math-textbook-margins.title: Math Textbook Margins
math-textbook-margins.description: Static web lesson wrapper: teacher supplies page links/owned excerpts and adds prediction, worked-step, and misconception prompts; students export a one-page…
math-textbook-margins.why: Put a prediction, a worked step, and one check beside any math reading.
math-textbook-margins.detail: Static web lesson wrapper: teacher supplies page links/owned excerpts and adds prediction, worked-step, and misconception prompts; students export a one-page answer record. Non-goals: textbook hosting, OCR of copyrighted PDFs, adaptive AI, or a full LMS.
math-textbook-margins.user: A math teacher using an interactive or PDF-based text who needs students to make predictions, sketch a step, and answer one check before receiving the next explanation.
math-textbook-margins.distinct: It adds active-recall margins around materials a teacher already has, instead of competing as another math content subscription.
math-textbook-margins.workaround: Assign textbook/PDF pages, add separate worksheets or LMS quizzes, and rely on students to self-check after seeing worked solutions.

math-tooling-notebook.title: Math Tooling Notebook
math-tooling-notebook.description: Static web notebook with 20 tool-literacy drills, an embedded function plotter, scratchpad, estimation reveal, and local progress. Non-goals: a CAS, full…
math-tooling-notebook.why: Learn when to estimate, table, graph, and verify through 20 hands-on mathematics drills.
math-tooling-notebook.detail: Static web notebook with 20 tool-literacy drills, an embedded function plotter, scratchpad, estimation reveal, and local progress. Non-goals: a CAS, full curriculum, adaptive AI tutor, or graded certificates.
math-tooling-notebook.user: An adult returning to mathematics who needs hands-on fluency with graphs, symbolic notation, estimates, and checks before tackling a formal course.
math-tooling-notebook.distinct: It teaches the workflow around math tools rather than competing as a graphing calculator or a content course.
math-tooling-notebook.workaround: Bounce among Desmos, WolframAlpha, calculators, videos, and paper notes without a guided tool-literacy sequence.

mbox-takeout-viewer.title: Streamed, in-browser viewer/search/extractor for multi-GB Gmail Takeout .mbox files
mbox-takeout-viewer.description: Search Gmail Takeout archives in your browser, then read and export the emails you need.
mbox-takeout-viewer.why: Search a Gmail Takeout archive in your browser. Read messages and export selected emails.
mbox-takeout-viewer.detail: Static PWA: open .mbox (or .mbox.gz) via streamed reads; build header index (from/to/date/subject/size) with progress; search/filter; render message (MIME decode, safe HTML sanitised); download attachments; export selection as EML ZIP. No import into a mail client, no send/reply, no cloud, no AI summarisation.
mbox-takeout-viewer.user: People who exported Gmail via Takeout (account closure, backup, legal/records) and are stuck with a 10–50 GB .mbox that nothing opens; job: search, read and pull out messages/attachments without Thunderbird or a paid converter.
mbox-takeout-viewer.distinct: All current options are desktop installs or paid converters; streaming + indexing in the browser makes a 50 GB export usable with no install and no trust in a vendor.
mbox-takeout-viewer.workaround: Thunderbird + ImportExportTools NG (slow on huge files), mboxShell terminal tool, paid SysTools/Mbox Viewer converters, Python mailbox scripts.

mcp-result-envelope.title: Result Envelope
mcp-result-envelope.description: Pack large MCP and CLI results into capped pages with summaries and schemas.
mcp-result-envelope.why: Pack tool results into summaries, schemas, and stable pages.
mcp-result-envelope.detail: An npm library and CLI that turns rows/JSON into a manifest, compact summary, schema, stable page cursors, and optional streamed chunks; it includes a local inspector. Non-goals: model calls, RAG, or database hosting.
mcp-result-envelope.user: MCP and CLI tool authors who need to return large structured results to models without silently truncating, over-tokenizing, or hiding the useful rows.
mcp-result-envelope.distinct: It is transport/representation infrastructure, not a thin LLM summary wrapper.
mcp-result-envelope.workaround: Dump JSON/CSV into a prompt, hand-write summaries, paginate ad hoc, or make the model issue repeated query calls.

meal-list-boundaries.title: Meal List Boundaries
meal-list-boundaries.description: A local-first weekly board that assigns each meal and ingredient to a named household/list, generates separate printable or shareable lists, and records a simpl

meal-list-boundaries.user: A household planning meals for more than one home or pickup context who needs a weekly menu to produce the right shopping list without leaking one household's items into another.
meal-list-boundaries.distinct: The primary object is a boundary-aware handoff from plan to the right buyer, not a generic recipe manager.
meal-list-boundaries.workaround: Duplicate recipes/lists, manually deselect items, or maintain separate chats and shopping apps per household.

meal-plan-pantry-check.title: Meal Plan Pantry Check

meal-plan-pantry-check.distinct: It is an explainable pantry-confirmed list builder, not a recipe-content app or a thin prompt around meal planning.
meal-plan-pantry-check.workaround: Copy ingredients into Notes, use an LLM-generated list, or maintain a heavyweight recipe server and manually resolve quantities.

mechanism-playground.distinct: It centers recognisable mechanical movements as playful building vocabulary, not an open-ended physics clone or an engineering CAD package.

med-handoff-card.title: Med Handoff Card

med-handoff-card.distinct: It is a caregiver handoff and exception log, not another reminder app or pill-dispenser marketplace.
med-handoff-card.workaround: Paper charts, a spreadsheet/Numbers checklist, pill boxes, text messages, or a pharmacy blister pack.

media-fidelity-audit.title: Media Fidelity Audit

media-fidelity-audit.detail: Local CLI/desktop app that compares a camera export or mounted source to an archive, reports byte/hash matches plus codec, frame rate, EXIF, Live Photo pairing, and missing originals, then writes a portable manifest. media-fidelity-audit.user: Families and photographers self-hosting a photo library who need proof that originals—not flattened or altered derivatives—made it into the archive.
media-fidelity-audit.distinct: It protects original-media fidelity across tools instead of being another photo-library clone.
media-fidelity-audit.workaround: Trust the photo-library UI, retain a second unverified copy, or compare filenames and sizes manually after an import.

medication-handoff-card.title: Medication Handoff Card

medication-handoff-card.user: Adult children and caregivers coordinating an older relative's medication list who need to record changes and hand a clear, dated list to family and clinicians.
medication-handoff-card.distinct: It improves human handoffs and accountability around a list, rather than becoming a medication-adherence or telehealth platform.
medication-handoff-card.workaround: Shared documents, a paper list, pill organizers, or an app that only the patient controls.

meeting-recall-markers.title: Meeting Recall Markers
meeting-recall-markers.description: Offline PWA with three giant keyboard/touch markers and an optional 10-second personal voice note; it outputs a chronological recall card. Non-goals: meeting…
meeting-recall-markers.why: Mark decisions, actions, and topics to revisit during meetings, then review a private recall card.
meeting-recall-markers.detail: Offline PWA with three giant keyboard/touch markers and an optional 10-second personal voice note; it outputs a chronological recall card. Non-goals: meeting recording, speaker diarization, calendar integration, or AI summaries.
meeting-recall-markers.user: Professionals with ADHD who lose the thread during meetings and need a private, low-effort way to reconstruct decisions and follow-ups afterward.
meeting-recall-markers.distinct: It captures attention anchors, not a surveillance-style transcript of everyone in the room.
meeting-recall-markers.workaround: Take unstructured notes, record the whole meeting, ask a colleague afterward, or use a bot-based meeting transcription product.

message-archive-audit.distinct: It verifies and documents exports people already obtain; it is not a cloud backup service or a platform scraper.

midi-practice-sandbox.user: Piano teachers and hobbyists using browser exercises who need a five-minute, no-account way to verify that a MIDI keyboard, browser permissions, sound, and note mapping all work before a lesson.
midi-practice-sandbox.distinct: The unit of value is a comprehensible setup diagnosis, not a piano-learning course or virtual instrument.
midi-practice-sandbox.workaround: Open a lesson site, guess which browser/device setting failed, install a DAW, or ask a teacher to troubleshoot live.

midi-theory-lens.title: MIDI Theory Lens
midi-theory-lens.description: See intervals, scales, and chord suggestions as you play.
midi-theory-lens.why: Play MIDI notes and see their intervals and likely chord quality.
midi-theory-lens.detail: A browser MIDI keyboard/fretboard view with a selected tonic, live interval labels, chord-quality guess, and a local replay trail. Non-goals: automatic composition, score transcription, user profiles, or course content.
midi-theory-lens.user: Music learners with a MIDI controller who want an immediate visual explanation of intervals, scales, and chord changes while they play their own notes.
midi-theory-lens.distinct: It is an explanatory instrument for a learner's own improvisation, not a gamified course or an AI music generator.
midi-theory-lens.workaround: Keep a circle-of-fifths chart open, use a piano visualiser that ignores key context, or buy a course with fixed exercises.

migration-commit-witness.title: Migration Commit Witness

migration-commit-witness.detail: A CI CLI that runs an existing migration command against a disposable database, snapshots selected schema/data invariants before and after commit, optionally runs a supplied rollback, and emits a signed Markdown/JSON witness. Non-goals: generating migrations, replacing a migration engine, or touching production databases.
migration-commit-witness.user: Backend teams reviewing SQL migrations who need a concrete record of what committed, what rolled back, and which rollback claim was actually exercised before production.
migration-commit-witness.distinct: It independently proves migration outcomes and rollback claims; it is not a competing migration DSL or schema-diff product.
migration-commit-witness.workaround: Rely on migration framework status, review raw SQL in a pull request, keep manually written rollback notes, and inspect a disposable database after the fact.

migration-lock-rehearsal.detail: Docker-first CLI: restore a sanitized sample, run one supplied migration under a configurable workload, record lock waits/statement timing/table size deltas, and generate a reversible runbook. Non-goals: migration authoring, production execution, schema management, or database hosting.
migration-lock-rehearsal.user: A Postgres or ClickHouse maintainer preparing a schema change who wants a concrete estimate of locking, table rewrite, and rollback risk before production.
migration-lock-rehearsal.distinct: It rehearses operational consequences of a change; it is not a schema-drift snapshot or a new migration framework.
migration-lock-rehearsal.workaround: Read vendor docs, inspect EXPLAIN/DDL manually, test on an approximate clone, or rely on migration framework defaults.

milkdrop-web.title: Milkdrop Web: mic-driven, beat-aware music visualizer for TVs and projectors — no audio routing
milkdrop-web.description: Turn room music into full-screen botanical visuals for TVs and projectors—without routing audio.
milkdrop-web.why: Show music-reactive visuals from a microphone on a TV or projector.

package-cost-explorer.detail: v1 static site: input name@version; fetch tarballs from the npm CDN (jsDelivr/unpkg) in the browser; resolve `exports`/`main`/`module`; bundle each export condition with esbuild-wasm (minify + gzip/brotli); show install size from packument metadata and dependency count; version-history sparkline; shareable URL; SVG badge served by a tiny worker. Not in v1: CSS/asset accounting, local package upload, Deno/JSR, or side-effect analysis.
package-cost-explorer.user: Frontend/Node developer choosing between dependencies who wants reliable install size, tree-shaken bundle size per subpath export, and dependency-tree bloat for a package@version, without a rate-limited, decaying service.
package-cost-explorer.distinct: Exports-map-per-entry costs plus install cost plus history in one client-side page is a capability none of the four incumbents has, and the client-side design removes the failure mode users complain about.
package-cost-explorer.workaround: bundlephobia (unreliable, main-entry only), bundlejs (esbuild in browser; manual import strings), pkg-size.dev, packagephobia (install size only), building a scratch project locally.

pad-light-choreographer.title: Pad Light Choreographer
pad-light-choreographer.description: Web MIDI PWA that discovers common grid pads, plays four-lane call-and-response patterns, lights target pads, and exports/imports compact JSON routines.…
pad-light-choreographer.why: Create four-lane pad-light routines and practise them hardware-first in your browser.
pad-light-choreographer.detail: Web MIDI PWA that discovers common grid pads, plays four-lane call-and-response patterns, lights target pads, and exports/imports compact JSON routines. Non-goals: DAW integration, commercial song charts, and device firmware flashing.
pad-light-choreographer.user: A MIDI-pad owner who wants hardware-first beat practice or tiny performances, with pad lights giving the next cue instead of a mouse-driven screen.
pad-light-choreographer.distinct: A cue-and-response instrument toy, not another piano-roll sequencer or a proprietary controller editor.
pad-light-choreographer.workaround: Map pads manually in a DAW, run scripts, or use controller lights only for generic demos.

page-pointer.title: Page Pointer
page-pointer.description: Guide emerging readers through physical books with a private, offline camera pointer.
page-pointer.why: Help emerging readers follow each word or line in a physical book.
page-pointer.detail: An offline mobile web app that uses the rear camera to detect printed text baselines, lets the adult tap the current word, and projects a high-contrast line/word guide on the phone screen. Non-goals: book scanning, child profiling, reading assessment, or cloud OCR archives.
page-pointer.user: Parents, tutors, and emerging readers who want a non-distracting way to keep a child oriented to the exact word or line in a physical book.
page-pointer.distinct: It supports joint attention during paper reading; it is neither an ebook reader nor a general OCR scanner.
page-pointer.workaround: A parent points with a finger, uses a bookmark or reading ruler, or buys a dedicated reading pen.

paid-before-ship-gate.title: Paid Before Ship Gate
paid-before-ship-gate.description: Check payments before packing, hold unpaid orders, and export only ready orders.
paid-before-ship-gate.why: Hold orders until payment is confirmed.
paid-before-ship-gate.detail: Local order-status board that imports orders and payment confirmations, flags 'hold until paid' rules by customer/order, logs an override reason, and exports a pack list. Non-goals: payment processing, credit scoring, debt collection, inventory reservation, or shipping labels.
paid-before-ship-gate.user: A tiny seller that quotes or takes orders on flexible terms but needs a visible, intentional rule for which orders must be paid before they are packed or dispatched.
paid-before-ship-gate.distinct: It adds a lightweight decision checkpoint between payment evidence and packing, rather than recreating order management.
paid-before-ship-gate.workaround: Use a spreadsheet column, remember customer exceptions, or stop shipments manually after an overdue invoice is noticed.

pairplay-motion.title: PairPlay Motion
pairplay-motion.description: A QR-pairing PWA with a host screen, two-phone motion calibration, and three original 2–4 player reaction games; it runs over local Wi-Fi and shows an explicit…
pairplay-motion.why: Turn spare phones into motion controllers for three quick room games.
pairplay-motion.detail: A QR-pairing PWA with a host screen, two-phone motion calibration, and three original 2–4 player reaction games; it runs over local Wi-Fi and shows an explicit permission screen. Non-goals: controller driver, social network, or copyrighted console emulation.
pairplay-motion.user: Friends and families with spare phones or split Joy-Cons who want a frictionless motion-controller party-game setup in a browser.
pairplay-motion.distinct: It makes unusual input the game mechanic, rather than shipping another controller-mapping utility or clone of a party-game franchise.
pairplay-motion.workaround: Install a platform-specific remote-control app, pair Bluetooth controllers, or avoid motion mechanics altogether.

pantry-meal-gap.title: Pantry Meal Gap
pantry-meal-gap.description: Local ingredient list, 20 manually entered staple meals, match score, acceptable substitutions, and auto-generated missing-items list. Non-goals: image…
pantry-meal-gap.why: See which meals are closest to what is already in your pantry, and make the smallest possible shopping list.
pantry-meal-gap.detail: Local ingredient list, 20 manually entered staple meals, match score, acceptable substitutions, and auto-generated missing-items list. Non-goals: image recognition, web recipe scraping, grocery delivery, meal-plan AI.
pantry-meal-gap.user: A home cook deciding dinner from imperfect on-hand ingredients who needs to see the smallest missing shopping list, not an idealized recipe catalog.
pantry-meal-gap.distinct: It answers ‘what can I make with one small gap?’ rather than generating recipes or maintaining a full food database.
pantry-meal-gap.workaround: Search recipes, mentally substitute ingredients, then make an ad-hoc grocery list.

parallel-ebook-reader.title: Parallel Reader
parallel-ebook-reader.description: An offline web reader for two DRM-free EPUBs with chapter alignment, manual paragraph anchors, side-by-side mode, and TSV export of selected sentence pairs.…
parallel-ebook-reader.why: Privately align your own DRM-free EPUB editions, read them in parallel, and export sentence pairs.
parallel-ebook-reader.detail: An offline web reader for two DRM-free EPUBs with chapter alignment, manual paragraph anchors, side-by-side mode, and TSV export of selected sentence pairs. Non-goals: selling books, DRM removal, machine translation, or public sharing.
parallel-ebook-reader.user: An intermediate language learner with legitimately obtained EPUBs in two languages who needs synchronized reading, audio, and private word capture.
parallel-ebook-reader.distinct: It connects the learner’s own parallel editions and audio workflow without trying to become a licensed-content library or automated translation wrapper.
parallel-ebook-reader.workaround: Open two readers, scroll manually, use Readlang/LingQ with their catalog constraints, or paste excerpts and screenshots into cards.

parameter-playground.title: Parameter Playground
parameter-playground.description: Build replayable model lessons by changing one parameter and checking the result.
parameter-playground.why: Build model lessons where learners predict, change one parameter, inspect the values, and explain the result.
parameter-playground.detail: Static-web builder for a small library of parameterized simulations: slider/table inputs, deterministic seed, accessible data table and narration fields, prediction prompt, and shareable preset URL. Non-goals: a CAS, arbitrary code execution, or generative explanations.
parameter-playground.user: Teachers and self-learners explaining algorithms or mathematical models who need an honest interactive visual that changes with parameters and exposes failed intuitions.
parameter-playground.distinct: It packages the pedagogical loop—predict, vary, inspect, explain—with accessibility, not just a charting canvas.
parameter-playground.workaround: Use a static animation, a notebook with hidden code, or a whiteboard explanation that cannot be replayed by the learner.

parent-kid-game-jam.title: Game Jam Sidekick
parent-kid-game-jam.description: Offline PWA with 20 printable/on-screen prompt cards, a three-step idea→asset→play loop, local project gallery, and a shareable completed-game postcard.…
parent-kid-game-jam.why: Make one small game together each week.
parent-kid-game-jam.detail: Offline PWA with 20 printable/on-screen prompt cards, a three-step idea→asset→play loop, local project gallery, and a shareable completed-game postcard. Non-goals: code editor, hosted games, AI generation, curriculum management.
parent-kid-game-jam.user: A programming parent helping an 8–13-year-old turn their own art and game ideas into one small playable project each week.
parent-kid-game-jam.distinct: It is a facilitation tool for co-making, not another programming course or game engine.
parent-kid-game-jam.workaround: Parents stitch together Scratch tutorials, art prompts, and a weekly video call or sit beside the child.

passkey-extension-check.title: Passkey Extension Check
passkey-extension-check.description: A browser extension that inventories password/passkey provider extensions and browser settings, runs a non-secret WebAuthn capability check, and generates a…
passkey-extension-check.why: Find overlapping passkey providers and prepare a recovery route before your next critical sign-in.
passkey-extension-check.detail: A browser extension that inventories password/passkey provider extensions and browser settings, runs a non-secret WebAuthn capability check, and generates a remediation/recovery checklist. Non-goals: storing credentials, intercepting authentication, or bypassing enterprise policy.
passkey-extension-check.user: An employee or privacy-conscious multi-browser user who needs to discover whether installed password-manager extensions can conflict before a passkey is their only login route.
passkey-extension-check.distinct: It diagnoses passkey-provider coexistence instead of competing as a password manager.
passkey-extension-check.workaround: Disable extensions one at a time, use an alternate browser/device, or discover the conflict only during authentication.

pause-garden.title: Pause Garden
pause-garden.description: Restore a shared garden with 2–4 remote friends in a 12-turn room-code game.
pause-garden.detail: A 2–4 player room-code garden-restoration game. In 15-minute chapters, each player places one action token at a time; an absent player becomes a harmless 'sleeping sprite' whose queued token can be completed by the group. Runs vary by weather, seed goals, and visitor requests. Non-goals: real-time combat, timers that punish absence, persistent grind, and social feed features.
pause-garden.user: Two to four remote friends with interrupted evenings—especially parents—who want a cozy cooperative game that remains meaningful when someone steps away.
pause-garden.distinct: The away-player mechanic is part of the game’s cooperative strategy, rather than an afterthought pause button on a real-time clone.
pause-garden.workaround: Pick turn-based games, ask friends to wait in voice chat, accept lost progress, or avoid co-op on nights with care duties.

payment-cadence.title: Gentle Nudge
payment-cadence.description: Local PWA with invoice dates, editable stage templates, a due-today queue, client-specific pause notes, and copy/email-draft output. Non-goals: auto-sending, pa
payment-cadence.detail: Local PWA with invoice dates, editable stage templates, a due-today queue, client-specific pause notes, and copy/email-draft output. Non-goals: auto-sending, payment prediction, debt collection, or access to bank accounts.
payment-cadence.user: Independent service providers who need to prepare consistent, escalating but human-approved payment reminders without delegating client relationships to an AI bot.
payment-cadence.distinct: It is a respectful human-in-the-loop reminder workspace, not a thin AI collections wrapper.
payment-cadence.workaround: Calendar reminders, copied email templates, and either avoiding follow-up or turning on impersonal automatic dunning.

payout-bundle-matcher.title: Settlement Match
payout-bundle-matcher.description: Local CSV matcher for one processor payout and one sales/invoice export: reconcile gross sales, fees, refunds, timing shifts, and produce a signed-off…
payout-bundle-matcher.why: Explain one processor payout from your sales CSVs, privately in your browser.
payout-bundle-matcher.detail: Local CSV matcher for one processor payout and one sales/invoice export: reconcile gross sales, fees, refunds, timing shifts, and produce a signed-off exception report. Non-goals: bank connectivity, automatic posting, tax reporting, or multi-store analytics.
payout-bundle-matcher.user: A one-store ecommerce or service business owner who needs to explain why a processor payout differs from that day’s orders and invoices without linking a bank account to another SaaS.
payout-bundle-matcher.distinct: It explains one payout bundle deterministically instead of being another accounting system or payments integration.
payout-bundle-matcher.workaround: Download processor and order CSVs, use spreadsheet formulas, and attach a note to one deposit or ask a bookkeeper to reconstruct it.

payout-reconciliation-explainer.title: Payout Reconciliation Explainer
payout-reconciliation-explainer.description: Reconcile one payout against order events and bank deposits in your browser.
payout-reconciliation-explainer.why: Explain one payout against orders, refunds, fees, and bank deposits — entirely on your device.
payout-reconciliation-explainer.detail: An offline web app that imports three CSVs (orders/events, payout, bank), applies transparent matching rules, shows fees/refunds/timing differences as a waterfall, and exports a reconciler CSV plus accountant handoff PDF. Non-goals: direct bank/Shopify connections, bookkeeping ledger, tax advice, or auto-posting journal entries.
payout-reconciliation-explainer.user: Small ecommerce operators and their bookkeepers who need to reconcile processor payouts against orders, refunds, fees, and bank deposits without opaque enterprise accounting tooling.
payout-reconciliation-explainer.distinct: It explains and hands off a single reconciliation rather than trying to replace accounting software or hide matching logic behind automation.
payout-reconciliation-explainer.workaround: Export CSVs from Shopify/Stripe/bank systems, combine them in spreadsheets, and leave a manual memo trail for an accountant.

pdf-flow-reader.title: PDF Flow Reader
pdf-flow-reader.description: Read long PDFs in one adjustable reading column.
pdf-flow-reader.why: Read PDFs in a clearer single-column layout.
pdf-flow-reader.detail: A browser-based local PDF reader with a single-column reflow mode, adjustable line/word spacing and contrast, heading navigation, keyboard reading position, and an explicit extraction-confidence warning. Non-goals: legal accessibility certification, PDF editing, or cloud OCR.
pdf-flow-reader.user: Knowledge workers with low vision who need long PDFs to read as stable, keyboard-first reflowed prose rather than zoomed page images or broken screen-reader line fragments.
pdf-flow-reader.distinct: It is a personal reading adaptation layer, not a generic PDF editor or automated compliance checker.
pdf-flow-reader.workaround: Increase browser zoom, use OS magnification/inverted contrast, buy a screen reader, or switch between viewers until one happens to expose usable text.

pdf-link-map.title: PDF Link Map
pdf-link-map.description: A CLI that accepts a PDF plus optional heading manifest, inventories internal/external annotations, validates destinations and duplicate anchors, and writes a c
pdf-link-map.detail: A CLI that accepts a PDF plus optional heading manifest, inventories internal/external annotations, validates destinations and duplicate anchors, and writes a clickable HTML map. Non-goals: PDF rendering, document authoring, or external-link crawling.
pdf-link-map.user: Operations and technical-document teams converting HTML or DOCX to PDF who need to know whether navigation survives the conversion.
pdf-link-map.distinct: It treats link integrity as a testable handoff contract, independent of the converter that created the file.
pdf-link-map.workaround: Open the PDF and manually click a handful of links or wait for a reader complaint.

pdf-redaction-proof.title: Redaction Proof
pdf-redaction-proof.description: A local drop-zone that inspects a PDF, flags recoverable text/objects/metadata behind requested redactions, creates a sanitized copy, and emits a machine-readab
pdf-redaction-proof.detail: A local drop-zone that inspects a PDF, flags recoverable text/objects/metadata behind requested redactions, creates a sanitized copy, and emits a machine-readable verification report. Non-goals: legal advice, cloud signing, or document editing.
pdf-redaction-proof.user: People sending converted or redacted PDFs who need evidence that hidden text, metadata, and removable overlays are not still present.
pdf-redaction-proof.distinct: The product verifies a security property of an output file rather than competing as a broad PDF editor.
pdf-redaction-proof.workaround: Trust a PDF editor's visual overlay, manually copy/paste-test pages, or flatten/reprint documents without a verification record.

pen-display-drills.title: Pen Display Drills
pen-display-drills.description: Practice tablet lines and perspective with five-minute feedback drills.
pen-display-drills.why: Practise pen strokes against visible drawing targets.
pen-display-drills.detail: Offline browser drills for straight lines, ellipses, boxes and one/two-point perspective; overlay a target, show deviation bands, support pen/mouse/touch, and save nothing by default. Non-goals: painting app, portfolio network, AI critique.
pen-display-drills.user: Early digital artists with a drawing tablet who need five-minute, feedback-rich drills for perspective and line control rather than another blank canvas.
pen-display-drills.distinct: It trains a physical skill in tiny loops rather than cloning a raster editor.
pen-display-drills.workaround: Follow long videos, print worksheets, or use a general drawing app and judge the result manually.

pen-latency-lab.title: Stroke Lab
pen-latency-lab.description: A local web test pad plus embeddable JS probe that records anonymized pointer timing, draws raw versus smoothed traces, and exports a reproducible issue…
pen-latency-lab.why: Measure pointer sampling, smoothing, render delay, and undo cost in a private local drawing lab.
pen-latency-lab.detail: A local web test pad plus embeddable JS probe that records anonymized pointer timing, draws raw versus smoothed traces, and exports a reproducible issue bundle. Non-goals: replacing brush engines, driver installation, or cloud telemetry.
pen-latency-lab.user: Digital artists and maintainers of browser/cross-platform drawing tools who need to isolate whether a bad stroke comes from smoothing, device sampling, rendering, or undo history.
pen-latency-lab.distinct: It measures and explains drawing feel; it is not a new canvas editor or a thin AI brush wrapper.
pen-latency-lab.workaround: Switch apps, toggle an undocumented smoothing setting, screen-record a bad stroke, or submit an issue without timing evidence.

persistent-ink-cues.title: Persistent Ink Cues
persistent-ink-cues.description: Offline canvas overlay with transient, persistent-until-clear, and fade modes; big clear/undo controls; exported static frame; e-ink-safe reduced-animation…
persistent-ink-cues.why: Keep presentation cues visible for pens, touch, and keyboards.
persistent-ink-cues.detail: Offline canvas overlay with transient, persistent-until-clear, and fade modes; big clear/undo controls; exported static frame; e-ink-safe reduced-animation mode. Non-goals: collaborative whiteboarding, cloud documents, OCR, and slide hosting.
persistent-ink-cues.user: A presenter or workshop leader using a pen/tablet who needs an emphasis mark to persist until deliberately cleared, including on slow-refresh e-ink displays.
persistent-ink-cues.distinct: A cue layer optimized for persistence and slow displays, not a general-purpose whiteboard clone.
persistent-ink-cues.workaround: Draw permanent ink that must later be erased, repeatedly redraw a laser line, or use a separate slide annotation tool.

personal-vocab-loop.title: Personal Vocab Loop
personal-vocab-loop.description: Capture personal phrases, replay your voice, and recall each one on a clear schedule.
personal-vocab-loop.why: Save your own words, sentences, and recordings for review.
personal-vocab-loop.detail: Offline mobile PWA: capture word, personal sentence, optional 10-second recording, and context tag; prompt active recall and replay on a transparent schedule. Non-goals: machine translation, public decks, and gamified streaks.
personal-vocab-loop.user: A language learner who wants words to survive in speech by practicing their own sentence and voice, not a generic streak.
personal-vocab-loop.distinct: It is a personal phrase-and-voice retention loop, not another language course, dictionary, or streak mechanic.
personal-vocab-loop.workaround: Use Duolingo or Anki plus separate notes, record voice memos, and manually protect personal annotations during deck changes.

phone-photo-intake.title: Photo Intake Receipt
phone-photo-intake.description: Move selected phone photos to a PC, check each copy, and keep a receipt before deleting originals.
phone-photo-intake.why: Move phone photos with a verified receipt before you delete a single original.
phone-photo-intake.detail: Companion desktop/Android pair that transfers a selected batch on LAN, resumes chunks, hashes files, and creates a signed-style receipt listing source count, destination count, missing files, and safe-to-delete status. Non-goals: general chat, remote cloud sharing, media management, or an account service.
phone-photo-intake.user: A person moving phone photos to a PC who needs a resilient transfer record: which files arrived, which did not, and which can be safely deleted from the phone.
phone-photo-intake.distinct: The product is the verifiable intake/deletion decision, not another broad file-transfer clone.
phone-photo-intake.workaround: USB cables, cloud drives, AirDrop-like tools, WeTransfer, retrying transfers, and manually eyeballing file counts.

photo-cull-review.title: Photo Cull Review
photo-cull-review.description: Review duplicate photos and likely bursts before exporting a move plan.
photo-cull-review.why: Review duplicate and burst photos side by side, then export your keep list.
photo-cull-review.detail: Desktop-local PWA that indexes selected folders, groups exact hashes and visually similar burst candidates, presents side-by-side keep decisions, and exports a move-to-review-folder manifest. Non-goals: cloud photo hosting, face recognition, or automatic deletion.
photo-cull-review.user: Households with large photo archives who need to safely decide which duplicate, burst, and unwanted media can be removed before backup costs and browsing noise grow further.
photo-cull-review.distinct: The product is a cautious decision workflow between detection and deletion, rather than another photo library or automatic deduper.
photo-cull-review.workaround: Run a duplicate finder, delete in batches, or postpone cleanup because tools offer opaque matches and destructive actions.

photo-edit-ledger.title: Sidecar Ledger
photo-edit-ledger.description: Check which photo metadata survives when you move an archive between tools.
photo-edit-ledger.why: Check which photo metadata and photo edit settings survive before you move a RAW archive between tools.
photo-edit-ledger.detail: Local CLI that inventories a folder plus XMP sidecars, compares declared source/destination capabilities, and emits a handoff manifest showing portable, lossy, and unknown fields. Non-goals: image editing, cloud sync, or attempting to reverse-engineer proprietary adjustment recipes.
photo-edit-ledger.user: Photographers moving RAW/DNG files between editors and self-hosted libraries who need to know which ratings, descriptions, and edits will survive each handoff.
photo-edit-ledger.distinct: The deliverable is an evidence-backed handoff contract, not a replacement photo catalog or a generic metadata editor.
photo-edit-ledger.workaround: Keep notes manually, duplicate originals, make rendered intermediates, or discover after import that a catalog's sidecar policy was incompatible.

photo-edit-portability-map.title: Edit Portability Map
photo-edit-portability-map.description: Read-only desktop CLI that inventories a Lightroom catalog/XMP and a target folder, classifies fields as embedded, sidecar, catalog-only, or…
photo-edit-portability-map.why: Map which Lightroom edits and metadata survive a migration.
photo-edit-portability-map.detail: Read-only desktop CLI that inventories a Lightroom catalog/XMP and a target folder, classifies fields as embedded, sidecar, catalog-only, or target-unsupported, and produces a migration checklist and verification sample. Non-goals: converting RAW development recipes or modifying a live catalog.
photo-edit-portability-map.user: Photographers leaving Lightroom or using a read-only external library who need to know exactly which edits, dates, ratings, and metadata will travel safely.
photo-edit-portability-map.distinct: It makes lock-in visible before a move instead of pretending to be a one-click Lightroom replacement.
photo-edit-portability-map.workaround: Export JPEGs, copy the catalog, search forum posts, and discover missing edits or metadata after switching applications.

photo-edit-sidecar-check.title: Edit Sidecar Check
photo-edit-sidecar-check.description: Local desktop/web checker that compares source plus sidecar/export, reports pixel-bearing edit data versus portable metadata, and produces a handoff checklist.…
photo-edit-sidecar-check.why: Check whether photo edits and ratings survive a RAW or DNG handoff.
photo-edit-sidecar-check.detail: Local desktop/web checker that compares source plus sidecar/export, reports pixel-bearing edit data versus portable metadata, and produces a handoff checklist. Non-goals: RAW development, cloud sync, or writing proprietary edits.
photo-edit-sidecar-check.user: Photographers moving edited RAW/DNG files between phone and desktop tools who need to know whether edits, ratings, and tags will survive an export before they lose work.
photo-edit-sidecar-check.distinct: It explains interoperability risk; it does not compete as another photo editor.
photo-edit-sidecar-check.workaround: Export a flattened JPEG/TIFF, keep several originals, or test each app combination manually and discover losses after a batch.

photo-exit-manifest.title: Photo Exit Manifest
photo-exit-manifest.description: Verify a Google Photos export against your family archive before leaving the cloud.
photo-exit-manifest.why: Check a Google Photos export and create a migration report.
photo-exit-manifest.detail: A local CLI that reads export inventories and destination folder reports, compares counts/hashes/dates/albums where available, records desired backup/mirror policies per device, and writes a cutover checklist with exceptions. Non-goals: transferring data, hosting photos, facial recognition, or two-way syncing.
photo-exit-manifest.user: Families leaving Google Photos or another consumer cloud who need a verifiable, interruption-safe migration plan into an independent archive without losing albums, edits, or device expectations.
photo-exit-manifest.distinct: It is a migration assurance layer across providers, not a replacement photo cloud or sync engine.
photo-exit-manifest.workaround: Export Takeout, copy folders into a NAS/Immich, and manually compare counts; keep paying for the original service because they cannot prove the new setup is complete.

photo-metadata-queue.title: Caption Queue
photo-metadata-queue.description: Caption large photo shoots and export XMP metadata without changing the original files.
photo-metadata-queue.why: Queue photo metadata and XMP sidecars for review.
photo-metadata-queue.detail: A local folder/CSV-driven queue that groups images by shoot, offers reusable caption tokens and controlled vocabularies, previews changes, and writes XMP sidecars. Non-goals: generative captions, face recognition, or a full DAM.
photo-metadata-queue.user: Photographers with large shoots who need a fast, deliberate queue for titles, captions, keywords, and IPTC fields without hand-editing every image in a DAM.
photo-metadata-queue.distinct: It is a metadata work queue and validator, not a broad image catalog or thin caption generator.
photo-metadata-queue.workaround: Copy/paste text, use Lightroom presets, write ad-hoc scripts, or postpone metadata until it never gets completed.

photo-proof-pile.title: Proof Pile
photo-proof-pile.description: Review duplicate photo copies, quarantine extras, and restore each move from a local decision log.
photo-proof-pile.detail: Local desktop/PWA scanner that groups exact, perceptual, and metadata-near duplicates; shows every copy's path, dimensions, EXIF and backup presence; then writes an undoable move-to-quarantine plan and CSV decision log. Non-goals: cloud photo hosting, face recognition, or auto-deletion.
photo-proof-pile.user: People with multi-drive photo libraries who need to remove duplicates and low-value shots without accidentally deleting the only meaningful copy.
photo-proof-pile.distinct: The product is a defensible review-and-reversal workflow for cleanup, not another gallery or magic duplicate detector.
photo-proof-pile.workaround: Use Photos/Google Photos, run dupeGuru or PhotoSweeper, then manually inspect folders and keep excess copies rather than risk a deletion.

photo-stack-proof.title: Photo Stack Proof
photo-stack-proof.description: Local analyser that groups candidate pairs by basename, reads available capture/content IDs and timestamps, and labels each as verified, ambiguous, or…
photo-stack-proof.why: Verify that same-name photos, videos, and sidecars really belong together before you stack, import, or delete.
photo-stack-proof.detail: Local analyser that groups candidate pairs by basename, reads available capture/content IDs and timestamps, and labels each as verified, ambiguous, or conflict; exports a review CSV. Non-goals: auto-merge/delete, a DAM, face recognition, or cloud backups.
photo-stack-proof.user: An iPhone/RAW photographer with years of exports who needs to verify that same-name images, videos, and sidecars really belong together before a DAM stacks or deletes them.
photo-stack-proof.distinct: It is a conservative identity-verification tool, not another automatic photo-stacking feature.
photo-stack-proof.workaround: Trust the DAM's grouping, rename files manually, or inspect EXIF fields with specialist tools.

photo-upload-audit.title: Photo Upload Audit
photo-upload-audit.description: Check which camera-export files reached your backup before clearing phone space.
photo-upload-audit.why: Compare a camera export with any backup folder.
photo-upload-audit.detail: Offline desktop/PWA scanner that reads a camera export and destination, matches hashes plus Live Photo pairs, and produces a missing/duplicate/changed report. Non-goals: photo hosting, cloud sync, facial recognition, or deletion automation.
photo-upload-audit.user: iPhone and Android owners who auto-back up photos but need proof that every original, Live Photo sidecar, and video reached their chosen disk or server.
photo-upload-audit.distinct: It verifies a backup handoff rather than becoming another photo library or sync service.
photo-upload-audit.workaround: Manually compare folders, trust a sync badge, or re-copy an entire camera roll.

photo-walk-scratchbook.title: Photo Walk Scratchbook
photo-walk-scratchbook.description: An offline tablet PWA with a short photo-walk prompt deck, a local-import contact sheet, stylus crop/line annotations, and an exportable one-page session…
photo-walk-scratchbook.why: Plan photo walks with contact sheets and framing notes.
photo-walk-scratchbook.detail: An offline tablet PWA with a short photo-walk prompt deck, a local-import contact sheet, stylus crop/line annotations, and an exportable one-page session sheet. Non-goals: image generation, cloud photo backup, social feed, or RAW development.
photo-walk-scratchbook.user: Photographers trying to make deliberate pictures with a real camera who want a tactile, offline prompt-and-annotation companion rather than automatic image enhancement.

raw-sidecar-sanity.user: A photographer importing RAW plus camera JPEG pairs who needs to catch impossible dimensions, aspect ratios, or timestamps before a catalog makes bad thumbnails and timelines.
raw-sidecar-sanity.distinct: It checks agreement among files and readers before import instead of becoming a photo catalog.
raw-sidecar-sanity.workaround: Open files one by one in several apps, compare against JPEGs, or discover defects after catalog import.

reader-setting-transfer.distinct: The differentiator is portable, inspectable accessibility preferences applied to extracted reading content—not another generic dark-mode extension.
reader-setting-transfer.workaround: Use browser zoom, adjust settings on each reader, invoke Reader Mode inconsistently, or maintain custom CSS stylesheets.

reading-archive-pack.title: Reading Archive Pack

reading-comfort-profiles.detail: Browser extension with keyboard-switchable per-domain profiles for base font, line height, code font, contrast, cursor/focus visibility, and optional table spacing; all settings stay locally. Non-goals: screen reader replacement, page scraping, or AI rewriting.
reading-comfort-profiles.user: Knowledge workers with low vision who need readable text, code, tables, and density settings across web-based work apps without changing every site manually.
reading-comfort-profiles.distinct: It treats readability as a saved, semantic per-workflow preference rather than a single global magnification setting.
reading-comfort-profiles.workaround: OS magnifier, browser zoom, reader mode where available, and repeated per-site CSS/font changes.

reading-margin-recall.title: Reading Margin Recall

reading-margin-recall.user: Language learners reading their own ebooks or web articles who need to turn selected passages into reviewable, source-linked notes.
reading-margin-recall.distinct: The emphasis is transparent learner-authored retrieval from reading margins, not an AI summary or a replacement ebook reader.
reading-margin-recall.workaround: Copy/paste into Anki, use a browser highlighter, or rely on a proprietary reader's word list.

reading-rail.title: Reading Rail
reading-rail.description: A browser extension with a movable focus rail, dimmable surrounding paragraphs, per-site line-height/letter-spacing presets, and optional browser TTS for the…

reading-rail.detail: A browser extension with a movable focus rail, dimmable surrounding paragraphs, per-site line-height/letter-spacing presets, and optional browser TTS for the current line. reading-rail.user: A reader with dyslexia or visual crowding who needs to keep their place in dense browser text and review one manageable line or paragraph at a time.

recall-calibrator.title: Recall Calibrator
recall-calibrator.description: A local review companion that samples typed exact/keyword recall before revealing an answer, compares it to the learner's grade, and reports personal…

recall-calibrator.detail: A local review companion that samples typed exact/keyword recall before revealing an answer, compares it to the learner's grade, and reports personal calibration with exportable intervals. Non-goals: replacing Anki, automatic grading of essays, or an LLM tutor.
recall-calibrator.user: Spaced-repetition users who distrust their own Good/Hard/Easy judgment and want to know whether they can actually retrieve an answer.
recall-calibrator.distinct: It measures the reliability of the review signal feeding an SRS rather than competing on another scheduling algorithm.
recall-calibrator.workaround: Tap a subjective rating, use a strict personal rule, or change Anki scheduler settings without feedback about calibration.

recall-objective-map.title: Recall Objective Map

recall-objective-map.detail: Offline PWA with an objective tree, manual evidence tags (explain, solve, recognize), a one-question recall check, and an exportable weekly weak-skill map. Non-goals: generating course content, a chatbot tutor, or replacing Anki scheduling.
recall-objective-map.user: A self-learner starting a broad topic who needs every review prompt tied to a stated learning objective and visible evidence of what they can actually explain.

receipt-to-room.title: Receipt to Room

Non-goals: automatic retailer scraping, cloud receipt storage, valuation estimates, or filing claims.
receipt-to-room.user: A renter or homeowner returning from a large purchase who needs to turn receipts into a searchable room-level inventory for warranties, insurance, and household replenishment.
receipt-to-room.distinct: It makes receipt intake reviewable and local, instead of being a cloud home-inventory clone or retailer scraper.

recipe-exit-pack.user: People leaving a single-platform recipe app who need their own recipes, notes, photos, and source attribution in a portable offline format.
recipe-exit-pack.distinct: It is an exit and preservation utility, not another recipe subscription, scraper, or AI recipe generator.
recipe-exit-pack.workaround: Manual copy/paste, screenshots, app-specific exports, and one-off command-line scripts.

recipe-import-repair.distinct: This is a deterministic repair bench for user-owned files, not a thin AI recipe parser.
recipe-import-repair.workaround: Retry imports blindly, hand-edit JSON, retype recipes, or depend on an LLM to rewrite source text.

recipe-library-move-check.title: Recipe Library Move Check

recipe-library-move-check.distinct: It de-risks the decision to move rather than becoming another shared recipe manager.

recipe-passport.title: Recipe Passport

recipe-passport.user: People leaving a recipe app or tired of ad-heavy recipe pages who need to preserve their own recipes in a portable, calm offline cooking format.
recipe-passport.distinct: It is a data-portability and offline-reading tool rather than another recipe manager trying to own the user's collection.

recipe-source-card.title: Recipe Source Card

recipe-source-card.distinct: It is a transparent, repairable personal capture pipeline, not a recipe database or thin LLM summarizer.
recipe-source-card.workaround: Browser bookmarks, screenshots, copy/paste into Notes, or importing into an opaque recipe app and correcting it by hand.

rehearsal-section-cues.user: A small ensemble leader or multi-instrument player who needs a clear, printable cue sheet for where a rehearsal section begins, who plays on each pass, and what is difficult there.

remote-code-lesson-replay.user: A remote programming tutor who needs to review a student's reasoning between live sessions without recording an entire screen call.

remote-file-handoff-manifest.title: Remote File Handoff Manifest

remote-screen-reader.user: A blind or low-vision person using a locked-down work, school, kiosk, or game computer who needs to hear the currently visible UI without installing software on that computer.
remote-screen-reader.distinct: It is a constrained remote fallback for inaccessible surfaces, not another general-purpose AI computer agent or cloud vision chatbot.

remote-web-task-recipes.title: Remote Web Task Recipes

remote-web-task-recipes.user: A low-vision or screen-reader user who must complete recurring tasks in browser-delivered remote/legacy software that exposes little usable accessibility metadata.
remote-web-task-recipes.distinct: It supplies reusable, user-owned task landmarks in inaccessible browser surfaces rather than trying to replace a screen reader or automate employment decisions.

rename-plan-reviewer.title: Rename Plan Reviewer

restore-drill.distinct: It verifies recovery rather than creating or hosting backups.
