retainer-release-ledger.why: Track deposits, milestones, and decisions to release work.
retainer-release-ledger.detail: Local job ledger with deposit, milestone, release, refund, and balance events; a client-facing receipt; and a red/amber/green release status. Non-goals: holding funds, charging cards, collections, or accounting-ledger replacement.
retainer-release-ledger.user: A freelancer or small service shop taking deposits who needs to know what has been prepaid, what work may be released, and what remains payable.
retainer-release-ledger.distinct: It answers 'may I release this job?' from a lightweight audit trail rather than trying to be invoicing software.
retainer-release-ledger.workaround: Label deposits in a spreadsheet or invoice notes, manually subtract them later, and decide by memory whether to release the final work.

retrieval-rhythm.title: Retrieval Rhythm
retrieval-rhythm.description: Offline PWA: create 20–100 prompt/answer items, answer by typing, receive transparent retry timing, and see a one-screen ‘due because…’ explanation. Non-goals:
retrieval-rhythm.detail: Offline PWA: create 20–100 prompt/answer items, answer by typing, receive transparent retry timing, and see a one-screen ‘due because…’ explanation. Non-goals: AI card generation, shared decks, and a full note app.
retrieval-rhythm.user: A self-learner who wants to remember a small set of facts without learning an unfamiliar flashcard grading system.
retrieval-rhythm.distinct: It removes confidence buttons rather than cloning a card database or wrapping an LLM around Anki.
retrieval-rhythm.workaround: Use Anki/Logseq buttons and guess a confidence rating, or abandon review after a few days.

return-ramp.title: Return Ramp
return-ramp.description: Plan three short study sessions after a break.
return-ramp.why: Make a small plan for returning to a paused task.
return-ramp.detail: An offline study-session planner with a missed-time check-in, a 5/10/20-minute return plan, backlog caps, and a private continuity calendar. Non-goals: social leaderboards, push-notification nagging, or replacing SRS algorithms.
return-ramp.user: Self-learners with interrupted routines who need to restart a study habit without a punitive streak or a giant overdue queue.
return-ramp.distinct: It treats restarting as the main job, rather than adding rewards to make a generic habit tracker stickier.
return-ramp.workaround: Reset a streak, lower new-card limits manually, skip backlog, or switch apps repeatedly.

review-backlog-forecast.title: Review Backlog Forecast
review-backlog-forecast.description: Plan a daily review schedule for an overdue Anki queue.
review-backlog-forecast.why: Compare catch-up plans for a study backlog by cards and minutes per day.
review-backlog-forecast.detail: A local import-and-preview tool that models three recovery policies (steady, deadline, gentle), shows cards/minutes per day and exactly which assumptions move cards. Non-goals: modifying Anki collections or guaranteeing retention.
review-backlog-forecast.user: A spaced-repetition learner returning after missed days who needs to recover a backlog without silently losing progress or creating one impossible session.
review-backlog-forecast.distinct: It explains and forecasts a backlog before rescheduling, rather than presenting another set of opaque review buttons.
review-backlog-forecast.workaround: Click reschedule, bury cards, skip reviews, or work through the pile until fatigue sets in.

review-backlog-restart.title: Review Backlog Restart
review-backlog-restart.description: Local companion that imports an Anki CSV export, asks for daily minutes and deadline, simulates three recovery plans, flags highest-risk cards, and exports a…
review-backlog-restart.why: Turn an overdue Anki backlog into an honest, time-boxed recovery plan. Private, local, and free.
review-backlog-restart.detail: Local companion that imports an Anki CSV export, asks for daily minutes and deadline, simulates three recovery plans, flags highest-risk cards, and exports a tagged action list. Non-goals: syncing to Anki, replacing FSRS, or making retention guarantees.
review-backlog-restart.user: Spaced-repetition users returning after a break who need an honest, manageable restart plan that protects high-risk material without forcing an all-night catch-up session.
review-backlog-restart.distinct: It is a recovery decision aid, not a scheduler, deck, or generic productivity timer.
review-backlog-restart.workaround: Set arbitrary daily limits, reset cards, grind through the queue, or abandon the deck and start again.

review-pdf-packet.title: Review Packet
review-pdf-packet.description: Package reviewed PDFs with comments, decisions, links, and attachments for external reviewers.
review-pdf-packet.why: Build a PDF review packet with comments, decisions, links, and attachments for an external reviewer.
review-pdf-packet.detail: Static local packet builder: add a PDF, structured comments/decisions, source links, and attachments; export a self-contained HTML folder and print stylesheet. Non-goals: editing PDFs, OCR, collaboration accounts, or conversion from proprietary workspaces.
review-pdf-packet.user: A professional handing an internally reviewed document to an external reviewer who needs comments, change context, and attachments visible without giving access to the source workspace.
review-pdf-packet.distinct: It is a cross-tool review handoff artifact, not yet another PDF editor or generic document converter.
review-pdf-packet.workaround: Screenshots, copy/paste into an email, Word tracked changes, separate attachment lists, or giving reviewers unwanted workspace access.

revision-feedback-receipts.title: Revision Receipts
revision-feedback-receipts.description: Compare student drafts, show feedback evidence, and export a revision receipt.
revision-feedback-receipts.why: Compare two drafts with teacher feedback goals and create a student revision receipt in your browser.
revision-feedback-receipts.detail: A browser-based document-pair tool: teacher marks 1–3 feedback goals, student uploads a revised plain-text/Markdown draft, and the tool produces quoted changed passages plus a student reflection. Non-goals: generating prose, plagiarism detection, grading, or an LMS.
revision-feedback-receipts.user: A secondary-school or college writing teacher who needs to give a class useful feedback and see whether a student acted on it without reading every draft side by side.
revision-feedback-receipts.distinct: The unit of value is evidence that feedback changed a draft, not another AI writing assistant or document editor.
revision-feedback-receipts.workaround: Teachers leave comments in Google Docs/Word, students resubmit, and teachers manually hunt for which suggestions were adopted.

rhythm-pedal-tidy.title: Rhythm Pedal Tidy
rhythm-pedal-tidy.description: Clean sustain-pedal overlaps, review each repair, and export practice takes without moving note starts.
rhythm-pedal-tidy.why: Clean sustain-pedal MIDI overlaps, compare each repair, replay the take, and export locally.
rhythm-pedal-tidy.detail: Offline Web MIDI recorder, sustain-aware de-overlap pass with before/after diff, tempo ramp, and replayable timing score. Non-goals: notation engraving, audio recording, subscriptions, and instrument lessons.
rhythm-pedal-tidy.user: Keyboard and e-kit players recording practice takes with sustain pedals who need a clean, playable MIDI capture instead of a tangle of overlapping notes.
rhythm-pedal-tidy.distinct: Combines pedal-aware MIDI repair with a motivating practice loop rather than attempting to replace a DAW or a rhythm game.
rhythm-pedal-tidy.workaround: Hand-edit overlapping piano-roll notes, avoid pedal capture, or tolerate inaccurate-looking takes.

rhythm-reader.title: Rhythm Reader: tap-in rhythm sight-reading trainer with real-music patterns and honest feedback
rhythm-reader.description: Practice rhythm patterns with clear tap timing feedback.
rhythm-reader.why: Practice short rhythms by tapping them and see early, on-time, late, and missed feedback.
rhythm-reader.detail: Choose meter, tempo, style-grammar (folk/march/swing/pop backbeat); a 2–4 bar rhythm renders as notation; count-in; you tap spacebar/screen or clap into the mic; each note gets an early/late/missed marker and a percentage; 'again / harder / stay here' controls. Streak calendar in localStorage. Deliberately NOT: pitch reading, MIDI piano grading, real copyrighted songs, accounts.
rhythm-reader.user: Adult amateur pianists/guitarists/drummers practising sight-reading who find random-note generators boring and cannot tell whether they actually played the notated rhythm.
rhythm-reader.distinct: Existing trainers are random-dice generators with a metronome; this scores you against notation with pattern-based content and explicit 'stay at this level' control.
rhythm-reader.workaround: Paper flashcards, metronome + self-judgement, paid apps (Rhythm Trainer, Complete Rhythm Trainer) that are drill-only.

riddle-grid.title: Riddle Grid
riddle-grid.description: Solve a daily 4×4 deduction grid by placing four illustrated specimens.
riddle-grid.why: Arrange illustrated clues into the one correct daily grid.
riddle-grid.detail: Daily 4x4 grid: arrange four illustrated clues under two rules, with exactly one final layout. Each attempt can request one visible constraint at a score cost; reveal gives a compact explanation. Non-goals: LLM judging, user-submitted clues, infinite puzzle library, or chat.
riddle-grid.user: Coffee-break puzzle players fatigued by spelling games who want one short daily deduction puzzle with a satisfying reveal.
riddle-grid.distinct: It avoids the saturated spelling loop by making reasoning and its explanation the payoff.
riddle-grid.workaround: Play word ladders, Boggle variants, and Wordle derivatives or abandon a puzzle when its vocabulary is obscure.

ride-sensor-truth.title: Ride Sensor Truth
ride-sensor-truth.description: Offline FIT/GPX companion that compares GPS, wheel speed, cadence, and pauses; flags suspect segments; previews alternate totals; and exports a repaired copy pl
ride-sensor-truth.detail: Offline FIT/GPX companion that compares GPS, wheel speed, cadence, and pauses; flags suspect segments; previews alternate totals; and exports a repaired copy plus provenance report. Non-goals: live navigation, hardware pairing, or social fitness feeds.
ride-sensor-truth.user: Cyclists using wheel or cadence sensors who need a trustworthy record when the sensor silently disagrees with GPS during a ride.
ride-sensor-truth.distinct: It is a data-integrity and provenance layer, not a competing ride tracker.
ride-sensor-truth.workaround: Notice after the ride, inspect charts manually, re-seat a magnet, or choose GPS/sensor data globally with no incident record.

room-code-mystery.title: Room Code Mystery
room-code-mystery.description: Solve a three-round mystery with 4–8 friends using one synchronized room code.
room-code-mystery.why: Compare private clues with friends and solve one timed browser mystery.
room-code-mystery.detail: A 4–8 player browser mystery told in three timed evidence rounds. Each player receives different visual clues; the group submits one accusation before a compact reveal. One host shares a code, remote players use personal views. Non-goals: public matchmaking, voice/video, LLM judging, permanent accounts, or a game portal.
room-code-mystery.user: Remote friend groups who want a warm, low-stakes 20-minute social deduction game with a room code, no pack purchase, and no AI-generated judgments.
room-code-mystery.distinct: It sells a complete human-authored social-deduction session, not a bundle storefront, collection site, or LLM comedy wrapper.
room-code-mystery.workaround: Buy a Jackbox pack, schedule a Discord game, or hunt through a general game portal for a room-compatible title.

route-fidelity-check.title: Route Fidelity Check
route-fidelity-check.description: Browser tool that accepts two GPX files, aligns them, highlights divergences over a user-set distance, and emits a printable cue/checklist. Non-goals: route…
route-fidelity-check.why: Compare an intended GPX route with an exported route and spot silent rerouting before you ride.
route-fidelity-check.detail: Browser tool that accepts two GPX files, aligns them, highlights divergences over a user-set distance, and emits a printable cue/checklist. Non-goals: route planning, turn-by-turn navigation, accounts, or map-data editing.
route-fidelity-check.user: A cyclist or club ride leader who has a deliberate GPX route and needs to know whether a navigation app/device silently rerouted it before riders follow it.
route-fidelity-check.distinct: It audits a route handoff instead of competing to be the next route planner.
route-fidelity-check.workaround: Manually inspect the route in each app/device, add many shaping points, or discover the deviation after export.

route-intent-planner.title: Route Intent Planner
route-intent-planner.description: A GPX/web planner that accepts a rough trace or named mandatory segments, locks those corridors, optimizes only gaps, and flags off-intent sections. Non-goals…
route-intent-planner.why: Lock the roads and paths you mean to ride, inspect every gap, and export a route that preserves your intent.
route-intent-planner.detail: A GPX/web planner that accepts a rough trace or named mandatory segments, locks those corridors, optimizes only gaps, and flags off-intent sections. Non-goals: turn-by-turn navigation, social feed, or proprietary map tiles.
route-intent-planner.user: Cyclists and ride leaders who know the roads or paths they intend to use and need a route planner that preserves those choices instead of silently redrawing them.
route-intent-planner.distinct: The core object is user-declared route intent and deviations, not a new general-purpose map.
route-intent-planner.workaround: Add excessive waypoints, draw a line in a separate map, export GPX, and repeatedly inspect segments for detours.

route-of-the-day.title: Route of the Day
route-of-the-day.description: Draw a daily route across a new spatial puzzle.
route-of-the-day.why: Lay route tiles to connect landmarks under a daily rule.
route-of-the-day.detail: A deterministic daily grid where players lay 6–10 route tiles to connect landmarks under one changing constraint; after completion, unlimited non-scored archived seeds unlock. Non-goals: social feed, streak punishments, news/political simulation, or account requirement.
route-of-the-day.user: Daily-puzzle regulars who want one fresh five-minute spatial route puzzle plus an optional archive and practice mode, without another word or chess clone.
route-of-the-day.distinct: A route-building spatial puzzle fills a daily-web-game gap without copying Wordle’s answer-checking loop.
route-of-the-day.workaround: Cycle through Wordle descendants, chess puzzles, and daily sites that often offer only one domain or block practice behind completion.

rss-saved-queue.title: RSS Saved Queue
rss-saved-queue.description: Save web links in a private RSS queue, then read them in your reader.
rss-saved-queue.why: Save web links in a private queue, set their order, and read them in your RSS reader.
rss-saved-queue.detail: A self-hostable service plus browser extension that saves URL/title/tags, serves an authenticated per-user RSS/Atom queue, and marks items read via the extension or feed-reader token endpoint. Non-goals: article scraping bypass, social feed aggregation, recommendation algorithms, or AI summaries.
rss-saved-queue.user: RSS-reader users who want saved web articles to re-enter their existing reading workflow as a private feed instead of accumulating in a separate read-later silo.
rss-saved-queue.distinct: It is an interoperability bridge between save actions and RSS habits, not a replacement feed reader or generic bookmark app.
rss-saved-queue.workaround: Use a separate Instapaper/Pocket-like inbox, public Raindrop feeds, automation services, or manually copy URLs into a reader.

rubric-comment-queue.title: Rubric Comment Queue
rubric-comment-queue.description: Web app: import plain text or paste excerpts, attach a rubric criterion, choose/edit a teacher-written comment block, add one personal next step, then export…
rubric-comment-queue.why: Review teacher-written feedback, personalize every comment, and export when it is ready.
rubric-comment-queue.detail: Web app: import plain text or paste excerpts, attach a rubric criterion, choose/edit a teacher-written comment block, add one personal next step, then export CSV/clipboard. Non-goals: essay scoring, plagiarism detection, student profiling, and automatic AI feedback.
rubric-comment-queue.user: A teacher who must give humane, consistent writing feedback to many students while retaining control over every comment.
rubric-comment-queue.distinct: It accelerates teacher-authored feedback selection and personalization, rather than being a thin LLM essay grader.
rubric-comment-queue.workaround: Copy/paste comment banks in documents, use rubrics in an LMS, or hand off first-pass feedback to opaque AI tools.

rubric-feedback-bundles.title: Rubric Feedback Bundles
rubric-feedback-bundles.description: Local-first browser tool to select reusable feedback fragments, tailor them per criterion, attach one short personal note, and export a readable student feedbac
rubric-feedback-bundles.detail: Local-first browser tool to select reusable feedback fragments, tailor them per criterion, attach one short personal note, and export a readable student feedback page plus anonymized class misconception summary. Non-goals: essay generation, plagiarism scoring, or automated marks.
rubric-feedback-bundles.user: Writing teachers with many short submissions who need to preserve meaningful, human feedback while avoiding repetitive retyping.
rubric-feedback-bundles.distinct: It accelerates human judgment and preserves full student language rather than generating generic feedback at scale.
rubric-feedback-bundles.workaround: Copy/paste boilerplate comments, mark only a sample, use generic AI feedback, or leave feedback in separate documents.

rubric-revision-loop.title: Rubric Revision Loop
rubric-revision-loop.description: Teacher-created rubric-code library, pasteable short feedback links, student revision checklist with before/after excerpt, and teacher review queue. Non-goals…
rubric-revision-loop.why: Turn reusable teacher rubric codes into concrete student revision evidence.
rubric-revision-loop.detail: Teacher-created rubric-code library, pasteable short feedback links, student revision checklist with before/after excerpt, and teacher review queue. Non-goals: essay generation, plagiarism detection, grading automation, or LMS replacement.
rubric-revision-loop.user: Teachers with a large writing-feedback load who need to give reusable, criterion-specific feedback and make the student's next revision visible without outsourcing judgment to an LLM.
rubric-revision-loop.distinct: It scales a teacher's reasons and revision dialogue rather than producing synthetic feedback or acting as an LMS.
rubric-revision-loop.workaround: Write repeated comments in Docs/LMS, use generic comment banks, or accept AI feedback that is hard to calibrate and explain.

s3-console.title: Backend-agnostic web console for any S3-compatible object store
s3-console.description: Manage S3-compatible storage from your browser with an isolated sample workspace.
s3-console.why: Browse and manage any S3-compatible storage from your browser.
s3-console.detail: v1 is a static single-page app (also shipped as a tiny Docker image) that stores endpoint credentials in the browser only and offers: bucket list/create/delete, object browse with prefix folders, multipart upload/download, delete, metadata/tags, bucket policy JSON editor, CORS and lifecycle rule editors, versioning toggle, and a presigned-URL generator — all via standard S3 calls through the AWS SDK. It deliberately does not implement user/IAM management (backend-specific), metrics, replication, or any server component in v1.
s3-console.user: Self-hoster or small-ops engineer running Garage, RustFS, SeaweedFS, Ceph RGW, Versity or a cloud bucket who lost MinIO's community console and needs a browser UI for buckets, objects, policies, lifecycle, CORS and presigned URLs.
s3-console.distinct: Existing consoles are each welded to one vendor's admin API; a console built only on the public S3 API is by construction portable across the whole post-MinIO ecosystem, which is exactly what the threads ask for.
s3-console.workaround: mc/aws CLI, the stale OpenMaxIO fork (MinIO-only, last push 2025-06), Filestash (general file manager, not an admin console), Cyberduck/S3 Browser desktop apps.

s3-dir-dev-server.title: Local S3-compatible dev server that maps a plain directory, with a built-in UI
s3-dir-dev-server.description: Run a local S3-compatible server from an ordinary directory for development and tests.
s3-dir-dev-server.detail: v1: `s3dir serve ./data --port 9000` exposes the core S3 API (buckets, Put/Get/Head/Delete/List v2, multipart, presigned GET/PUT, CORS, basic metadata/tags via sidecar files) and a `/ui` route embedding the s3-console SPA; a Docker image, a `--seed` flag for fixtures, and a `--events` webhook for object-created notifications so apps that consume S3 events can be tested. Not in v1: IAM, versioning, replication, erasure coding, production performance, or resolving the `foo` vs `foo/bar` POSIX-conflict edge cases beyond documenting them.
s3-dir-dev-server.user: Application developer who needs `docker compose up` to give them an S3 endpoint for local dev/tests that stores objects as normal files on disk and lets them inspect/edit them in a browser.
s3-dir-dev-server.distinct: Every existing option is either a production object store pressed into dev duty or a headless mock; a directory-backed, UI-included, dev-first server is the concrete thing asked for three times in one year.
s3-dir-dev-server.workaround: MinIO images pinned to old tags, LocalStack (heavy), rclone serve s3 (experimental, no UI, metadata lost), Garage (cluster-oriented, no UI), Versity gateway (no UI), s3proxy (JVM).

sampling-budget-coordinator.title: Sampling Budget Coordinator
sampling-budget-coordinator.description: Set safe OpenTelemetry sampling goals as fleet replicas change.
sampling-budget-coordinator.why: Set safe per-instance OpenTelemetry sampling goals and block deployments that exceed one fleet budget.
sampling-budget-coordinator.detail: A CLI that reads collector configs and replica counts, estimates effective head/tail sampling volume, recommends safe per-instance goals, and emits a deploy-time budget assertion. Non-goals: receiving traces, replacing collectors, or providing an observability backend.
sampling-budget-coordinator.user: Platform engineers operating multiple OpenTelemetry collectors who need to keep tail-sampling volume within a real fleet-wide budget as instances scale up and down.
sampling-budget-coordinator.distinct: It audits the economics of sampling configuration rather than becoming a telemetry collector or dashboard.
sampling-budget-coordinator.workaround: Guess a per-instance fraction, manually divide by replica count, or accept surprise ingestion spikes after autoscaling.

sandbox-capacity-probe.title: Sandbox Capacity Probe
sandbox-capacity-probe.description: Measure safe Docker or Podman container capacity before rollout with a bounded local probe.
sandbox-capacity-probe.why: Measure a safe Docker or Podman container scale before rollout, with a bounded local capacity probe.
sandbox-capacity-probe.detail: A CLI that launches bounded synthetic containers against a chosen Docker/Podman host, records startup percentiles and rule counts, and writes a capacity envelope. Non-goals: running untrusted agent code, cluster orchestration, or stress testing third-party systems.
sandbox-capacity-probe.user: Teams running many isolated agent or customer containers who need a repeatable preflight showing whether networking, ports, mounts, and startup latency will remain safe at planned scale.
sandbox-capacity-probe.distinct: It measures the operational envelope of a sandbox design rather than offering another sandbox runtime.
sandbox-capacity-probe.workaround: Load-test a staging host late, read runtime logs after startup slows, or impose arbitrary container and port limits.

scaled-cook-card.title: Scaled Cook Card
scaled-cook-card.description: Scale recipe servings and see the right amount in every cooking step.
scaled-cook-card.why: Scale a recipe and keep each cooking step linked to its ingredients.
scaled-cook-card.detail: Static/offline web app that imports a small YAML/JSON recipe, scales servings, renders bound ingredient tokens in each step, and saves actual yield/substitutions locally. Non-goals: web recipe scraping, meal planning, nutrition claims, or social recipe publishing.
scaled-cook-card.user: A home cook scaling a familiar recipe who needs every preparation step to retain the correctly scaled ingredient quantities while cooking hands-free.
scaled-cook-card.distinct: It treats a recipe as a live, scaled procedure rather than a collection to browse.
scaled-cook-card.workaround: Do arithmetic while cooking, annotate screenshots, or repeatedly scroll between an ingredient list and steps.

scan-count-pad.title: Scan Count Pad
scan-count-pad.description: Offline PWA: import SKU/barcode CSV, choose a count session, scan/tap quantity, flag unknowns and variance, then export adjustments as CSV. Non-goals: POS, supp
scan-count-pad.detail: Offline PWA: import SKU/barcode CSV, choose a count session, scan/tap quantity, flag unknowns and variance, then export adjustments as CSV. Non-goals: POS, supplier ordering, live multi-site inventory, or camera-based AI recognition.
scan-count-pad.user: A single-location shop or maker that needs to count/adjust stock at the shelf with a phone or Bluetooth scanner, even when connectivity is poor.
scan-count-pad.distinct: It is a deliberately narrow physical stock-count tool, not an inventory database or POS clone.
scan-count-pad.workaround: Use a paper tally then spreadsheet, type product names into a web inventory app, or buy a POS/ERP scanner module.

scan-reading-pack.title: Scan Reading Pack
scan-reading-pack.description: An offline desktop/PWA flow for image-only PDFs: OCR locally, produce Markdown/EPUB-like HTML with page anchors and extracted figures, queue low-confidence…
scan-reading-pack.why: Turn scanned pages into a reading pack.
scan-reading-pack.detail: An offline desktop/PWA flow for image-only PDFs: OCR locally, produce Markdown/EPUB-like HTML with page anchors and extracted figures, queue low-confidence lines, and export SSML/plain text. Non-goals: cloud LLM correction, DRM removal, or hosting copyrighted books.
scan-reading-pack.user: Readers with scanned books or reports who need trustworthy selectable text and an audiobook-ready package while retaining page references to the original scan.
scan-reading-pack.distinct: The valuable output is a verifiable reading package with source-page traceability, not an opaque AI transcription wrapper.
scan-reading-pack.workaround: Run conventional OCR, copy pages into a chat model, or create text and images separately with no reliable page mapping.

scan-repair-local.title: Scan Repair Local
scan-repair-local.description: Offline desktop/PWA tool that detects skew/blur/contrast, previews reversible repairs, runs local OCR, and exports searchable PDF plus Markdown with page…
scan-repair-local.why: Repair scanned pages and extract text locally for readers and researchers with archival PDFs.
scan-repair-local.detail: Offline desktop/PWA tool that detects skew/blur/contrast, previews reversible repairs, runs local OCR, and exports searchable PDF plus Markdown with page references. Non-goals: cloud document storage, LLM chat, or perfect handwriting recognition.
scan-repair-local.user: Readers and researchers with scanned books or archival PDFs who need usable text without uploading sensitive material.
scan-repair-local.distinct: It is a local quality-and-confidence workflow around OCR, not another generic PDF toolbox or AI summarizer.
scan-repair-local.workaround: Manually crop pages, use a cloud LLM/OCR, or run several disconnected image and OCR tools.

scheduled-run-receipts.title: Scheduled Run Receipts
scheduled-run-receipts.description: A CLI plus static viewer that reads an expected schedule, accepts signed run-start/run-finish receipts, detects missing/late/overlapping runs, and exports a wee
scheduled-run-receipts.detail: A CLI plus static viewer that reads an expected schedule, accepts signed run-start/run-finish receipts, detects missing/late/overlapping runs, and exports a weekly HTML evidence page. Non-goals: job scheduling, queue hosting, or alert-routing platform.
scheduled-run-receipts.user: A small-team operator with cron jobs, queues, or scheduled workflows who needs to prove both that a run occurred and that a missed expected run was noticed.
scheduled-run-receipts.distinct: It is an absence detector and evidence trail, not another dashboard that merely displays received pings.
scheduled-run-receipts.workaround: Ping an uptime service from scripts, watch logs manually, or discover the gap through stale downstream data.

schema-drift-snapshot.title: Schema Drift Snapshot
schema-drift-snapshot.description: Read-only CLI that snapshots schema metadata, compares environments, classifies destructive/ORM-invisible differences, and writes a Markdown review. Non-goals…
schema-drift-snapshot.why: Compare PostgreSQL or MySQL schema metadata and explain production drift before repair.
schema-drift-snapshot.detail: Read-only CLI that snapshots schema metadata, compares environments, classifies destructive/ORM-invisible differences, and writes a Markdown review. Non-goals: executing migrations, row-data diffing, or DB hosting.
schema-drift-snapshot.user: Developers with PostgreSQL/MySQL schemas and ORM migrations who need a human-reviewable explanation of production drift before applying a repair.
schema-drift-snapshot.distinct: It is an incident-review artifact for drift, not a new migration framework.
schema-drift-snapshot.workaround: Run ad-hoc schema dumps, use ORM migration status, or compare SQL manually.

scope-deposit-ledger.title: Scope Deposit Ledger
scope-deposit-ledger.description: Offline PWA for one operator: create a scope, record a deposit, allocate it across milestones, and export a client-readable PDF/CSV balance trail. Non-goals…
scope-deposit-ledger.why: Track what each client deposit covers in a private offline ledger.
scope-deposit-ledger.detail: Offline PWA for one operator: create a scope, record a deposit, allocate it across milestones, and export a client-readable PDF/CSV balance trail. Non-goals: payment processing, general ledger, tax filing, or a CRM.
scope-deposit-ledger.user: A solo trade or professional-services operator who takes a deposit or retainer and needs to show exactly which agreed scope it is held against and when it becomes billable.
scope-deposit-ledger.distinct: It is a narrow deposit-to-scope evidence ledger, not an invoice generator or payments clone.
scope-deposit-ledger.workaround: Create a normal invoice, keep a note or spreadsheet of the deposit, then manually apply a credit when the final invoice is sent.

score-aligned-choir-cleanup.title: Score-Aligned Choir Cleanup
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.description: Make rehearsal packs from choir archive recordings with score-marked passages and local cleanup.
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.why: Clean choir recordings against a score.
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.detail: Desktop app that imports audio plus a MusicXML/PDF section map, lets the user mark rehearsal passages, applies transparent local noise/EQ presets, and exports labeled excerpts with an edit receipt. Non-goals: voice cloning, generative replacement vocals, automatic perfect source separation, or cloud storage.
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.user: Community choirs preserving archival recordings when they have the score but need a cautious, local way to make rehearsal copies easier to hear.
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.distinct: It connects careful restoration to rehearsal structure instead of pretending a generic AI enhancer can recreate a lost performance.
score-aligned-choir-cleanup.workaround: Try generic denoisers, manually cut and label sections in Audacity, pay a restoration engineer, or accept an archive that is hard to rehearse from.

screen-landmark-lens.title: Screen Landmark Lens
screen-landmark-lens.description: Find visible labels that screen readers miss in older and remote software.
screen-landmark-lens.why: Find and read visible controls in one chosen window on your computer.
screen-landmark-lens.detail: A desktop app that captures only a user-selected window, runs local OCR, and offers keyboard shortcuts for ‘read visible labels’, ‘find text’, and ‘describe likely buttons’ with a simple directional cue. Non-goals: remote control, autonomous clicking, cloud image upload, or medical interpretation.
screen-landmark-lens.user: A blind or low-vision worker using remote desktops, legacy apps, or inaccessible job software who needs to find and activate a visible control without that app exposing accessibility metadata.
screen-landmark-lens.distinct: It is an on-demand visual landmark finder for inaccessible rendered software, not a general chatbot or another screen reader.
screen-landmark-lens.workaround: Ask another person, use OCR plus trial-and-error keyboard navigation, or abandon the inaccessible workflow.

screen-reader-smoke-test.title: Announce Check
screen-reader-smoke-test.description: Compare keyboard focus and status messages before releasing a critical web flow.
screen-reader-smoke-test.why: Check one browser flow for changed keyboard focus and status messages before release.
screen-reader-smoke-test.detail: NPM CLI plus local HTML reporter that drives a short scripted browser flow, captures accessibility-tree/ARIA-live changes, compares them to a checked-in expected transcript, and points to the first divergence. Non-goals: emulating every screen reader, hosted testing SaaS, or WCAG certification.
screen-reader-smoke-test.user: Small web teams that need to verify the screen-reader announcements of one critical signup, search, or form flow before release.
screen-reader-smoke-test.distinct: It narrows the problem to an approval-friendly announcement contract, not an opaque accessibility score or a full automation framework.
screen-reader-smoke-test.workaround: Run manual VoiceOver/NVDA checks late, rely on linting, or adopt a larger automation library and write custom harnesses.

screenreader-task-audit.title: Screenreader Task Audit
screenreader-task-audit.description: Record screen-reader task evidence and review blockers in priority order.
screenreader-task-audit.why: Test a task with a screen reader and record the result.
screenreader-task-audit.detail: A privacy-preserving web app that lets a team define five critical tasks, captures a screen-reader tester's structured observations and optional local event trace, then outputs a prioritized reproducible report. Non-goals: automated accessibility certification, remote surveillance, or synthetic speech testing.
screenreader-task-audit.user: Blind founders and small product teams who need to demonstrate whether essential dashboard tasks can actually be completed with a screen reader.
screenreader-task-audit.distinct: It centers lived task evidence from a screen-reader user, filling the gap automated scanners explicitly cannot cover.
screenreader-task-audit.workaround: Run automated scans, ask a consultant for a broad audit, or rely on sighted colleagues to complete essential tasks.

scrubbed-log-casefile.title: Scrubbed Log Casefile
scrubbed-log-casefile.description: Scrub incident logs locally into encrypted casefiles before sharing.
scrubbed-log-casefile.why: Prepare a redacted log case for support.
scrubbed-log-casefile.detail: An offline CLI that applies named redaction policies, preserves stable placeholders across logs/configs/traces, records what rule fired without values, and produces a shareable encrypted zip plus manifest. Non-goals: log hosting, LLM analysis, or centralized SIEM.
scrubbed-log-casefile.user: Engineers escalating a bug to a vendor, teammate, or issue tracker who need a useful log bundle without leaking passwords, identifiers, or configuration.
scrubbed-log-casefile.distinct: The product is a safe, reproducible bug-handoff artifact, not an observability backend or generic redactor.
scrubbed-log-casefile.workaround: Run regex replacement, paste a subset of logs into a ticket, or trust a third-party incident/SaaS tool's masking rules.

season-gap-garden.title: Season Gap Garden
season-gap-garden.description: Offline bed list, sow/transplant/expected-clear dates, a calendar strip showing open windows, user-defined successor templates, and season CSV export.…
season-gap-garden.why: Spot open bed windows and plan what comes next using your own garden dates.
season-gap-garden.detail: Offline bed list, sow/transplant/expected-clear dates, a calendar strip showing open windows, user-defined successor templates, and season CSV export. Non-goals: weather prediction, plant marketplace, companion-plant claims, automated agronomy.
season-gap-garden.user: A small-space food gardener who wants to spot an empty bed window and choose a simple follow-on crop from their own past planting notes.
season-gap-garden.distinct: A crop-turnover planner for one gardener’s real beds, not a CAD garden designer or generic gardening content app.
season-gap-garden.workaround: Draw a bed plan, keep planting dates in a notebook, and manually work out what can follow a harvested crop.

secret-exposure-path.title: Secret Exposure Path
secret-exposure-path.description: Trace declared credentials before they reach logs, Git diffs, or build artifacts.
secret-exposure-path.why: Trace where a secret can leak through a project.
secret-exposure-path.detail: A shell/CI wrapper that traces declared workspace outputs, detects secret-shaped values and taint propagation into staged diffs/log files/artifacts, then emits a redacted path graph. Non-goals: recovering leaked secrets, acting as a vault, or monitoring all user activity.
secret-exposure-path.user: Teams using coding agents and CI who need to see where a credential can travel—from local file to git diff, log, artifact, or prompt—before it leaks.
secret-exposure-path.distinct: It exposes how a secret travels, rather than becoming another static repository scanner.
secret-exposure-path.workaround: Use gitleaks/pre-commit, ignore .env files, and react to scanner alerts after a secret is already in a diff or repository history.

secret-finding-triage.title: Secret Finding Triage
secret-finding-triage.description: A CLI that consumes SARIF/JSON findings, renders a local HTML/Markdown triage card with line-numbered masked context, entropy/type clues, and a signed…
secret-finding-triage.why: Turn SARIF and Gitleaks findings into locally masked evidence cards with signed resolution records.
secret-finding-triage.detail: A CLI that consumes SARIF/JSON findings, renders a local HTML/Markdown triage card with line-numbered masked context, entropy/type clues, and a signed resolution record. Non-goals: scanning repositories, rotating credentials, or cloud issue tracking.
secret-finding-triage.user: Security-conscious developers handling secret-scanner findings who need enough safe context to decide whether a finding is real without pasting source into an external ticket or chat.
secret-finding-triage.distinct: It improves the evidence quality of a scanner finding without becoming another scanner or secret vault.
secret-finding-triage.workaround: Open the source locally, paste snippets into tickets, broadly allowlist noisy rules, or close findings with little audit trail.

secret-injection-diff.title: Secret Injection Diff
secret-injection-diff.description: Check secret-name access before code merges.
secret-injection-diff.why: Compare how secrets enter two builds.
secret-injection-diff.detail: Local CLI that parses declared env, Compose, CI, and Kubernetes manifests; reports only secret identifiers and recipient boundaries; fails CI when an undeclared recipient gains a secret. Non-goals: secret storage, decryption, value scanning, agent monitoring, or outbound telemetry.
secret-injection-diff.user: A developer using IDEs, CI, and deployment tools who needs to prove which process receives which secret names and whether that scope changed in a pull request.
secret-injection-diff.distinct: It audits injection scope and change review, not secret storage or another environment-variable manager.
secret-injection-diff.workaround: Read CI YAML and shell profiles manually, use broad env files, or trust a secret manager without an end-to-end recipient view.

secret-sync-preflight.title: Secret Sync Preflight
secret-sync-preflight.description: Check secret key drift before deployment with a local CLI for DevOps teams.
secret-sync-preflight.detail: CLI reads a key-only desired manifest and provider exports, highlights missing/extra/renamed keys, detects destination limits and dangerous delete plans, and emits CI annotations without reading values. Non-goals: storing or rotating secret values, replacing a secret manager, or automatic remediation.
secret-sync-preflight.user: A DevOps developer moving configuration through IaC, a secret manager, CI, and hosting providers who needs to detect missing, excess, stale, or provider-limited secrets before deployment.
secret-sync-preflight.distinct: It is a cross-layer safety check, not another vault or an AI-generated configuration assistant.
secret-sync-preflight.workaround: Compare provider consoles by hand, keep an unreliable spreadsheet, or discover drift only when an application fails to start.

seed-sprint.title: Seed Sprint
seed-sprint.description: Race friends on one shared five-minute signal puzzle, then compare results by link.
seed-sprint.why: Rotate tiles to connect signals before the timer ends in a daily puzzle.
seed-sprint.detail: A single daily 6x6 signal-routing puzzle: rotate a limited set of tiles to connect sources before the clock. Finish screen produces a spoiler-safe colored result card and an optional room link where friends race the identical seed. Non-goals: infinite puzzle feed, chat, user accounts, or paid hints.
seed-sprint.user: Puzzle friends who want to compare a five-minute daily result on the same fair board, with a link instead of an account or a real-time appointment.
seed-sprint.distinct: It makes the shared seed and spoiler-safe comparison primary, rather than cloning a word puzzle's vocabulary mechanic.
seed-sprint.workaround: Screenshot a Wordle-style score, coordinate in a group chat, or use an app-specific friend system.

self-study-checkpoints.title: Self-Study Checkpoints
self-study-checkpoints.description: Plan self-study checkpoints for reviewer feedback and export a change-checked packet.
self-study-checkpoints.why: Plan a self-study checkpoint, ask a reviewer for feedback, and export a completion packet.
self-study-checkpoints.detail: A static-web checkpoint builder: define a syllabus slice, target date, problem set links, proof/code submission prompts, and an invited reviewer rubric; export a signed completion packet. Non-goals: issuing accredited credentials, auto-solving proofs, or proctoring.
self-study-checkpoints.user: A serious independent math or computer-science learner who needs an externally legible way to prove progress through a difficult topic without enrolling in a full course.
self-study-checkpoints.distinct: It supplies commitment and evidence around self-study, not another content library or AI answer engine.
self-study-checkpoints.workaround: Follow a textbook alone, solve selected exercises, join an expensive course, or publish informal notes without a coherent mastery record.

self-study-proofbook.title: Self-Study Proofbook
self-study-proofbook.description: Record cited problems, timed attempts, and revisions in a private offline ledger.
self-study-proofbook.why: Keep evidence of work completed while studying.
self-study-proofbook.detail: Local Markdown-first proof/problem ledger with source citation, attempt timer, solution revision history, and printable mastery index. Non-goals: proctoring, grading claims, credential issuance, or answer generation.
self-study-proofbook.user: Serious self-learners in math or CS who need a credible, private record of what they can actually solve rather than a course-completion badge.
self-study-proofbook.distinct: It records evidence of deliberate practice rather than pretending to certify knowledge or solve problems for the learner.
self-study-proofbook.workaround: Keep a notebook, copy exam PDFs into a folder, post isolated questions online, or collect course certificates.

selfhost-observability-fit.title: Observability Fit Check
selfhost-observability-fit.description: CLI that ingests a bounded OTLP sample, estimates cardinality/storage/query load, and emits comparable local compose profiles and retention budgets. Non-goals…
selfhost-observability-fit.why: Estimate self-hosted observability storage, cardinality, and resource fit from a local OTLP sample.
selfhost-observability-fit.detail: CLI that ingests a bounded OTLP sample, estimates cardinality/storage/query load, and emits comparable local compose profiles and retention budgets. Non-goals: hosted telemetry or a benchmark leaderboard.
selfhost-observability-fit.user: A solo operator or small platform team choosing a self-hosted observability stack who needs to test resource and retention fit before committing production telemetry.
selfhost-observability-fit.distinct: It is a neutral fit and capacity test, rather than a competing observability backend.
selfhost-observability-fit.workaround: Read comparison blogs, deploy several stacks, and guess from VM recommendations.

selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.title: Self-Host Upgrade Rehearsal
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.description: Rehearse self-hosted upgrades and issue customer-safe readiness receipts.
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.why: Rehearse Compose or Kubernetes upgrades and issue customer-safe readiness receipts.
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.detail: A distributable CLI kit that validates a declared Compose/Kubernetes upgrade path in an ephemeral environment: captures config schema changes, backup/restore result, required disk/memory, and produces a customer-safe readiness report. Non-goals: a control plane, hosting, remote access, or automatic customer upgrades.
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.user: A small company offering or operating a Docker-based self-hosted product that must make upgrades supportable across unknown customer environments.
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.distinct: It is an upgrade proof kit for vendors, not another self-hosted deployment dashboard.
selfhost-upgrade-rehearsal.workaround: Tell users to back up manually, maintain a large compatibility wiki, or only test the vendor’s own Compose setup.

service-notification-router.title: Service Notification Router
service-notification-router.description: Self-hosted rules endpoint: receive a normalized booking email/webhook, map service/provider to a recipient, add a minimal acknowledgment link, and purge…
service-notification-router.why: Route each booking notice to the one coordinator responsible for it.
service-notification-router.detail: Self-hosted rules endpoint: receive a normalized booking email/webhook, map service/provider to a recipient, add a minimal acknowledgment link, and purge payloads after a configured interval. Non-goals: booking pages, WhatsApp scraping, marketing messages, or workforce management.
service-notification-router.user: A micro-clinic, studio, or multi-service office where a booking must alert the right service coordinator without giving every staff member every booking notification.
service-notification-router.distinct: It is a narrow responsibility router for already-created bookings, not a scheduler or generic automation canvas.
service-notification-router.workaround: Forward all booking email to a shared inbox or WhatsApp group, manually forward it, or use an expensive scheduler tier/automation service.

service-proof-loop.title: Service Proof Loop
service-proof-loop.description: Send visit proof and carry approved extras into the next recurring visit.
service-proof-loop.why: Send proof after a service visit and record the client’s response.
service-proof-loop.detail: Technician upload/checklist, client proof page, one-tap accept/problem/rating, configurable extras, and automatic attachment to the next recurring job export. Non-goals: dispatch, payments, payroll, public-review solicitation campaigns, or worker tracking.
service-proof-loop.user: Recurring cleaning and maintenance businesses that need post-job proof, client feedback, and approved extras to flow into the next visit without building a custom customer portal.
service-proof-loop.distinct: The product closes the operational loop from completed visit to an actionable next visit, not just feedback collection or a generic client portal.
service-proof-loop.workaround: Text photos, ask for reviews manually, retain notes in a CRM, and retype client requests into the next job card.

session-layout-capsule.title: Session Layout Capsule
session-layout-capsule.description: Local web dashboard that saves named layouts of tabs, MIDI cue panels, timers, and text notes; offers a restore checklist and a printable QR handoff.…
session-layout-capsule.why: Save and restore the links, MIDI cues, timers, and notes around a creative session.
session-layout-capsule.detail: Local web dashboard that saves named layouts of tabs, MIDI cue panels, timers, and text notes; offers a restore checklist and a printable QR handoff. Non-goals: controlling arbitrary desktop windows, cloud sync, or DAW project parsing.
session-layout-capsule.user: A home producer or live visualist who reopens a project and needs their auxiliary controls in the same spatial arrangement immediately.
session-layout-capsule.distinct: It preserves a creative session's intent across lightweight tools, rather than pretending a browser can replace a window manager.
session-layout-capsule.workaround: Take screenshots, reopen and reposition windows manually, or write one-off scripts and configs.

set-context-log.title: Set Context Log
set-context-log.description: Log lifting-set context, then review it before your next session.
set-context-log.why: Record weight, reps, effort, and set context. Review the previous session before your next set.
set-context-log.detail: Offline PWA with a fast set row (weight, reps, RPE, one-tap caveat), a next-session recall card, and CSV/JSON export. Non-goals: workout programming marketplace, social feed, wearable sync, nutrition logging.
set-context-log.user: A self-directed lifter who needs to record what changed a set—not just weight and reps—so the next workout has usable context.
set-context-log.distinct: It is a decision-memory layer for lifting, not another exercise catalog or AI workout generator.
set-context-log.workaround: Put a cryptic note in a phone app or general notes app, or remember it until the next session.

set-note-progression.title: Set Note Progression
set-note-progression.description: Save set details and use rule chips to choose the next load.
set-note-progression.why: Log workout sets and get a visible rule for your next progression.
set-note-progression.detail: Offline workout log with an exercise template, per-set text chips, rep ranges, and a deterministic 'hold/add reps/increase' suggestion that always exposes its rule. Non-goals: generated workouts, social leaderboards, wearables, or medical injury advice.
set-note-progression.user: A recreational lifter who needs to retain the reason behind each set and apply a repeatable double-progression rule next session.
set-note-progression.distinct: It makes the explanation for progression first-class instead of competing as a general workout-plan generator.
set-note-progression.workaround: Put cryptic annotations in a session note, use a spreadsheet, or decide increases from memory.

shared-piano-takebook.title: Takebook
shared-piano-takebook.description: Web MIDI piano-roll recorder: record up to 60 seconds, loop a marked bar range, attach a teacher note, and export standard MIDI/WAV. Non-goals: notation…
shared-piano-takebook.why: Record, annotate, loop, and export short piano practice takes without a DAW.
shared-piano-takebook.detail: Web MIDI piano-roll recorder: record up to 60 seconds, loop a marked bar range, attach a teacher note, and export standard MIDI/WAV. Non-goals: notation engraving, collaboration server, licensed sounds.
shared-piano-takebook.user: Music teachers and pairs practicing a short piano phrase together who need to keep, annotate, and reopen takes without a DAW.
shared-piano-takebook.distinct: A take-and-feedback utility, not a generic online piano or a DAW clone.
shared-piano-takebook.workaround: Use Shared Piano then screen-record, download files manually, or move to a full DAW.

shelf-rotation-picklist.title: Shelf Rotation Picklist
shelf-rotation-picklist.description: Pick neglected board games that fit tonight’s players, time, and setup.
shelf-rotation-picklist.why: Pick neglected board games that fit tonight's players, time, and setup.
shelf-rotation-picklist.detail: Local CSV/manual import of title, last-played, player range, minutes, setup friction, and tags; filters tonight's constraints and creates a 3–5 game rotation with a visible reason for each pick. Non-goals: recommendations from scraped ratings, marketplace prices, or full collection management.
shelf-rotation-picklist.user: A board gamer with a growing shelf who wants a fair, practical next-play shortlist based on neglect, player count, setup burden, and what is actually available tonight.
shelf-rotation-picklist.distinct: It converts neglected owned items into a constraint-aware play plan, rather than duplicating a game library.
shelf-rotation-picklist.workaround: Scroll a collection, spin a randomizer, use a spreadsheet, or never revisit the shelf-of-shame.

shop-fit-sheet.title: Shop Fit Sheet
shop-fit-sheet.description: Check a fitted build before buying sheet material.
shop-fit-sheet.why: Check cabinet clearances, panels, doors, and sheet material before you buy.
shop-fit-sheet.detail: Offline web calculator for outer envelope, openings, panel thickness, supports, clearances, and stock list; export one printable build sheet. Non-goals: 3D CAD, CNC/G-code, structural engineering certification, or a materials marketplace.
shop-fit-sheet.user: Home makers fitting a cabinet, bench, or storage build into a garage, utility room, or vehicle who need a constraint-first cut/material brief before buying stock.
shop-fit-sheet.distinct: It is a pre-build constraint checker for physically fitted home projects, not a general CAD clone or a bin-packing-only cut-list generator.
shop-fit-sheet.workaround: Measure on paper, use a full CAD package, make a generic cut list, and mentally track clearances and hardware constraints.

shopping-list-handoff.title: Shopping List Handoff
shopping-list-handoff.description: Turn pasted ingredients into a handoff card.
shopping-list-handoff.why: Turn ingredients into one clear, checkable shopping list.
shopping-list-handoff.detail: Static local web page that turns pasted ingredients or a neutral recipe bundle into a concise, unit-normalized, checkable handoff card with print, plain-text, QR, and expiration-free local file options. Non-goals: retailer ordering, user accounts, live collaborative sync, or automatic web recipe extraction.
shopping-list-handoff.user: A household cook who needs to hand a precise shopping list to someone who does not use the same meal-planning app.
shopping-list-handoff.distinct: It optimizes the handoff boundary between users and apps rather than duplicating a full grocery-list platform.
shopping-list-handoff.workaround: Screenshots, copied text, SMS messages, paper lists, or persuading every shopper to install the same app.

sideload-readiness.title: Sideload Readiness
sideload-readiness.description: Check an Android device before updating an approved sideloaded app.
sideload-readiness.why: Check whether an Android device is ready for an approved sideloaded update.
sideload-readiness.detail: Signed desktop CLI with brew/winget/scoop installers that runs read-only adb diagnostics, checks developer options, storage, USB mode, package signer continuity and recovery visibility, then emits a shareable report and recovery checklist. Non-goals: bypassing platform controls, bootloader unlocks, or distributing APKs.
sideload-readiness.user: Android power users and small IT teams who need to determine whether a device can safely install, update, and recover approved sideloaded software under changing Android rules.
sideload-readiness.distinct: A diagnostic and recovery planner, rather than an alternative app store or a sideloading circumvention tool.
sideload-readiness.workaround: Users search forums, run ad-hoc adb commands, discover signing or storage failures after an attempted update, and keep undocumented manual steps.

silent-focus-sentinel.title: Silent Focus Sentinel
silent-focus-sentinel.description: Catch silent or repeated VoiceOver focus stops in iOS Simulator runs.
silent-focus-sentinel.detail: An iOS simulator-focused CLI that records a scripted focus traversal, flags focusable nodes with empty/duplicate announcements, and emits a compact JSON/HTML diff. Non-goals: a full mobile test framework, physical-device automation, or uploading app screens.
silent-focus-sentinel.user: Mobile app teams and VoiceOver users who need to catch focus stops that announce nothing before a release makes navigation confusing.
silent-focus-sentinel.distinct: It tests the sequence a screen-reader user experiences—especially silence—not merely whether accessibility attributes exist.
silent-focus-sentinel.workaround: Manually swipe every screen with VoiceOver, record a video, and inspect platform accessibility tools after a user finds a regression.

sim-lab-replay.title: Sim Lab Replay
sim-lab-replay.description: Embeddable JS recorder that captures named controls/events (not student identity), lets authors add prediction/observation prompts, and exports a…
sim-lab-replay.why: Record a browser simulation’s reasoning path and export an accessible replay lesson.
sim-lab-replay.detail: Embeddable JS recorder that captures named controls/events (not student identity), lets authors add prediction/observation prompts, and exports a self-contained replay lesson. Non-goals: physics engine, LMS, grading, or student surveillance.
sim-lab-replay.user: Teachers and independent simulation makers who need to turn an exploratory physics/orbit simulation into a short, shareable experiment that students can replay and explain.
sim-lab-replay.distinct: It packages the reasoning path through a simulation, rather than cloning a simulation library or bolting an LLM onto worksheets.
sim-lab-replay.workaround: Share a bare URL and verbal instructions, take screenshots, or prepare a slide deck that loses the interactive evidence.

sing-to-controller.title: Sing Switch
sing-to-controller.description: An in-browser calibrator that maps pitch bands, onset, sustained sound, and silence to a virtual controller state and exports a compact JSON mapping or…
sing-to-controller.why: Turn vocal pitch and held notes into inspectable browser game controls—locally, without training a model.
sing-to-controller.detail: An in-browser calibrator that maps pitch bands, onset, sustained sound, and silence to a virtual controller state and exports a compact JSON mapping or WebSocket stream. Non-goals: speech recognition, identity/biometric analysis, music generation, or competitive-game anti-cheat.
sing-to-controller.user: Experimental game makers, music teachers, and accessible-play designers who want to map simple vocal pitch and sustained-note gestures to browser game controls without training a model or installing audio middleware.
sing-to-controller.distinct: It is a transparent input adapter for expressive control, not a voice AI wrapper or virtual instrument clone.
sing-to-controller.workaround: Hand-roll microphone analysis, use keyboard emulation, add a MIDI device, or abandon unusual input after engine action mapping fails.

skill-decision-drills.title: Skill Decision Drills
skill-decision-drills.description: Rehearse real choices with browser-saved drills for coaches and self-learners.
skill-decision-drills.why: Practise choices from real situations as a coach or learner.
skill-decision-drills.detail: Offline scenario editor/player: author a decision tree with photo/text prompts, consequences, hint path, and debrief; replay with randomized branches and export aggregate misconception counts. Non-goals: regulated safety certification, scoring real-world competence, or a content marketplace.
skill-decision-drills.user: Coaches and self-learners in procedural skills who need to rehearse decisions from real scenarios, not memorize isolated facts.
skill-decision-drills.distinct: It generalizes the useful branching-repertoire mechanic to learner-authored decisions rather than cloning a quiz app or chess trainer.
skill-decision-drills.workaround: Rewatch lectures, memorize rules on cards, use instructor-led role-play, or build one-off scenario slides.

skill-drill-studio.title: Skill Drill Studio
skill-drill-studio.description: A static web authoring tool for three drill types—ordered steps, exact command input, and image hotspot—with deterministic answer checks and shareable JSON…
skill-drill-studio.why: Build short procedural drills with deterministic feedback, then share them as portable JSON files.
skill-drill-studio.detail: A static web authoring tool for three drill types—ordered steps, exact command input, and image hotspot—with deterministic answer checks and shareable JSON files. Non-goals: arbitrary code execution, AI question generation, LMS replacement, or student profiles.
skill-drill-studio.user: A teacher, bootcamp instructor, or self-learner who needs to turn a small procedural skill into short browser drills with immediate deterministic feedback.
skill-drill-studio.distinct: It is constrained active-practice authoring for procedural skills, not a generic quiz builder or an AI worksheet generator.
skill-drill-studio.workaround: Make a custom web page, assign a worksheet, use flashcards for actions, or repeatedly re-read tutorials.

small-business-export-map.title: Export Map
small-business-export-map.description: Prepare CSV files with the columns, separators, numbers, and dates your accountant requested.
small-business-export-map.why: Export before handing them to your accountant.
small-business-export-map.detail: Offline CSV preflight tool with saved recipient profiles, delimiter/decimal/date checks, required-column mapping, visible transformations, and a handoff manifest. Non-goals: bookkeeping, direct accounting integrations, data warehousing, or automatic tax categorization.
small-business-export-map.user: Owners of tiny businesses who need a dependable, accountant-friendly export of admin records without discovering incompatible CSV fields at handoff time.
small-business-export-map.distinct: It validates the handoff boundary between existing tools instead of cloning an accounting system.
small-business-export-map.workaround: Open CSV in a spreadsheet, fix delimiters and decimal columns by hand, then email a version whose transformations are undocumented.

solo-practice-bridge.title: Solo Practice Bridge
solo-practice-bridge.description: Local web workbook with a repertoire goal, one observed obstacle, a timed drill/piece alternation, success cue, spaced revisit dates, and printable…
solo-practice-bridge.why: Connect one music drill to a piece you want to play.
solo-practice-bridge.detail: Local web workbook with a repertoire goal, one observed obstacle, a timed drill/piece alternation, success cue, spaced revisit dates, and printable teacher-ready history. Non-goals: audio grading, generated lessons, subscriptions to a content catalog, or replacing a teacher.
solo-practice-bridge.user: Intermediate self-taught musicians who have lost regular teacher feedback and need a modest, non-AI plan that connects drills to pieces they actually want to play.
solo-practice-bridge.distinct: It scaffolds self-directed reflection and drill-to-repertoire transfer rather than wrapping a chatbot around music lessons.
solo-practice-bridge.workaround: Follow generic exercise videos, maintain an ambitious practice list, or avoid drills and hope repertoire alone closes technique gaps.

solution-trace-practice.title: Show Your Debugging
solution-trace-practice.description: Record each debugging hypothesis, test, fix, and clue before asking a coding assistant.
solution-trace-practice.why: Record a debugging hypothesis and test result before you reveal a fix.
solution-trace-practice.detail: VS Code extension that asks for a one-line hypothesis before reveal, captures test output and the learner's chosen fix, then produces a local 'debugging receipt' for review. Non-goals: code generation, surveillance, grading, or disabling assistants.
solution-trace-practice.user: Beginning developers using AI coding tools who need a lightweight practice constraint that preserves independent diagnosis and debugging skill.
solution-trace-practice.distinct: It is a learner-owned reflection tool that works alongside AI rather than another AI coding assistant.
solution-trace-practice.workaround: Turn off AI entirely, use a paper notebook, or accept generated patches and hope later repetition creates understanding.

song-loop-earcoach.title: Hookback
song-loop-earcoach.description: PWA that accepts a local audio clip, loops an A/B region, records a short microphone or MIDI answer, estimates contour/pitch distance, and keeps a lightweight…
song-loop-earcoach.why: Learn melodies by ear from short clips you choose. Private, local, and offline-ready.
song-loop-earcoach.detail: PWA that accepts a local audio clip, loops an A/B region, records a short microphone or MIDI answer, estimates contour/pitch distance, and keeps a lightweight practice queue. Non-goals: streaming-catalog import, transcription of full songs, social feed, or AI song generation.
song-loop-earcoach.user: Self-taught instrumentalists who want to learn melodies by ear from songs they already like, rather than drill abstract intervals.
song-loop-earcoach.distinct: It teaches transferable musical recall from the learner's own short clips, not another question-bank ear trainer or an LLM music generator.
song-loop-earcoach.workaround: Loop a song in YouTube/Spotify, slow it manually, then check notes against a piano or a generic interval quiz.

songsketch-anykey.title: SongSketch AnyKey
songsketch-anykey.description: PWA with drum grid, free-pitch piano roll, one editable pitch curve, loop/export MIDI and a self-contained HTML share file. Non-goals: stems, VSTs, cloud…
songsketch-anykey.why: Sketch unrestricted melodies, pitch bends, and drum loops in your browser—even offline.
songsketch-anykey.detail: PWA with drum grid, free-pitch piano roll, one editable pitch curve, loop/export MIDI and a self-contained HTML share file. Non-goals: stems, VSTs, cloud accounts, AI composition, and multitrack mixing.
songsketch-anykey.user: A young or returning browser-based songwriter who wants to sketch an any-length melody and drums without being locked to a scale or installing a DAW.
songsketch-anykey.distinct: It is not another prompt-to-song generator or full DAW: the product is deliberately a portable, unrestricted melody sketch surface.
songsketch-anykey.workaround: Chrome Music Lab, scale-constrained sequencers, desktop DAWs, or manually exporting MIDI between tools.

sound-toy-patchcard.title: Patchcard
sound-toy-patchcard.description: Open JSON patch-card format plus embeddable widget that stores named parameters, a tiny waveform preview, optional local WAV render, QR share, and printable…
sound-toy-patchcard.why: Save, share, print, and re-grow the sounds you discover in browser toys with an open patch-card format.
sound-toy-patchcard.detail: Open JSON patch-card format plus embeddable widget that stores named parameters, a tiny waveform preview, optional local WAV render, QR share, and printable card. Non-goals: synthesizer engine, user accounts, sample marketplace, or social network.
sound-toy-patchcard.user: Curious non-musicians and workshop facilitators who make a sound they like in a browser toy and need to save, print, and re-create it without learning a DAW.
sound-toy-patchcard.distinct: It preserves and explains playful sound settings across toys rather than being another browser synth.
sound-toy-patchcard.workaround: Screenshot knobs, screen-record audio, write down settings, or lose the patch on refresh.

source-to-recall-gate.title: Source-to-Recall Gate
source-to-recall-gate.description: Browser extension and PWA that saves a selected passage locally, requires one paraphrase, one cue, and one use-case before export as Markdown/CSV/Anki TSV.…
source-to-recall-gate.why: Turn selected passages into recall prompts by making three deliberate decisions before export.
source-to-recall-gate.detail: Browser extension and PWA that saves a selected passage locally, requires one paraphrase, one cue, and one use-case before export as Markdown/CSV/Anki TSV. Non-goals: web scraping, AI-generated cards, cloud highlight sync, or a reader app.
source-to-recall-gate.user: Students converting highlights into study prompts who need to decide what is worth remembering and encode it as a personally meaningful recall cue before it becomes queue debt.
source-to-recall-gate.distinct: It deliberately reduces card creation and makes encoding quality visible instead of automating more flashcards.
source-to-recall-gate.workaround: Dump highlights into Readwise/Notion, import cloze deletions wholesale, or reread passages on a schedule.

source-trail-workbook.title: Source Trail Workbook
source-trail-workbook.description: Trace each research claim from search query to checked source, evidence, and classroom-ready export.
source-trail-workbook.why: Help students record how a search, checked source, and quotation support a research claim.
source-trail-workbook.detail: Offline-first workbook with structured entries for question, query, source metadata, credibility notes, supporting/contradicting quote, and citation export; teachers can distribute a template JSON file. Non-goals: web scraping, AI research answers, or a reference manager replacement.
source-trail-workbook.user: A humanities instructor teaching undergraduates how to research digitally and needing a repeatable exercise that shows search decisions, source quality, and claims.
source-trail-workbook.distinct: It teaches the reasoning trail behind research, not merely reference collection or AI-powered search.
source-trail-workbook.workaround: Demonstrate browser searches live, ask students to submit a bibliography, and use Zotero/JabRef without capturing how sources or claims were selected.

speak-page-actions.title: Speak Page Actions
speak-page-actions.description: Use your voice or keyboard to activate visible browser controls with review before sensitive clicks.
speak-page-actions.why: Speak visible page actions with review before sensitive clicks.
speak-page-actions.detail: A Chromium extension that enumerates visible, labelled buttons/links/form fields, supports offline grammar for 'click <label>', then shows a confirmation for destructive actions. Non-goals: voice passwords, banking automation, background microphone capture, or a general assistant.
speak-page-actions.user: People with limited vision or hand mobility who need to operate ordinary browser pages by speaking a small, reviewable set of visible actions.
speak-page-actions.distinct: It deliberately narrows voice control to inspectable accessible page actions, avoiding an unreliable, overreaching voice agent.
speak-page-actions.workaround: Use Dragon/Talon/Vimium combinations, numbered-link overlays, keyboard shortcuts, or proprietary browser add-ons.

speaker-lane-captions.title: Caption Lanes
speaker-lane-captions.description: Follow small-group conversations with live captions split into left, centre, and right lanes.
speaker-lane-captions.why: Place live captions in left, centre, and right speaker lanes.
speaker-lane-captions.detail: Android app for tabletop conversations that renders separate caption lanes and coarse left/center/right direction from the phone microphone array; users can lock a lane color or hide low-confidence text. Non-goals: identity/voiceprint recognition, cloud meeting archives, or forensic audio capture.
speaker-lane-captions.user: Deaf and hard-of-hearing people in small in-person groups who need to know which person a live caption belongs to without reading one merged text wall.
speaker-lane-captions.distinct: It is about visual turn-taking structure, not an LLM transcript, translation wrapper, or generic speaker diarization dashboard.
speaker-lane-captions.workaround: Infer speakers from context, manually ask people to identify themselves, use meeting-specific caption products, or read a single mixed transcript.

spend-pulse.title: Spend Pulse
spend-pulse.description: Check weekly spending pace with private entries kept in this browser.
spend-pulse.why: See recent spending as a simple pulse.
spend-pulse.detail: Offline PWA with a weekly discretionary allowance, a one-tap amount entry, a rolling pace indicator, and optional on-device daily/weekly notification. Non-goals: transaction import, account aggregation, investment views, credit products, or AI coaching.
spend-pulse.user: People who repeatedly abandon bloated finance apps but still want a small, private daily or weekly prompt showing whether discretionary spending is on pace.
spend-pulse.distinct: It replaces account-heavy finance dashboards with a single habit loop for spending pace, not a thin chat-based money coach.
spend-pulse.workaround: Ignore the budget until month-end, use a generic reminder, check a bank app, or maintain a manual spreadsheet.

split-pass-through-costs.title: Split Cost Slip
split-pass-through-costs.description: Split supplier bills into billable costs and overhead, then export client-ready records.

split-pass-through-costs.detail: A local PWA where a user photographs or attaches one supplier bill, divides its total into named rows, marks each row billable/non-billable, and exports CSV plus a client-ready pass-through line list. Non-goals: bank sync, OCR guarantees, general ledger, or automatic tax categorization.
split-pass-through-costs.user: Time-and-materials contractors who receive one supplier bill containing both their own costs and client-reimbursable items.
split-pass-through-costs.distinct: The product’s primary artifact is one source bill split into billable and non-billable job costs, rather than another receipt scanner.
split-pass-through-costs.workaround: Enter the transaction once with a vague category, duplicate it into multiple expenses, or keep billable portions in a separate spreadsheet before recreating them on an invoice.

sprite-frame-lab.title: Frame UV Lab

sprite-frame-lab.user: 2D game artists and shader-capable developers who need a visual, reliable way to apply per-frame effects to sprite sheets and UI icons without hand-deriving UV math.
sprite-frame-lab.distinct: It turns a subtle asset-coordinate problem into a visual test bench rather than replacing a game engine.
sprite-frame-lab.workaround: Pass UV uniforms manually, duplicate image assets, write one-off shader code, or crop icons externally.

sqlite-sync-guard.distinct: It makes existing file sync safer instead of claiming to solve distributed SQLite synchronization.
sqlite-sync-guard.workaround: Exclude the database, close the app before sync, hope WAL files are stable, or replace sync with a bespoke server database.

sqlite-workload-lab.title: SQLite Workload Lab

sqlite-workload-lab.detail: A CLI that executes declarative SQLite workloads in containers or QEMU profiles, captures SQLite version/compile options/PRAGMAs/query plans/CPU flags, and generates a diffable Markdown/JSON report. Non-goals: a database ORM, hosted benchmark farm, or automatic query tuning.

sqlite-workload-lab.distinct: It is a reproducibility and portability harness for SQLite workloads, not another SQLite GUI or vector database.

state-transition-capsule.title: State Transition Capsule

state-transition-capsule.user: Application developers debugging a workflow that succeeds once but fails or degrades on subsequent runs because persisted client or server state changed.
state-transition-capsule.distinct: It diagnoses stateful repeatability, rather than becoming another client database, agent framework, or recording service.
state-transition-capsule.workaround: Reset databases and browser storage, capture ad-hoc logs, or attempt to reproduce the same sequence manually.

statement-reconcile-bridge.title: Statement Reconcile Bridge

statement-reconcile-bridge.user: People who keep a private budget spreadsheet or local ledger and need to reconcile a downloaded bank statement without surrendering transactions to an aggregator.
statement-reconcile-bridge.distinct: The product is a portable reconciliation handoff, not a replacement budget app.
statement-reconcile-bridge.workaround: Download CSV/OFX, hand-normalize merchant strings in a spreadsheet, and visually search for duplicates against a ledger.

static-qr-no-signup.distinct: Explicitly anti-dynamic: static payloads, batch and verification in one no-upload page rather than another link-shortener funnel.
static-qr-no-signup.workaround: qrencode CLI/Python; a few indie static generators (e.g. the one recommended in the HN thread); paying for dynamic-QR SaaS.

stock-label-run.title: Stock Label Run

stock-label-run.user: Small shops and makers who receive stock and need a local, repeatable way to turn a purchase list into correct barcode labels and a print receipt.
stock-label-run.distinct: The differentiator is receiving-run traceability, not another online barcode generator.

stock-return-trail.title: Stock Return Trail

stock-return-trail.user: A field-service team or tiny maker with a main store and temporary personal/job locations who needs to return unused stock to the exact origin without reconstructing its history.
stock-return-trail.distinct: It is a return-provenance workflow for temporary stock, not a general inventory system.
stock-return-trail.workaround: Search old movement records or inventory screens item-by-item, then manually transfer each unused item back.

storage-aware-expiry.title: Storage-Aware Expiry

storage-aware-expiry.user: A household tracking pantry/freezer stock who needs date defaults and a practical use-first view that change with storage location.
storage-aware-expiry.distinct: It deliberately avoids full pantry accounting and focuses on the storage/date decision that makes inventory worthwhile.
storage-aware-expiry.workaround: Write dates on containers, use a generic reminder, guess after freezing, or buy a heavy self-hosted stock-management system.

storage-exit-check.title: Storage Exit Check
