storage-exit-check.user: Privacy-conscious individuals moving files from cloud storage to a NAS or local disks who need evidence their replacement is complete and recoverable before cancelling a subscription.
storage-exit-check.distinct: It is a migration confidence and restore-evidence layer, not another sync or backup engine.
storage-exit-check.workaround: Run rsync/Syncthing/restic and compare free-space numbers, or retain cloud subscriptions indefinitely because no one has tested a restore.

stream-access-cues.title: Stream Access Cues

stream-access-cues.user: A blind or keyboard-first independent streamer who needs a reliable local cue surface for stream metadata, scenes, and timing without inaccessible embedded web controls.
stream-access-cues.distinct: It narrows to independent, accessible live control instead of building another streaming platform, chatbot, or visual macro deck.

stream-reader-compass.distinct: The value is continuity and semantic navigation of existing streams, not generating another chat transcript with an LLM.
stream-reader-compass.workaround: Open a separate accessible view, copy fragments to a document, or repeatedly restart navigation from the latest answer.

study-material-import-check.title: Study Material Import Check

study-material-import-check.user: Calm, non-gamified learners who want to bring their own small CSV/text study materials into practice without opaque errors or a content-platform lock-in.
study-material-import-check.distinct: It makes learner-owned materials portable and intelligible instead of becoming another engagement-oriented study destination.
study-material-import-check.workaround: Hand-edit CSVs, search forum posts after an error, or accept a proprietary course/app's import format.

subcontractor-margin-chain.title: Subcontractor Margin Chain

subcontractor-margin-chain.user: Boutique agencies that deliver through freelancers and subcontractors but need to see end-client commitments, subcontractor cost, approval, and invoice status in one job chain. Paying customer: agency owner; wedge: job-level margin protection at $79/month.
subcontractor-margin-chain.distinct: The central object is a commercial delivery chain, not a generic task board or freelancer marketplace.

subscription-renewal-calendar.title: Subscription Renewal Calendar

subscription-renewal-calendar.user: A small business that pays many SaaS and operating subscriptions and needs to see upcoming renewals, rising costs, and a human owner before the next charge.
subscription-renewal-calendar.distinct: It turns recurring spend into a decision calendar, not a generic spend dashboard or an LLM receipt wrapper.
subscription-renewal-calendar.workaround: Use a spreadsheet or personal subscription app, search bank transactions, or rely on calendar reminders with no amount/owner context.

supplier-due-board.user: A sole proprietor or household-sized business that needs a clean view of incoming supplier invoices, due dates, and manual payment status before cash arrives.

sure-shot.distinct: Confidence is the game mechanic across several original micro-challenges, not a thin quiz wrapper or a medical claim.

sync-conflict-lens.title: Sync Conflict Lens

tab-context-capsule.title: Tab Context Capsule

tab-context-capsule.detail: A browser extension that turns selected tabs into a named capsule with title, URL, optional one-line note, ordering, next step, and Markdown/JSON export; it can reopen a capsule locally. Non-goals: cloud sync, browsing-history analytics, or LLM summarization.

tab-sunset-list.title: Tab Sunset List

tab-sunset-list.user: Knowledge workers with chronic browser-tab overload who need a low-friction way to turn stale tabs into deliberate keep, schedule, bookmark, or close decisions.
tab-sunset-list.distinct: It uses time-bounded decisions and exportable outcomes, rather than treating tab hoarding as a storage or workspace-management problem.
tab-sunset-list.workaround: Keep everything open, bulk-close tabs, create tab groups, or move important pages into bookmarks/read-later services.

tableclock.title: Tableclock: a multi-device turn timer / N-player chess clock for board-game tables
tableclock.description: Time every board-game turn on one shared phone.
tableclock.why: Time every player’s turn on one shared phone for board-game groups of two to eight players.
tableclock.detail: Single screen: add 2–8 players, choose mode (count-up, bank, Fischer increment, fixed per-turn), tap to end turn; big colour blocks readable across a table; audio/vibration cues. Optional room code: every phone shows the same clock and any player can end their own turn. Presets encoded in URL (e.g. '5 min interrogation' for social-deduction games). Deliberately NOT: scoring, play logging, BGG integration, accounts.
tableclock.user: Board-game groups and parents with analysis-paralysis players who want a 3–8 player clock that survives OS updates and works on whatever phones are at the table.
tableclock.distinct: Not another chess clock: N-player turn-order semantics, table-readable UI and phone-sync are the product; deliberately stateless and minimal so it doesn't rot like the app-store incumbents.
tableclock.workaround: Phone stopwatch passed around, sand timers, discontinued DGT hardware, or Shared Game Timer (web, feature-rich but heavier).

tabletop-match-ledger.title: Tabletop Match Ledger
tabletop-match-ledger.description: Local-network/offline PWA with a five-second setup, configurable players/rounds/score tracks, lap counters, target scoring, undo history, and a shareable final
tabletop-match-ledger.detail: Local-network/offline PWA with a five-second setup, configurable players/rounds/score tracks, lap counters, target scoring, undo history, and a shareable final receipt. Non-goals: game rules enforcement, a BoardGameGeek clone, or public profiles.
tabletop-match-ledger.user: Tabletop groups playing multi-round games with wraparound boards or cumulative scoring who need a shared, reliable match state between rounds.
tabletop-match-ledger.distinct: It models the state between rounds—laps, targets, and correction history—rather than being a generic numeric score pad.
tabletop-match-ledger.workaround: Use paper, phone notes, a generic counter, or remember score laps separately from the game board.

tabular-file-diff.title: Key-aware diff for CSV/Parquet/Arrow files with git and DVC integration
tabular-file-diff.description: Compare keyed CSV, Parquet, and Arrow snapshots locally from Python, Git, or DVC.
tabular-file-diff.why: Compare keyed CSV, Parquet, and Arrow data snapshots from Python, Git, or DVC.
tabular-file-diff.detail: v1: `tdiff a.parquet b.parquet --key id` prints row counts added/removed/modified, per-column change counts, schema differences and sample changed rows; `--html` writes a self-contained report; a `git difftool` driver plus `.gitattributes` recipe; Python API returning Arrow tables of diffs. Built on DuckDB. Not in v1: database connections, unkeyed fuzzy alignment, patch application, or a web service.
tabular-file-diff.user: Data engineer or analyst who keeps Parquet/CSV snapshots in a repo or DVC and needs added/removed/changed rows and columns between two versions — at millions of rows — as a terminal summary and an HTML report.
tabular-file-diff.distinct: Not a database comparator and not a CSV aligner: file-native, key-aware, scale-oriented and git/DVC-integrated — the combination the asker describes as missing and that the new micro-projects each cover only partially.
tabular-file-diff.workaround: Ad-hoc DuckDB/pandas anti-joins, daff (CSV only, in-memory), csvdiff, converting Parquet to CSV then `diff`, or Datafold Cloud.

takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.title: Drag-in Google Photos Takeout repair (JSON sidecar → EXIF, dedupe, rename)
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.description: Repair Google Photos Takeout dates, locations, exact copies, and filenames on your device.
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.why: Fix dates and locations saved in Google JSON files.
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.detail: Static PWA: select the extracted Takeout folder (or zips), preview matches/unmatched, write EXIF from JSON (JPEG/HEIC/PNG/MP4 date via exiftool-like WASM or piexif), optional rename to date pattern, skip album duplicates by hash, write results into a chosen output folder. Does not upload, does not re-encode, does not organise by faces/AI.
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.user: People leaving Google Photos who unzip Takeout and find photos with wrong dates, stripped GPS, mangled filenames and sidecar .json files; job: get a clean chronological folder with correct metadata without installing Python.
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.distinct: Turns a well-known, script-only fix into a no-install local tool; the existing browser option uploads your photos.
takeout-photo-metadata-fixer.workaround: Run GooglePhotosTakeoutHelper / porte / exiftool scripts from the terminal; metadatafixer.com (paid upload); manual folder merging.

taper-calendar-card.title: StepDown Card
taper-calendar-card.description: Copy a clinician-provided taper into a private card, then check each scheduled day.
taper-calendar-card.why: Put a clinician's dose schedule into a private calendar.
taper-calendar-card.detail: A local offline scheduler where the user enters a clinician’s exact start date, dose steps, and end date; it produces a calendar card, acknowledgement log, and printable summary. Non-goals: calculating taper plans, recommending dosage, drug-interaction checks, or notifications that claim clinical reliability.
taper-calendar-card.user: People following a clinician-provided medication taper who need a clear, private day-by-day regimen they can acknowledge and export.
taper-calendar-card.distinct: It is a faithful schedule-transcription and acknowledgement tool, not an AI health advisor or generalized pill reminder.
taper-calendar-card.workaround: Calendar events, annotated pill bottles, handwritten date tables, or manually altering repeating reminders.

team-agent-skills.title: Team Skills Registry
team-agent-skills.description: Publish reviewed agent skill packages to assigned repositories.
team-agent-skills.why: Publish approved agent skills with versioned rollout and execution records.
team-agent-skills.detail: Hosted registry with Git-backed skill packages, target-agent adapters, approval/ring rollout, and an execution receipt naming the exact skill version. Non-goals: model hosting, prompt marketplace, or automated code execution.
team-agent-skills.user: Engineering leads standardizing several coding agents who need reusable, reviewable instructions and safe rollout across repositories.
team-agent-skills.distinct: The wedge is controlled distribution and provenance of team behavior, not a thin prompt library.
team-agent-skills.workaround: Copy AGENTS.md files between repos, paste prompts into a wiki, or let each developer maintain private instructions.

telemetry-budget-guard.title: Telemetry Budget Guard
telemetry-budget-guard.description: A CLI that consumes a bounded redacted OTLP sample and collector config, estimates cardinality/storage/egress deltas for rule changes, and fails a declared…
telemetry-budget-guard.why: Estimate OpenTelemetry cost and cardinality before merge.
telemetry-budget-guard.detail: A CLI that consumes a bounded redacted OTLP sample and collector config, estimates cardinality/storage/egress deltas for rule changes, and fails a declared budget in CI. Non-goals: trace storage, a hosted dashboard, or vendor recommendation engine.
telemetry-budget-guard.user: Engineers adding OpenTelemetry to a small service who need to prevent cardinality, retention, and log-volume changes from silently creating an unaffordable observability bill.
telemetry-budget-guard.distinct: It prevents costly telemetry before export instead of competing as an observability backend.
telemetry-budget-guard.workaround: Guess sampling rates, wait for a vendor invoice, drop data broadly, or hand-maintain collector filters with no before/after estimate.

telemetry-export-receipts.title: Telemetry Export Receipts
telemetry-export-receipts.description: A self-hostable reverse proxy/sidecar for approved telemetry-export endpoints that enforces query bounds and emits signed JSON/Markdown receipts. Non-goals: sto
telemetry-export-receipts.detail: A self-hostable reverse proxy/sidecar for approved telemetry-export endpoints that enforces query bounds and emits signed JSON/Markdown receipts. Non-goals: storing telemetry, building dashboards, or bypassing product permissions.
telemetry-export-receipts.user: Self-hosted observability administrators who need a defensible record of which user exported which bounded telemetry dataset and under what policy.
telemetry-export-receipts.distinct: It governs and proves data egress, not usage metering or observability collection itself.
telemetry-export-receipts.workaround: Trust application access logs, disable downloads altogether, or save unstructured reverse-proxy logs that cannot describe the exported query.

telemetry-question-book.title: Telemetry Question Book
telemetry-question-book.description: Track recurring telemetry answers from approved readings your support team enters or imports.
telemetry-question-book.why: Track recurring telemetry answers from readings you enter or import.
telemetry-question-book.detail: Static web app plus local config that turns approved read-only query links or CSV exports into named question cards (for example ‘Did feed X arrive?’), with owner, freshness, threshold, and a shareable answer snapshot. Non-goals: ingesting telemetry, query-language generation, alerting, or general BI.
telemetry-question-book.user: An engineering/support pair that repeatedly answers the same customer-impact questions from Grafana, Kibana, and logs but cannot safely hand raw observability tools to non-engineers.
telemetry-question-book.distinct: It constrains and translates recurring questions instead of replacing an observability system or adding generic dashboards.
telemetry-question-book.workaround: Screenshots, manual Slack updates, shallow status pages, or broad dashboard access.

tempo-earcheck.title: Tempo Earcheck
tempo-earcheck.description: Offline PWA with tap-tempo, accented-meter click, named tempo trials, and a compact practice card that records a starting BPM, passed BPM, and next step.…
tempo-earcheck.why: Hear, tap, and keep a defensible practice tempo—offline.
tempo-earcheck.detail: Offline PWA with tap-tempo, accented-meter click, named tempo trials, and a compact practice card that records a starting BPM, passed BPM, and next step. Non-goals: streaming music, score hosting, or AI performance grading.
tempo-earcheck.user: Instrumentalists choosing practice and ensemble tempos who need to hear, tap, and record a defensible target tempo before they encode it in a score or rehearsal plan.
tempo-earcheck.distinct: It links tempo audition to a repeatable rehearsal decision, rather than duplicating a bare metronome.
tempo-earcheck.workaround: Use a separate metronome or tap-tempo app, remember a number informally, then manually re-enter it into notation and practice notes.

terminal-recall.title: Terminal Recall
terminal-recall.description: Save chosen terminal output locally, search it later, and export redacted excerpts.
terminal-recall.why: Search selected terminal sessions locally and export a redacted record when needed.
terminal-recall.detail: CLI installers plus optional TUI that wrap selected commands, retain encrypted local session chunks, provide instant full-text search and redacted export, and expire data by policy. terminal-recall.user: CLI-heavy developers and operators who need to search, preserve, and share a bounded record of terminal/TUI output after it scrolls away or a session exits.
terminal-recall.distinct: It is a privacy-first terminal evidence layer, not an AI coding assistant or a replacement terminal emulator.
terminal-recall.workaround: People increase scrollback, use tmux logs, copy output manually, or rerun commands and hope the same output appears.

theory-playalong-sidecar.title: Theory Playalong Sidecar
theory-playalong-sidecar.description: Play notes over a local backing track and see how each one fits your chosen key.

theory-playalong-sidecar.user: Beginning instrumentalists using a MIDI keyboard who want to see harmony and try ideas while a score or backing track continues playing.
theory-playalong-sidecar.distinct: It turns live, exploratory playing into visible harmonic context rather than grading a lesson or becoming a DAW.
theory-playalong-sidecar.workaround: Pause notation software, record ideas separately, or use a DAW and theory chart side by side.

tide-and-tile.title: Tide & Tile
tide-and-tile.description: Rotate water tiles into one continuous harbor route, then return for a new daily board.

tide-and-tile.distinct: It is a deliberately teachable tactile ritual, not a photo scramble or word-puzzle clone.

time-budget-new-cards.title: Time Budget New Cards
time-budget-new-cards.description: An offline companion that ingests review duration/history or a CSV, estimates the marginal time cost of new cards, and recommends today’s safe new-card cap.…

time-budget-new-cards.detail: An offline companion that ingests review duration/history or a CSV, estimates the marginal time cost of new cards, and recommends today’s safe new-card cap. Non-goals: changing the scheduler or generating cards.

time-budget-new-cards.distinct: The controlled variable is minutes and cognitive load, rather than another queue that assumes every card costs the same.
time-budget-new-cards.workaround: Set one fixed daily-new-card number, manually lower it after a hard day, or stop adding cards entirely.

timeline-json-viewer.description: Browse exported Google Timeline JSON locally, then export selected dates as CSV, GPX, or KML.
timeline-json-viewer.why: Browse and export Google Maps Timeline JSON privately, in your browser.

timezone-slot-proof.title: Timezone Slot Proof

timezone-slot-proof.distinct: It validates scheduling outputs without competing as another booking calendar.

timing-calibrator.distinct: It diagnoses the boundary between musical timing and hardware timing instead of trying to be a music editor.
timing-calibrator.workaround: Hand-place beat markers, guess an audio offset per device, or change engine settings without knowing whether the asset or device is at fault.

touch-canvas-drills.title: Touch Canvas Drills
touch-canvas-drills.description: Practice touch drawing with 20 guided offline drills on phones and tablets.

touch-canvas-drills.detail: Installable PWA with 20 timed line/curve/shape drills, a simple stroke replay, local progress calendar, left-handed layout, and export of a single drill image. Non-goals: social feeds, AI critique, cloud portfolios, or replacement drawing tools.
touch-canvas-drills.user: People learning to draw on an Android tablet or phone who want tiny, repeatable touch exercises that work offline and do not demand a desktop-first editor.
touch-canvas-drills.distinct: It is deliberate-practice scaffolding for touch drawing, not a whiteboard clone or a generated-art app.
touch-canvas-drills.workaround: Use desktop-oriented whiteboards, buy a complex art app before learning basics, or follow passive video tutorials.

tour-route-intent.title: Tour Route Intent
tour-route-intent.description: Static web GPX planner that lets a user lock segments/waypoints and attach terse intent notes (surface, water, ferry, avoid-at-night), then validates whether…

tour-route-intent.detail: Static web GPX planner that lets a user lock segments/waypoints and attach terse intent notes (surface, water, ferry, avoid-at-night), then validates whether an exported route still passes them. Non-goals: turn-by-turn navigation, live traffic, or map-data scraping.
tour-route-intent.user: Self-supported touring cyclists who know the roads or paths they want but need a route file that preserves those deliberate choices across navigation apps.
tour-route-intent.distinct: It protects deliberate route intent across tools rather than replacing a full navigation product.
tour-route-intent.workaround: Add many waypoints, hand-draw a GPX in a desktop planner, and hope the phone app does not silently re-route during navigation.

trace-before-run.title: Trace Before Run
trace-before-run.description: Practice Python tracing by predicting values, paths, and output before each reveal.
trace-before-run.why: Predict a short Python program before seeing its result.
trace-before-run.detail: Static browser game with short editable Python-like snippets, variable-table prediction, branch-path selection, reveal-after-commit, and original micro-puzzles. Non-goals: code execution for arbitrary input, accounts, ranking, or an AI hint bot.
trace-before-run.user: Beginning programming students who can write fragments of Python but struggle to apply logic and debug simple problems.
trace-before-run.distinct: Prediction before execution is the product mechanic; it is neither a generic code playground nor an answer-generating tutor.
trace-before-run.workaround: Watch tutorials, ask an LLM for the answer, repeatedly run code, or copy solutions from practice sites.

trace-context-probe.title: Trace Context Probe

trace-context-probe.detail: A Node CLI/test helper that inserts named async-boundary probes, records expected versus observed trace/span lineage, and emits a static propagation graph with minimal attributes. Non-goals: trace storage, log routing, or vendor replacement.
trace-context-probe.user: Node.js service teams adding OpenTelemetry instrumentation who need to prove where async trace context is lost across queues, callbacks, and framework boundaries.
trace-context-probe.distinct: It verifies trace lineage before observability data is exported, rather than becoming another telemetry backend or LLM log proxy.
trace-context-probe.workaround: Add temporary console logs of trace IDs, rely on vendor SDK behavior, or patch private context-manager internals.

trajectory-test-cases.title: Trajectory Test Cases

trajectory-test-cases.why: Test whether a system follows expected paths.
trajectory-test-cases.detail: An npm library/CLI that records a scrubbed tool event sequence, matches it against a declarative partial-order state machine, injects deterministic retry faults, and produces a visual failure trace. Non-goals: model judging, prompt optimization, or hosted experiments.
trajectory-test-cases.user: Engineers testing tool-calling agents in CI who need to assert critical intermediate actions and retries without unstable LLM judges or brittle whole-transcript snapshots.
trajectory-test-cases.distinct: It verifies operational path invariants, not another judge-driven prompt benchmark.
trajectory-test-cases.workaround: Snapshot full conversations, use an LLM judge, replay against a live service, or write one-off mocked tests per agent.

transcript-redaction-gate.title: Transcript Redaction Gate

transcript-redaction-gate.user: Teams sharing agent or terminal transcripts with models, support, or CI who need deterministic proof that secrets and configured sensitive patterns are removed before any upload.
transcript-redaction-gate.distinct: It puts a deterministic privacy boundary before model context, not an LLM-based cleanup step after exposure.
transcript-redaction-gate.workaround: Trust a model to redact, search text manually, redact after upload, or avoid sharing useful logs entirely.

transcript-study-slicer.title: Transcript Study Slicer

transcript-study-slicer.detail: Browser extension that operates only on an open page's official transcript/captions or pasted text, removes line-wrap noise, lets the learner mark passages, and exports Markdown/CSV with source links. Non-goals: downloading video, bypassing access controls, transcription hosting, or automatic quiz generation.
transcript-study-slicer.user: Text-first learners, including people who struggle to learn from video, who need to turn a legally available transcript into small navigable study passages.
transcript-study-slicer.distinct: It improves reading access and learner-directed segmentation without relying on copyrighted content ingestion or an LLM summary layer.
transcript-study-slicer.workaround: Copy malformed transcripts into notes, watch video at low speed, or manually cut text into cards one document at a time.

tutor-session-trace.title: Tutor Session Trace
tutor-session-trace.description: A small web app with timestamped lesson moments, attempt/outcome tags, code snippet or link attachment, student-visible next task, and PDF/Markdown recap.…

tutor-session-trace.detail: A small web app with timestamped lesson moments, attempt/outcome tags, code snippet or link attachment, student-visible next task, and PDF/Markdown recap. Non-goals: video calling, code execution, proctoring, or a full LMS.
tutor-session-trace.user: One-to-one remote coding tutors who need a lightweight record of student attempts, handoffs, and next practice tasks while teaching through existing video and editor tools.
tutor-session-trace.distinct: It preserves the pedagogical trace around an existing coding session rather than competing with editors or video calls.
tutor-session-trace.workaround: Keep notes in a separate document, send chat follow-ups, record a video, or rely on the editor's transient session state.

unbilled-work-sweep.title: Unbilled Work Sweep

unbilled-work-sweep.detail: Local CSV importer for task/time/invoice exports that matches client/project names, lists unmatched completed work, and produces an invoice-draft checklist. Non-goals: time tracking, invoicing, payroll, or live account integrations in v1.
unbilled-work-sweep.user: A freelancer or tiny agency that records tasks or time in more than one tool and needs a weekly, local view of completed work that has not yet reached an invoice.
unbilled-work-sweep.distinct: It is an attention queue built from existing exports, not another time tracker or invoicing platform.
unbilled-work-sweep.workaround: Open task, time, and invoice screens side-by-side, run ad-hoc reports, or maintain a manual 'invoice next' tag.

video-code-exit-tickets.distinct: The product is a narrow, embeddable verification layer for existing lessons, not another video course or online IDE.

viewport-fact-sheet.workaround: Inspect computed styles manually, use DevTools overlays, scroll and screenshot repeatedly, or guess from accessibility snapshots.

voice-comfort-meter.distinct: It addresses recording comfort and understandable feedback, not audio editing, AI enhancement, or clinical voice analysis.

voice-riff-loop.title: Voice Riff Loop
voice-riff-loop.description: Mobile-first PWA with one-tap record, manual trim/slice, four rhythm pads, fixed-tempo loop, WAV export, and a local project store. Non-goals: AI voice conversi
voice-riff-loop.detail: Mobile-first PWA with one-tap record, manual trim/slice, four rhythm pads, fixed-tempo loop, WAV export, and a local project store. Non-goals: AI voice conversion, cloud upload, stem separation, social publishing, or licensed sounds.
voice-riff-loop.user: New electronic-music makers who want to make a short rhythmic sketch with their own voice before buying instruments, plugins, or learning a DAW.
voice-riff-loop.distinct: It is a deliberately constrained first-loop instrument, not a DAW, sample subscription, or AI music wrapper.
voice-riff-loop.workaround: Record voice notes, import and trim them in a DAW, use copyrighted sample packs, or abandon the first idea because setup is too large.

vram-fieldtest.title: VRAM Field Test
vram-fieldtest.description: Test GPU memory and save a local report before you buy or resell.
vram-fieldtest.why: Test GPU memory and save a clear report before you buy or resell.
vram-fieldtest.detail: Signed CLI installers that enumerate available VRAM, run safe Vulkan/Metal/DirectX pattern suites, make coverage explicit, capture thermals/clocks, and emit JSON plus a one-page report. Non-goals: overclocking, repair advice, or kernel drivers.
vram-fieldtest.user: People buying, reselling, or diagnosing a GPU who need an installable, repeatable memory-integrity test with an understandable report.
vram-fieldtest.distinct: The product is a cross-vendor test protocol and evidence report, not another benchmark chart or overclocking panel.
vram-fieldtest.workaround: Users combine gpu-burn, vendor tools, repair-wiki commands, and stress tests with no standard evidence bundle.

wallpage.title: Wallpage: a browser 'screensaver' gallery of evolving generative scenes for TVs, second monitors and wall displays
wallpage.description: Show calm generative art on an idle TV, wall display, or second monitor.
wallpage.why: Turn a TV, wall display, or second monitor into a calm gallery of moving browser scenes.
wallpage.detail: Full-screen page with ~10 original generative scenes (flow fields, Pong-Wars-like cellular duels, fractal flames, tide/cloud systems), each seeded from date+time so it slowly evolves and is never repeated; unobtrusive clock overlay toggle; auto-rotate every N minutes; dim-at-night schedule; keyboard/remote hotkeys; 'share this seed' link. Deliberately NOT: a shader editor, user uploads, social features, native screensaver packaging (offer instructions for 'webpage as screensaver' tools instead).
wallpage.user: Developers and design-minded people who miss collectible screensavers and want an ambient, evolving, clock-aware generative display for an idle screen or a TV, without installing anything.
wallpage.distinct: Not a shader sandbox or a wallpaper app: it is the 'After Dark' collection idea rebuilt as a stateless web page tuned for idle screens, with time-seeded evolution as the hook.
wallpage.workaround: Leave a CodePen/Shadertoy tab open, ElectricSheep, Apple aerials, YouTube 'ambient' videos with ads.

web-audio-route-map.title: Web Audio Route Map
web-audio-route-map.description: A dependency-free JS library plus demo that renders a live, keyboard-accessible node/route map from an explicit graph declaration and exports SVG. Non-goals…
web-audio-route-map.why: Publish a clear, accessible SVG map beside any small Web Audio signal chain.
web-audio-route-map.detail: A dependency-free JS library plus demo that renders a live, keyboard-accessible node/route map from an explicit graph declaration and exports SVG. Non-goals: audio hosting, an audio engine, or automatic inspection of arbitrary minified code.
web-audio-route-map.user: A browser-audio maker who needs to understand and share a small Web Audio signal chain without manually diagramming it.
web-audio-route-map.distinct: A comprehension aid for open web-audio projects, not a DAW, player, or generative-music wrapper.
web-audio-route-map.workaround: Read source code, draw a diagram, use browser devtools, or keep a DAW patchbay and window layout open.

webhook-quiet-hours.title: Webhook Quiet Hours
webhook-quiet-hours.description: Self-hosted receiver with signed endpoint aliases, event fingerprints, digest/quiet-hour rules, and a single escalation link. Non-goals: webhook delivery/retry…
webhook-quiet-hours.detail: Self-hosted receiver with signed endpoint aliases, event fingerprints, digest/quiet-hour rules, and a single escalation link. Non-goals: webhook delivery/retry service or a general automation platform.
webhook-quiet-hours.user: Small engineering teams receiving internal webhooks who need actionable failures without routing every event into Slack.
webhook-quiet-hours.distinct: It classifies and compresses inbound operational noise rather than acting as another webhook proxy.
webhook-quiet-hours.workaround: Send everything to Slack, suppress alerts manually, or inspect provider logs after a complaint.

webmcp-safety-check.title: WebMCP Safety Check
webmcp-safety-check.description: Check browser-tool declarations before an agent acts.
webmcp-safety-check.why: Inspect WebMCP and MCP safety declarations locally.
webmcp-safety-check.detail: A browser extension plus CLI that reads a WebMCP/MCP manifest or session transcript, classifies tools by read/mutate/external-navigation/credential scope, and fails CI on missing approval or evidence declarations. Non-goals: executing agent tasks, scraping pages, or deciding whether a vendor is trustworthy.
webmcp-safety-check.user: Web teams exposing WebMCP/browser automation tools who need to inspect which operations can mutate state, use a real profile, or access an origin before an agent is allowed to call them.
webmcp-safety-check.distinct: It is a static/sessional safety inspector for browser-agent surfaces, not an MCP server, agent, or generic browser automation product.
webmcp-safety-check.workaround: Read prose tool descriptions, trust server defaults, manually inspect scripts, or disable browser automation entirely.

winter-ride-window.title: Winter Ride Window
winter-ride-window.description: Static web planner where riders enter route exposure and personal thresholds, then receive a cited condition checklist, daylight/battery plan, and 'unknowns to…
winter-ride-window.why: Compare a winter cycling forecast with your own limits and route exposure.
winter-ride-window.detail: Static web planner where riders enter route exposure and personal thresholds, then receive a cited condition checklist, daylight/battery plan, and 'unknowns to check' rather than a safety verdict. Non-goals: live navigation, legal road-condition claims, or emergency advice.
winter-ride-window.user: Commuter cyclists deciding whether a particular route is reasonably rideable in winter without turning vague weather anxiety into an all-or-nothing rule.
winter-ride-window.distinct: It makes a rider's own limits explicit and auditable instead of issuing opaque, potentially unsafe 'ride/no ride' predictions.
winter-ride-window.workaround: Check several weather pages, make a subjective call, or avoid cycling for an entire season after a bad experience.

wordlist-arcade.title: Wordlist Arcade: paste a vocab list, get six playable classroom games, unlimited and account-free
wordlist-arcade.description: Make six classroom vocabulary games from one pasted word-pair list.
wordlist-arcade.why: Make six vocabulary games for class from one word list.
wordlist-arcade.detail: One textarea: 'word — definition' pairs (or word → translation). Instantly generates 6 original game templates from the same list: match-up, whack-the-right-word, anagram, cloze/hangman-style, memory pairs, quiz race. Whole game state encoded in the URL (or a tiny short-link service) so it can be pasted into an LMS. Fullscreen projector mode plus per-student mode. Deliberately NOT: student accounts, grading, printable worksheets v1, image uploads, AI content.
wordlist-arcade.user: Language, ESL and primary teachers who need a quick matching/spelling/quiz game from this week's vocabulary and have used up Wordwall's lifetime free allowance.
wordlist-arcade.distinct: Wordwall's moat is 70 templates + accounts; this is the opposite: stateless, link-shaped, list-first, six good games instead of seventy mediocre ones.
wordlist-arcade.workaround: Overwrite old activities, use other teachers' public ones, Google-site-search Wordwall, or pay ~$5/mo.

workbook-constellation.title: Workbook Constellation
workbook-constellation.description: Map formula paths in XLSX and XLSM workbooks before changing a cell.
workbook-constellation.why: Inspect a workbook across related sheets.
workbook-constellation.detail: A local XLSX parser that extracts formulas, generates a navigable tab-to-tab dependency graph, flags external links/circular references/opaque formulas, and exports a static handoff report. Non-goals: spreadsheet editing, calculation engine, macro execution, or AI analysis.
workbook-constellation.user: People inheriting operational or financial workbooks who need to see cross-tab formula dependencies before changing a cell or handing the workbook to another owner.
workbook-constellation.distinct: It offers structural proof for human review, not an opaque AI spreadsheet analyst or another spreadsheet editor.
workbook-constellation.workaround: Click Excel/Sheets trace precedents one cell at a time, build a manual tab map, buy an enterprise add-in, or ask an AI and manually verify it.

workload-reschedule-receipts.title: Deadline Reality Check
workload-reschedule-receipts.description: Reschedule missed study time and show which deadlines are at risk.
workload-reschedule-receipts.why: Reschedule missed study work and see the risk before deadlines slip.
workload-reschedule-receipts.detail: Local calendar importer where a learner enters task chunks and marks one block missed; it proposes a constrained reschedule and emits an honest risk receipt. Non-goals: LMS scraping, AI-generated coursework, social accountability, or grade forecasting.
workload-reschedule-receipts.user: Students with several overlapping assignments who need a believable reschedule plan after they miss a work block, not another idealized calendar.
workload-reschedule-receipts.distinct: It is an after-the-plan failure-recovery tool, not another task list or AI calendar assistant.
workload-reschedule-receipts.workaround: Manually drag calendar blocks, rewrite to-do lists, hide overdue tasks, or work late without re-estimating downstream consequences.

worklog-appendix.title: Worklog Appendix
worklog-appendix.description: Turn approved worklogs into dated invoice appendices and matching invoice lines.
worklog-appendix.why: Turn approved worklog rows into a client-ready PDF appendix.
worklog-appendix.detail: Local CSV-to-PDF generator that groups approved worklog rows into client-readable milestones, preserves drill-down rows in an appendix, and produces a matching invoice-line summary. Non-goals: timers, project management, invoicing or employee surveillance.
worklog-appendix.user: Freelancers whose clients dispute billed hours because the invoice has a total but no readable account of completed work.
worklog-appendix.distinct: It translates evidence of work into an invoice companion, rather than becoming another time tracker.
worklog-appendix.workaround: Send a raw timesheet CSV, explain hours by email, or manually summarize work in invoice line items.

workspace-history-porter.title: Workspace History Porter
workspace-history-porter.description: A browser extension plus local sidecar that stores an encrypted workspace journal, bookmarks terminal/PR/test URLs, and exports an interoperable handoff file.…
workspace-history-porter.why: Carry encrypted workspace notes and links between browsers.
workspace-history-porter.detail: A browser extension plus local sidecar that stores an encrypted workspace journal, bookmarks terminal/PR/test URLs, and exports an interoperable handoff file. Non-goals: syncing model transcripts, providing a hosted IDE, or accessing code without user action.
workspace-history-porter.user: People moving between browsers and remote development workspaces who need their task/session index and handoff notes to follow the workspace without making chat history a vendor lock-in.
workspace-history-porter.distinct: It ports the small operational index around work, rather than competing as another chat or remote IDE.
workspace-history-porter.workaround: Keep ad-hoc Markdown notes, export chat manually, pin browser tabs, or restart context in each browser.

workspace-reflow.title: Workspace Reflow
workspace-reflow.description: Browser extension: user selects a DOM region, opens a high-contrast reflow pane with font/line-width presets and keyboard sentence navigation, and saves a…
workspace-reflow.why: Enlarge one web-app region in a keyboard-first reading pane while nearby controls.
workspace-reflow.detail: Browser extension: user selects a DOM region, opens a high-contrast reflow pane with font/line-width presets and keyboard sentence navigation, and saves a per-site rule. Non-goals: screen-reader replacement, OCR, or remote page processing.
workspace-reflow.user: Knowledge workers with low vision who need to read dense web-app panes without losing the task context around them.
workspace-reflow.distinct: It is contextual reflow for a chosen live workspace region, not another magnifier or generic reader mode.
workspace-reflow.workaround: Browser zoom, OS magnifier, reader mode, or switching completely to a screen reader.

worktree-secret-broker.title: Worktree Secret Broker
worktree-secret-broker.description: Give worktree processes approved development variables.
worktree-secret-broker.why: Give separate worktrees the secrets they need.
worktree-secret-broker.detail: A local CLI that maps approved variable names to OS-keychain/1Password references, injects them into one named worktree process, and prints an expiry/revocation receipt. Non-goals: cloud vault hosting, secret scanning, or sharing production credentials.
worktree-secret-broker.user: Developers creating disposable coding-agent worktrees who need a tested, least-privilege way to make only required development secrets available.
worktree-secret-broker.distinct: It brokers temporary worktree access rather than replacing an organization's secret manager.
worktree-secret-broker.workaround: Copy .env files manually, use symlinks, paste values into shells, or broadly expose a developer's secret-manager session.
